251.s:
agnir uvāca
bhrāntamudbhrāntamāviddhamāplutaṃ viplutaṃ sṛtaṃ /
sampātaṃ samudīśañca śyenapātamathākulaṃ //
251.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
भ्रान्तमुद्भ्रान्तमाविद्धमाप्लुतं विप्लुतं सृतं /
सम्पातं समुदीशञ्च श्येनपातमथाकुलं //
251.m:
Agni said:
Whirling, whirling high, swirling, leaping forward, leaping apart, gliding, / falling down, rising up, the hawk's pounce, and confusion;

251.s:
uddhūtamavadhūtañca savyaṃ dakṣiṇameva ca /
anālakṣitavisphoṭau karālendramahāsakhau(1) //
251.d:
उद्धूतमवधूतञ्च सव्यं दक्षिणमेव च /
अनालक्षितविस्फोटौ करालेन्द्रमहासखौ(1) //
251.m: shaking upward, shaking downward, leftward, and rightward; / the unseen explosion, the terrible, the great friend of Indra;

251.s:
vikarālanipātau ca vibhīṣaṇabhayānakau /
samagrārdhatṛtīyāṃśapādapādardhavārijāḥ //
251.d:
विकरालनिपातौ च विभीषणभयानकौ /
समग्रार्धतृतीयांशपादपादर्धवारिजाः //
251.m: the dreadful fall, the terrifying, the frightening, / full step, half step, third-of-a-step, footstep, half-footstep, and lotus;

251.s:
pratyālīḍhamathālīḍhaṃ varāhaṃ lulitantathā /
iti dvātriṃśato jñeyāḥ khaḍgacarmavidhau raṇe //
251.d:
प्रत्यालीढमथालीढं वराहं लुलितन्तथा /
इति द्वात्रिंशतो ज्ञेयाः खड्गचर्मविधौ रणे //
251.m: the pratyālīḍha stance, the ālīḍha stance, the boar stance, and the rolling: / these thirty-two [movements] should be known in the use of sword and shield in battle.

251.s:
parāvṛttamapāvṛttaṃ gṛhītaṃ laghusañjñitaṃ /
ūrdhvāt kṣiptamadhaḥ kṣiptaṃ sandhāritavidhāritaṃ //
251.d:
परावृत्तमपावृत्तं गृहीतं लघुसञ्ज्ञितं /
ऊर्ध्वात् क्षिप्तमधः क्षिप्तं सन्धारितविधारितं //
251.m: Turned away, turned back, seized, known as the light, / thrown from above, thrown down, held back, torn apart,

251.s:
śyenapātaṃ gajapātaṃ grāhagrāhyantathaiva ca /
evamekādaśavidhā jñeyāḥ pāśavidhā narāḥ //
251.d:
श्येनपातं गजपातं ग्राहग्राह्यन्तथैव च /
एवमेकादशविधा ज्ञेयाः पाशविधा नराः //
251.m: the hawk's fall, the elephant's fall, and seizing the catchable: / thus eleven kinds of noose operations should be known by men.

251.s:
ṛjvāyataṃ viśālañca tiryagbhrāmitameva ca /
pañcakarma vinirdiṣṭaṃ vyaste pāśe mahātmabhiḥ //
251.d:
ऋज्वायतं विशालञ्च तिर्यग्भ्रामितमेव च /
पञ्चकर्म विनिर्दिष्टं व्यस्ते पाशे महात्मभिः //
251.m: Straight-extended, wide, oblique, and whirling: / five actions are declared by the great-souled for the thrown noose.

251.s:
chedanaṃ bhedanaṃ pāto bhramaṇaṃ śayanaṃ(2) tathā /
vikartanaṃ kartanañca cakrakarmedameva ca //
251.d:
छेदनं भेदनं पातो भ्रमणं शयनं(2) तथा /
विकर्तनं कर्तनञ्च चक्रकर्मेदमेव च //
251.m: Cutting, piercing, felling, whirling, resting, / slicing through, and severing: this is the action of the discus.

251.s:
āsphoṭaḥ kṣeḍanaṃ bhedastrāsāndolitakau tathā /
:n
1 karālendramahāravāviti ka.. , ja.. , ṭa.. ca
2 śamanamiti gha.. , ja.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 404
śūlakarmāṇi jānīhi ṣaṣṭhamāghātasañjñitaṃ //
251.d:
आस्फोटः क्षेडनं भेदस्त्रासान्दोलितकौ तथा /
:न्
1 करालेन्द्रमहारवाविति क.. , ज.. , ट.. च
2 शमनमिति घ.. , ज.. , ट.. च
:प् 404
शूलकर्माणि जानीहि षष्ठमाघातसञ्ज्ञितं //
251.m:
Slapping, throwing, splitting, scaring, swinging,
[Footnotes]
1. 'karālendramahāravau' in manuscripts ka, ja, and ṭa.
2. 'śamanam' in manuscripts gha, ja, and ṭa.
[Page 404]
know these as the actions of the spear; the sixth is called striking.

251.s:
dṛṣṭighātaṃ bhujāghātaṃ pārśvaghātaṃ dvijottama /
ṛjupakṣeṣuṇā pātaṃ tomarasya prakīrtitaṃ //
251.d:
दृष्टिघातं भुजाघातं पार्श्वघातं द्विजोत्तम /
ऋजुपक्षेषुणा पातं तोमरस्य प्रकीर्तितं //
251.m: Striking at the eye, striking at the arm, striking at the flank, O best of brahmins, / and falling straight as a feathered arrow, are declared for the javelin.

251.s:
āhataṃ vipra gomūtraprabhūtaṅkamalāsanaṃ /
tatordhvagātraṃ namitaṃ vāmadakṣiṇameva ca //
251.d:
आहतं विप्र गोमूत्रप्रभूतङ्कमलासनं /
ततोर्ध्वगात्रं नमितं वामदक्षिणमेव च //
251.m: Struck, O brahmin, cow's-urine-like, abundant, the lotus-seat, / then upper body, bent, and left and right.

251.s:
āvṛttañca parāvṛttaṃ pādoddhūtamaplutaṃ /
haṃsamardaṃ vimardañca(1) gadākarma prakīrtitaṃ //
251.d:
आवृत्तञ्च परावृत्तं पादोद्धूतमप्लुतं /
हंसमर्दं विमर्दञ्च(1) गदाकर्म प्रकीर्तितं //
251.m:
Turning, turning back, raising the foot, leaping,
treading like a swan, and crushing are declared to be the actions of the mace.

251.s:
karālamavaghātañca daśopaplutameva ca /
kṣiptahastaṃ sthitaṃ śūnyaṃ parāśostu vinirdiśet //
251.d:
करालमवघातञ्च दशोपप्लुतमेव च /
क्षिप्तहस्तं स्थितं शून्यं पराशोस्तु विनिर्दिशेत् //
251.m:
Dreadful [blow], striking down, leaping tenfold,
thrusting the hand, standing firm, empty [motion], one should designate for the battle-axe.

251.s:
tāḍanaṃ chedanaṃ vipra tathā cūrṇanameva ca /
mudgarasya tu karmāṇi tathā plavanaghātanaṃ //
251.d:
ताडनं छेदनं विप्र तथा चूर्णनमेव च /
मुद्गरस्य तु कर्माणि तथा प्लवनघातनं //
251.m:
Striking, cleaving, O Brahmin, and likewise pulverizing
are the actions of the mallet, as well as leaping strikes.

251.s:
saṃśrāntamatha viśrāntaṃ govisargaṃ sudurdharaṃ /
bhindipālasya karmāṇi laguḍasya ca tānyapi //
251.d:
संश्रान्तमथ विश्रान्तं गोविसर्गं सुदुर्धरं /
भिन्दिपालस्य कर्माणि लगुडस्य च तान्यपि //
251.m:
Wearied, rested, the cow-discharge, the irresistible—
these are the actions of the bhindipāla, and they belong to the club as well.

251.s:
antyaṃ madhyaṃ parāvṛttaṃ nideśāntaṃ dvijottama /
vajrasyetāni karmāṇi paṭṭiśasya ca tānyapi //
251.d:
अन्त्यं मध्यं परावृत्तं निदेशान्तं द्विजोत्तम /
वज्रस्येतानि कर्माणि पट्टिशस्य च तान्यपि //
251.m:
The rear, the middle, turning back, ending with command, O best of Brahmins—
these are the actions of the vajra, and they belong to the paṭṭiśa as well.

251.s:
haraṇaṃ chedanaṃ ghāto baloddhāraṇamāyataṃ /
kṛpāṇakarma nirdiṣṭaṃ pātanaṃ sphoṭanaṃ tathā //
251.d:
हरणं छेदनं घातो बलोद्धारणमायतं /
कृपाणकर्म निर्दिष्टं पातनं स्फोटनं तथा //
251.m:
Seizing, cutting, striking, vigorous pulling, extended [thrust],
felling, and splitting are designated as sword actions.

251.s:
trāsanaṃ rakṣaṇaṃ ghāto baloddharaṇamāyatam /
kṣepaṇīkarma nirdiṣṭaṃ yantrakarmaitadeva tu //
251.d:
त्रासनं रक्षणं घातो बलोद्धरणमायतम् /
क्षेपणीकर्म निर्दिष्टं यन्त्रकर्मैतदेव तु //
251.m:
Frightening, protecting, striking, vigorous pulling, extended [movement]
are designated as the work of the sling; and this indeed is the action of mechanical engines.

251.s:
santyāgamavadaṃśaś ca varāhoddhūtakaṃ tathā /
hastāvahastamālīnamekahastastāvahastake //
251.d:
सन्त्यागमवदंशश् च वराहोद्धूतकं तथा /
हस्तावहस्तमालीनमेकहस्तस्तावहस्तके //
251.m:
Complete abandonment, biting, and tossing like a boar,
hand, back of the hand, clinging, one hand on the back of the hand,

251.s:
dvihastavāhupāśe ca kaṭirecitakodgate /
:n
1 haṃsamārgaṃ vimārgañceti gha.. , ña.. ca / samārgañca vimārgañceti
ṭa..
:p 405
urolalāṭaghāte ca bhujāvidhamanantathā //
251.d:
द्विहस्तवाहुपाशे च कटिरेचितकोद्गते /
:न्
1 हंसमार्गं विमार्गञ्चेति घ.. , ञ.. च / समार्गञ्च विमार्गञ्चेति
ट..
:प् 405
उरोललाटघाते च भुजाविधमनन्तथा //
251.m:
in the two-handed arm-snare, in the whirling and rising of the waist,
[...]
1. Manuscripts gha and ña read "haṃsamārgaṃ vimārgañ ca"; manuscript ṭa reads "samārgañ ca vimārgañ ca". / [Page 405]
in blows to the chest and forehead, and the shaking of the arms,

251.s:
karoddhūtaṃ vimānañca pādāhati vipādikaṃ /
gātrasaṃśleṣaṇaṃ śāntaṃ tathā gātraviparyayaḥ //
251.d:
करोद्धूतं विमानञ्च पादाहति विपादिकं /
गात्रसंश्लेषणं शान्तं तथा गात्रविपर्ययः //
251.m:
tossing with the hand, lack of balance, foot-strikes, moving without steps,
embracing the body, calms, and twisting the body,

251.s:
ūrdhvaprahāraṃ ghātañca gomūtraṃ savyadakṣiṇe /
pārantārakaṃ daṇḍaṃ(1) karavīrandhamākulaṃ //
251.d:
ऊर्ध्वप्रहारं घातञ्च गोमूत्रं सव्यदक्षिणे /
पारन्तारकं दण्डं(1) करवीरन्धमाकुलं //
251.m:
an upward blow, a strike, cow's urine, on the left and the right,
the crossing over, the staff, the oleander, blind, confused,

251.s:
tiryagbandhamapāmārgaṃ(2) bhīmavegaṃ sudarśanaṃ /
siṃhākrāntaṃ gajākrāntaṃ gardabhākrāntameva ca //
251.d:
तिर्यग्बन्धमपामार्गं(2) भीमवेगं सुदर्शनं /
सिंहाक्रान्तं गजाक्रान्तं गर्दभाक्रान्तमेव च //
251.m:
oblique binding, the apāmārga, terrible speed, pleasing to behold,
assault of a lion, assault of an elephant, and assault of a donkey—

251.s:
gadākarmāṇi jānīyānniyuddhasyātha karma ca /
ākarṣaṇaṃ vikarṣaṇañca bāhūnāṃ mūlameva ca //
251.d:
गदाकर्माणि जानीयान्नियुद्धस्याथ कर्म च /
आकर्षणं विकर्षणञ्च बाहूनां मूलमेव च //
251.m:
one should know these as mace actions, and now the action of hand-to-hand combat:
pulling, dragging, striking the base of the arms,

251.s:
grīvāviparivartañca pṛṣṭhabhaṅgaṃ sudāruṇaṃ /
paryāsanaviparyāsau paśumāramajāvikaṃ //
251.d:
ग्रीवाविपरिवर्तञ्च पृष्ठभङ्गं सुदारुणं /
पर्यासनविपर्यासौ पशुमारमजाविकं //
251.m:
twisting the neck, terrible breaking of the back,
overturning and reversal, animal slaughter, slaughtering like sheep and goats,

251.s:
pādaprahāramāsphoṭaṃ kaṭirecitakantathā /
gātrāśleṣaṃ skandhagataṃ mahīvyājanameva ca //
251.d:
पादप्रहारमास्फोटं कटिरेचितकन्तथा /
गात्राश्लेषं स्कन्धगतं महीव्याजनमेव च //
251.m:
kicking with the foot, clapping, whirling of the waist,
embracing the body, going onto the shoulders, and feinting on the ground,

251.s:
urolalāṭaghātañca vispaṣṭakaraṇantathā /
uddhūtamavadhūtañca tiryaṅmārgagataṃ tathā //
251.d:
उरोललाटघातञ्च विस्पष्टकरणन्तथा /
उद्धूतमवधूतञ्च तिर्यङ्मार्गगतं तथा //
251.m:
striking the chest and forehead, making clear maneuvers,
lifting up, shaking down, and moving on oblique paths,

251.s:
gajaskandhamavakṣepamaparāṅmukhameva ca /
devamārgamadhomārgamamārgagamanākulaṃ //
251.d:
गजस्कन्धमवक्षेपमपराङ्मुखमेव च /
देवमार्गमधोमार्गममार्गगमनाकुलं //
251.m:
the elephant-shoulder, throwing down, turning the face away,
the divine path, the lower path, moving about on false paths,

251.s:
yaṣṭighātamavakṣepo vasudhādāraṇantathā /
jānubandhaṃ bhujābandhaṃ sudāruṇaṃ //
251.d:
यष्टिघातमवक्षेपो वसुधादारणन्तथा /
जानुबन्धं भुजाबन्धं सुदारुणं //
251.m:
striking with a stick, throwing down, tearing the earth,
locking the knees, locking the arms, exceedingly fierce,

251.s:
vipṛṣṭhaṃ sodakaṃ śubhraṃ bhujāveṣṭitameva ca /
sannaddhaiḥ saṃyuge bhāvyaṃ saśastraistair gajādibhiḥ //
251.d:
विपृष्ठं सोदकं शुभ्रं भुजावेष्टितमेव च /
सन्नद्धैः संयुगे भाव्यं सशस्त्रैस्तैर् गजादिभिः //
251.m:
back-to-back, watery, brilliant, and encircling with arms.
In battle, those elephants and others must be fully equipped and armed.

251.s:
varāṅkuśadharau cobhau eko grīvāgato 'paraḥ /
:n
1 pārakaṃ tārakaṃ gaṇḍamiti kha.. , gha.. ca
2 tiryagūrdhvamapāmārgamiti gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 406
skandhau dvau ca dhānuṣkau dvau ca khaḍgadharau gaje //
251.d:
वराङ्कुशधरौ चोभौ एको ग्रीवागतो ऽपरः /
:न्
1 पारकं तारकं गण्डमिति ख.. , घ.. च
2 तिर्यगूर्ध्वमपामार्गमिति घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 406
स्कन्धौ द्वौ च धानुष्कौ द्वौ च खड्गधरौ गजे //
251.m:
Two goad-bearers [should be present]: one mounted on the neck, another
[...]
1. Manuscripts kha and gha read "pārakaṃ tārakaṃ gaṇḍam".
2. Manuscripts gha and ña read "tiryagūrdhvam apāmārgam". / [Page 406]
on both shoulders, and two archers and two sword-bearers on the elephant.

251.s:
rathe raṇe gaje caiva turagāṇāṃ trayaṃ bhavet /
dhānuṣkāṇāntrayaṃ proktaṃ rakṣārthe turagasya ca //
251.d:
रथे रणे गजे चैव तुरगाणां त्रयं भवेत् /
धानुष्काणान्त्रयं प्रोक्तं रक्षार्थे तुरगस्य च //
251.m:
In a chariot, in battle, and for an elephant, there should be three horses;
three archers are prescribed for the protection of a horse.

251.s:
dhanvino rakṣaṇārthāya carmiṇantu(1) niyojayet /
svamantraiḥ śastramabhyarcya śāstrantrailokyamohanaṃ //
251.d:
धन्विनो रक्षणार्थाय चर्मिणन्तु(1) नियोजयेत् /
स्वमन्त्रैः शस्त्रमभ्यर्च्य शास्त्रन्त्रैलोक्यमोहनं //
251.m:
To protect an archer, one should assign a shield-bearer.
Having worshipped the weapon with its mantras, [and knowing] the science that deludes the three worlds,

251.s:
yo yuddhe yāti ca jayedarīn sampālayedbhuvaṃ //34//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe dhanurvedo
nāmaikapañcāśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha dvipañcāśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
vyavahārakathanaṃ
251.d:
यो युद्धे याति च जयेदरीन् सम्पालयेद्भुवं //34//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे धनुर्वेदो
नामैकपञ्चाशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ द्विपञ्चाशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
व्यवहारकथनं
251.m:
he who goes to battle conquers his enemies and protects the earth. //34
Thus, in the sacred Agni Purāṇa, the two hundred and fifty-first chapter, entitled “The Science of Archery.”
Now begins the two hundred and fifty-second chapter.
Explanation of Judicial Procedure

252.s:
agnir uvāca
vyavahāraṃ pravakṣyāmi nayānayavivekadaṃ /
catuṣpācca catuḥsthānaś catuḥsādhana ucyate //
252.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
व्यवहारं प्रवक्ष्यामि नयानयविवेकदं /
चतुष्पाच्च चतुःस्थानश् चतुःसाधन उच्यते //
252.m:
Agni said:
I shall proclaim judicial procedure, which grants discrimination between policy and impolicy.
It is spoken of as having four feet, four locations, and four means,

252.s:
caturhitaś caturvyāpī catuṣkārī ca kīrtyate /
aṣṭāṅgo 'ṣṭādaśapadaḥ śataśākhastathaiva ca //
252.d:
चतुर्हितश् चतुर्व्यापी चतुष्कारी च कीर्त्यते /
अष्टाङ्गो ऽष्टादशपदः शतशाखस्तथैव च //
252.m:
as having four benefits, fourfold pervasive, producing four fruits,
having eight limbs, eighteen titles, and likewise a hundred branches,

252.s:
triyonirdvyabhiyogaś ca dvidvāro dvigatis tathā /
dharmaś ca vyavahāraś ca caritraṃ rājaśāsanaṃ //
252.d:
त्रियोनिर्द्व्यभियोगश् च द्विद्वारो द्विगतिस् तथा /
धर्मश् च व्यवहारश् च चरित्रं राजशासनं //
252.m:
having three origins, two plaints, two entrances, and two outcomes:
moral duty, judicial procedure, custom, and royal decree.

252.s:
catuṣpādvyavahārāṇāmuttaraḥ pūrvasādhakaḥ /
tatra satye sthito dharmo vyavahārastu sākṣiṣu //
:n
1 varmiṇantviti gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 407
252.d:
चतुष्पाद्व्यवहाराणामुत्तरः पूर्वसाधकः /
तत्र सत्ये स्थितो धर्मो व्यवहारस्तु साक्षिषु //
:न्
1 वर्मिणन्त्विति घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 407
252.m:
Of the four feet of legal procedures, the latter overrides the former.
Among them, moral duty rests on truth, but judicial procedure rests on witnesses;
[Footnote]
1. "varmiṇaṃ tu" thus in manuscripts gha and ña. / [Page 407]

252.s:
caritraṃ saṅgrahe puṃsāṃ rājājñāyāntu śāsanaṃ /
sāmābhyupāyasādhyatvāccatuḥsādhana ucyate //
252.d:
चरित्रं सङ्ग्रहे पुंसां राजाज्ञायान्तु शासनं /
सामाभ्युपायसाध्यत्वाच्चतुःसाधन उच्यते //
252.m:
custom rests on the usage of men, while the decree rests on the king’s order.
Because it is to be effected by the [four] expedients such as conciliation, it is called fourfold in means.

252.s:
caturṇāmāśramāṇāñca rakṣaṇātsa caturhitaḥ /
kartāraṃ sākṣiṇaś caiva satyānrājānameva ca //
252.d:
चतुर्णामाश्रमाणाञ्च रक्षणात्स चतुर्हितः /
कर्तारं साक्षिणश् चैव सत्यान्राजानमेव च //
252.m:
Because it protects the four stages of life, it has four benefits.
[Because] it reaches each of its feet—the perpetrator, the witness,

252.s:
vyāpnoti pādago yasmāccaturvyāpī tataḥ smṛtaḥ /
dharmasyārthasya yaśaso lokapaṅktestathaiva ca //
252.d:
व्याप्नोति पादगो यस्माच्चतुर्व्यापी ततः स्मृतः /
धर्मस्यार्थस्य यशसो लोकपङ्क्तेस्तथैव च //
252.m:
the judges of truth, and the king—it is considered fourfold pervasive.
Because it brings about the four—

252.s:
caturṇāṅkaraṇādeṣa catuṣkārī prakīrtitaḥ /
rājā sapuruṣaḥ sabhyāḥ śāstraṃ gaṇakalekhakau //
252.d:
चतुर्णाङ्करणादेष चतुष्कारी प्रकीर्तितः /
राजा सपुरुषः सभ्याः शास्त्रं गणकलेखकौ //
252.m:
moral duty, wealth, fame, and social respectability—it is celebrated as producing four fruits.
The king, his officer, the assessors, the legal treatise, the accountant, the scribe,

252.s:
hiraṇyamagnirudakamaṣṭāṅgaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ /
kāmāt krodhācca lobhācca tribhyo yasmāt pravartate //
252.d:
हिरण्यमग्निरुदकमष्टाङ्गः समुदाहृतः /
कामात् क्रोधाच्च लोभाच्च त्रिभ्यो यस्मात् प्रवर्तते //
252.m:
gold, fire, and water—it is declared to have eight limbs.
Because it arises from three—from desire, from anger, and from greed—

252.s:
triyoniḥ kīrtyate tena trayametadvivādakṛt /
dvyabhiyogastu vijñeyaḥ śaṅkātattvābhiyogataḥ //
252.d:
त्रियोनिः कीर्त्यते तेन त्रयमेतद्विवादकृत् /
द्व्यभियोगस्तु विज्ञेयः शङ्कातत्त्वाभियोगतः //
252.m:
it is celebrated as having three origins; this triad generates disputes.
Plaints are to be known as twofold: based on suspicion and based on facts.

252.s:
śaṅkāṣaḍbhistu saṃsargāttattvaṣoḍhādidarśaṇāt /
pakṣadvayābhisambandhāddvidvāraḥ samudāhṛtaḥ //
252.d:
शङ्काषड्भिस्तु संसर्गात्तत्त्वषोढादिदर्शणात् /
पक्षद्वयाभिसम्बन्धाद्द्विद्वारः समुदाहृतः //
252.m:
Suspicion arises from association with six [types], and fact from viewing the sixfold [evidence] and the like.
Because it is connected with two sides, it is declared to have two entrances.

252.s:
pūrvavādastayoḥ pakṣaḥ pratipakṣastvanantaraḥ /
bhūtacchalānusāritvāddvigatiḥ samudāhṛtā //
252.d:
पूर्ववादस्तयोः पक्षः प्रतिपक्षस्त्वनन्तरः /
भूतच्छलानुसारित्वाद्द्विगतिः समुदाहृता //
252.m:
Of these two, the first statement is the claim, and immediately next is the reply.
Because it follows reality or pretext, it is declared to have two outcomes.

252.s:
ṛṇandeyamadeyañca yena yatra yathā ca yat /
dānagrahaṇadharmaś ca ṛṇādānamiti smṛtam //
252.d:
ऋणन्देयमदेयञ्च येन यत्र यथा च यत् /
दानग्रहणधर्मश् च ऋणादानमिति स्मृतम् //
252.m:
A debt to be paid or not to be paid, by whom, where, how, and what,
along with the law of giving and taking—this is known as non-repayment of debt.

252.s:
svadravyaṃ yatra viśrambhānnikṣipatyaviśaṅkitaḥ /
nikṣepannāma tat proktaṃ vyavahārapadambudhaiḥ //
252.d:
स्वद्रव्यं यत्र विश्रम्भान्निक्षिपत्यविशङ्कितः /
निक्षेपन्नाम तत् प्रोक्तं व्यवहारपदम्बुधैः //
252.m:
Where one unhesitatingly deposits one’s property out of trust,
that is called “deposit” by the wise, a title of judicial procedure.

252.s:
vaṇikprabhṛtayo yatra karma sambhūya kurvate /
tatsambhūyasamuptyānaṃ vyavahārapadaṃ viduḥ //
252.d:
वणिक्प्रभृतयो यत्र कर्म सम्भूय कुर्वते /
तत्सम्भूयसमुप्त्यानं व्यवहारपदं विदुः //
252.m:
Where merchants and others conduct business in partnership,
that they know as “undertaking of joint venture,” a title of judicial procedure.

252.s:
dattvā dravyañca samyagyaḥ punarādātumicchati /
:p 408
dattvāpradānikaṃ nāma tadvivādapadaṃ smṛtaṃ //
252.d:
दत्त्वा द्रव्यञ्च सम्यग्यः पुनरादातुमिच्छति /
:प् 408
दत्त्वाप्रदानिकं नाम तद्विवादपदं स्मृतं //
252.m:
When someone, having given away property properly, wishes to take it back,
[Page 408]
that is called “resumption of gift,” considered a title of dispute.

252.s:
abhyupetya ca śuśrūṣāṃ yastāṃ na pratipadyate /
aśuśrūṣābhyupetyaitadvivādapadamucyate //
252.d:
अभ्युपेत्य च शुश्रूषां यस्तां न प्रतिपद्यते /
अशुश्रूषाभ्युपेत्यैतद्विवादपदमुच्यते //
252.m:
And whoever, having promised service, does not undertake it,
this is called “breach of contract of service,” a title of dispute.

252.s:
bhṛtyānāṃ vetanasyoktādānādānavidhikriyā /
vetanasyānapākarma tadvivādapadaṃ smṛtam //
252.d:
भृत्यानां वेतनस्योक्तादानादानविधिक्रिया /
वेतनस्यानपाकर्म तद्विवादपदं स्मृतम् //
252.m:
The rules and actions regarding the payment and non-payment of servants’ wages:
that is considered the title of dispute named “non-payment of wages.”

252.s:
nikṣiptaṃ vā paradravyaṃ naṣṭaṃ labdhvā prahṛtya vā /
kikrīyate parokṣaṃ yat sa jñeyo 'svāmivikrayaḥ //
252.d:
निक्षिप्तं वा परद्रव्यं नष्टं लब्ध्वा प्रहृत्य वा /
किक्रीयते परोक्षं यत् स ज्ञेयो ऽस्वामिविक्रयः //
252.m:
When another's property, deposited, found after being lost, or stolen,
is sold in secret, that is to be known as “sale without ownership.”

252.s:
vikrīya paṇyaṃ mūlyena kretre yacca na dīyate /
vikrīyāsampradānantadvivādapadamucyate //
252.d:
विक्रीय पण्यं मूल्येन क्रेत्रे यच्च न दीयते /
विक्रीयासम्प्रदानन्तद्विवादपदमुच्यते //
252.m:
When merchandise, having been sold for a price, is not handed over to the buyer,
that is called “non-delivery of sold goods,” a title of dispute.

252.s:
krītvā mūlyena yatpaṇyaṃ kretā na bahu manyate /
krītvā mūlyena yat paṇyaṃ duṣkrītaṃ manyate krayī //
252.d:
क्रीत्वा मूल्येन यत्पण्यं क्रेता न बहु मन्यते /
क्रीत्वा मूल्येन यत् पण्यं दुष्क्रीतं मन्यते क्रयी //
252.m:
When a buyer, having purchased merchandise for a price, does not think highly of it,
[or when] the purchaser, having bought goods for a price, considers it a bad purchase—

252.s:
pāṣaṇḍanaigamādīnāṃ sthitiḥ samaya ucyate /
samayasyānapākarma tadvivādapadaṃ smṛtaṃ //
252.d:
पाषण्डनैगमादीनां स्थितिः समय उच्यते /
समयस्यानपाकर्म तद्विवादपदं स्मृतं //
252.m: The established custom of heretics, merchants, and others is called agreement; / non-observance of agreement is remembered as that title of dispute.

252.s:
setukedāramaryādāvikṛṣṭākṛṣṭaniś cayāḥ /
kṣetrādhikāre yatra syurvivādaḥ kṣetrajastu saḥ //
252.d:
सेतुकेदारमर्यादाविकृष्टाकृष्टनिश् चयाः /
क्षेत्राधिकारे यत्र स्युर्विवादः क्षेत्रजस्तु सः //
252.m: Determinations regarding embankments, field boundaries, and tilled and untilled [lands], / wherever they occur regarding title to a field, that dispute arises from land.

252.s:
vaivāhiko vidhiḥ strīnāṃ yatra puṃsāñca kīrtyate /
strīpuṃsayogasaṃjñantu tadvivādapadaṃ smṛtam //
252.d:
वैवाहिको विधिः स्त्रीनां यत्र पुंसाञ्च कीर्त्यते /
स्त्रीपुंसयोगसंज्ञन्तु तद्विवादपदं स्मृतम् //
252.m: Where the marital rule of women and men is declared, / that title of dispute is remembered as the union of woman and man.

252.s:
vibhāgorthasya paitrasya putrair yastu prakalpyate /
dāyamāgamiti proktaṃ tadvivādapadaṃ budhaiḥ //
252.d:
विभागोर्थस्य पैत्रस्य पुत्रैर् यस्तु प्रकल्प्यते /
दायमागमिति प्रोक्तं तद्विवादपदं बुधैः //
252.m: The division of paternal property that is arranged by sons, / is declared by the wise as inheritance and acquisition, that title of dispute.

252.s:
sahasā kriyate karma yat kiñcit baladarpitaiḥ /
tat sāhasamiti proktaṃ vivādapadamucyate //
252.d:
सहसा क्रियते कर्म यत् किञ्चित् बलदर्पितैः /
तत् साहसमिति प्रोक्तं विवादपदमुच्यते //
252.m: Whatever deed is done rashly by those arrogant with power, / that is declared violence, a title of dispute.

252.s:
deśajātikulādīnāmākrośatyaṅgasaṃyutam /
yadvacaḥ pratikūlārthaṃ vākpāruṣyaṃ taducyate //
:p 409
252.d:
देशजातिकुलादीनामाक्रोशत्यङ्गसंयुतम् /
यद्वचः प्रतिकूलार्थं वाक्पारुष्यं तदुच्यते //
:प् 409
252.m:
Speech that reviles country, caste, lineage, and so forth, or concerns physical defects, / having an offensive meaning, that is called verbal assault.
[Page 409]

252.s:
paragātreṣvabhidrehī hastapādāyudhādibhiḥ /
agnyādibhiś copaghātair(?) daṇḍapāruṣyamucyate //
252.d:
परगात्रेष्वभिद्रेही हस्तपादायुधादिभिः /
अग्न्यादिभिश् चोपघातैर्(?) दण्डपारुष्यमुच्यते //
252.m: Hostility toward the limbs of another by means of hands, feet, weapons, and the like, / and by injuries through fire and so forth, is called physical assault.

252.s:
akṣavajjaśalākādyair daivataṃ dyūtamucyate /
pañcakriḍāvayobhiś ca prāṇidyutasamāhvayaḥ //
252.d:
अक्षवज्जशलाकाद्यैर् दैवतं द्यूतमुच्यते /
पञ्चक्रिडावयोभिश् च प्राणिद्युतसमाह्वयः //
252.m: With dice, leather straps, sticks, and so forth, gaming without animate beings is called [gambling]; / and with betting on five types of play and birds, it is designated betting on live animals.

252.s:
prakīrṇakaḥ punarjñeyo vyavahāro nirāśrayaḥ /
rājñāmājñāpratoghātastatkarmākaraṇantathā //
252.d:
प्रकीर्णकः पुनर्ज्ञेयो व्यवहारो निराश्रयः /
राज्ञामाज्ञाप्रतोघातस्तत्कर्माकरणन्तथा //
252.m: Miscellaneous legal proceedings are moreover to be known as having no single ground; / [such as] defying the command of kings, as well as failing to perform their work.

252.s:
vyavahāro 'ṣṭādaśapadasteṣāṃ bhedo 'tha vai śatam /
kriyābhedānmanuṣyānāṃ śataśākho nigadyate //
252.d:
व्यवहारो ऽष्टादशपदस्तेषां भेदो ऽथ वै शतम् /
क्रियाभेदान्मनुष्यानां शतशाखो निगद्यते //
252.m: Judicial procedure has eighteen titles, and their subdivisions number one hundred; / owing to the variety of human transactions, it is said to have a hundred branches.

252.s:
vyavahārānnṛpaḥ paśyej jñāniviprair akopanaḥ /
śatrumitrasamāḥ sabhyā alobhāḥ śrutivedinaḥ //
252.d:
व्यवहारान्नृपः पश्येज् ज्ञानिविप्रैर् अकोपनः /
शत्रुमित्रसमाः सभ्या अलोभाः श्रुतिवेदिनः //
252.m: The king, free from anger, should look into legal proceedings alongside learned Brāhmaṇas; / the jurors should treat enemy and friend alike, be free from greed, and know the Vedas.

252.s:
apaśyatā(1) kāryavaśāt sabhyair vipraṃ niyojayet /
rāgāllobhādbhayādvāpi smṛtyapetādikāriṇaḥ //
252.d:
अपश्यता(1) कार्यवशात् सभ्यैर् विप्रं नियोजयेत् /
रागाल्लोभाद्भयाद्वापि स्मृत्यपेतादिकारिणः //
252.m: If unable to examine due to urgent affairs, he should appoint a Brāhmaṇa alongside the jurors; / but those acting contrary to the Smṛtis out of passion, greed, or fear,

252.s:
sabhyāḥ pṛthak pṛthag daṇḍyā vivādādvdiguṇo damaḥ /
smṛtyācāraeṣvyapetena mārgeṇa dharṣitaḥ paraiḥ //
252.d:
सभ्याः पृथक् पृथग् दण्ड्या विवादाद्व्दिगुणो दमः /
स्मृत्याचारएष्व्यपेतेन मार्गेण धर्षितः परैः //
252.m: such jurors are each to be punished individually with twice the fine of the dispute. / One who is injured by others in a manner contrary to Smṛti and custom,

252.s:
āvedayati yadrājñe vyavahārapadaṃ hi tat /
pratyarthino 'grato lekhyaṃ yathā veditamarthinā //
252.d:
आवेदयति यद्राज्ञे व्यवहारपदं हि तत् /
प्रत्यर्थिनो ऽग्रतो लेख्यं यथा वेदितमर्थिना //
252.m: and informs the king—that indeed is a title of judicial procedure. / It should be written down before the defendant just as stated by the plaintiff,

252.s:
samāmāsatadardhāharnāmajātyādicihnitam /
śrutārthasyottaraṃ lekhyaṃ pūrvāvedakasannidhau //
252.d:
समामासतदर्धाहर्नामजात्यादिचिह्नितम् /
श्रुतार्थस्योत्तरं लेख्यं पूर्वावेदकसन्निधौ //
252.m: marked with year, month, fortnight, day, name, caste, and so forth. / The answer to what was heard should be written down in the presence of the original complainant.

252.s:
tapto 'rthī lekhayetsadyaḥ pratijñātārthasādhanam /
tatsiddhau siddhamāpnoti viparītamato 'nyathā //
252.d:
तप्तो ऽर्थी लेखयेत्सद्यः प्रतिज्ञातार्थसाधनम् /
तत्सिद्धौ सिद्धमाप्नोति विपरीतमतो ऽन्यथा //
252.m: The eager plaintiff should immediately record the means of proving the matter asserted; / if that is proven, he obtains success; otherwise, the reverse [occurs].

252.s:
catuṣpādvyavahāroyaṃ vivādeṣūpadarśitaḥ /
:n
1 apaśyatā ity ayaṃ pāṭho na sādhuḥ
:p 410
abhiyogamanistīrya nainaṃ pratyabhiyojayet //
252.d:
चतुष्पाद्व्यवहारोयं विवादेषूपदर्शितः /
:न्
1 अपश्यता इत्य् अयं पाठो न साधुः
:प् 410
अभियोगमनिस्तीर्य नैनं प्रत्यभियोजयेत् //
252.m:
This judicial procedure is shown as having four feet in legal disputes:
[Footnote]
1 The reading apaśyatā is not correct.
[Page 410]
Without answering the complaint, he must not file a counter-suit against him;

252.s:
abhiyuktañca nānyena tyaktaṃ viprakṛtiṃ nayet /
kuryāt pratyabhiyogantu kalahe sāhaseṣu ca //
252.d:
अभियुक्तञ्च नान्येन त्यक्तं विप्रकृतिं नयेत् /
कुर्यात् प्रत्यभियोगन्तु कलहे साहसेषु च //
252.m: and he should not alter an accused person who has been released by another; / but he may make a counter-accusation in cases of affray and violent crimes.

252.s:
ubhayoḥ pratibhūrgrāhyaḥ samarthaḥ kāmyanirṇaye /
nihnave bhāvito dadyāddhanaṃ rājñe tu tatsamam //
252.d:
उभयोः प्रतिभूर्ग्राह्यः समर्थः काम्यनिर्णये /
निह्नवे भावितो दद्याद्धनं राज्ञे तु तत्समम् //
252.m: A surety competent in determining the desired result should be taken from both sides; / if a denial is proven [false], he should pay that sum, and the same amount to the king.

252.s:
mithyābhiyogād dviguṇamabhiyogāddhanaṃ haret /
sāhasasteyapāruṣyeṣvabhiśāpātyaye striyāḥ //
252.d:
मिथ्याभियोगाद् द्विगुणमभियोगाद्धनं हरेत् /
साहसस्तेयपारुष्येष्वभिशापात्यये स्त्रियाः //
252.m: Because of a false complaint, one should take twice the sum from the complaint. / In violent crimes, theft, assault, capital accusations, and regarding women,

252.s:
vicārayetsadyaḥ eva kālo 'nyatrecchayā smṛtaḥ /
deśāddeśāntaraṃ yāti sṛkkaṇī parileḍhi ca //
252.d:
विचारयेत्सद्यः एव कालो ऽन्यत्रेच्छया स्मृतः /
देशाद्देशान्तरं याति सृक्कणी परिलेढि च //
252.m: he should deliberate immediately; elsewhere the time is remembered according to desire. / He who shifts from place to place and licks the corners of his mouth,

252.s:
lalāṭaṃ svidyate cāsya mukhavaivarṇyameva ca /
svabhāvādvikṛtaṃ gacchenmanovākkāyakarmabhiḥ //
252.d:
ललाटं स्विद्यते चास्य मुखवैवर्ण्यमेव च /
स्वभावाद्विकृतं गच्छेन्मनोवाक्कायकर्मभिः //
252.m: whose forehead sweats, and whose face changes color; / he who alters from his natural state in mind, speech, body, and actions,

252.s:
abhiyoge 'tha vā sākṣye vāgduṣṭaḥ parikīrtitaḥ /
sandigdhārthaṃ svatantro yaḥ sādhayedyaś ca niṣpatet //
252.d:
अभियोगे ऽथ वा साक्ष्ये वाग्दुष्टः परिकीर्तितः /
सन्दिग्धार्थं स्वतन्त्रो यः साधयेद्यश् च निष्पतेत् //
252.m: in accusation or in testimony, is proclaimed as corrupt in speech. / He who independently establishes a doubtful claim, or who flees,

252.s:
na cāhūto vadet kiñciddhanī daṇḍyaś ca sa smṛtaḥ /
sākṣiṣūbhayataḥ satsu sākṣiṇaḥ pūrvavādinaḥ //
252.d:
न चाहूतो वदेत् किञ्चिद्धनी दण्ड्यश् च स स्मृतः /
साक्षिषूभयतः सत्सु साक्षिणः पूर्ववादिनः //
252.m: and who, when summoned, says nothing—he is considered liable to punishment. / When there are witnesses on both sides, the witnesses of the plaintiff [are heard];

252.s:
pūrvapakṣe 'dharībhūte bhavantyuttaravādinaḥ /
sagaṇaścedvivādaḥ syāttatra hīnantu dāpayet //
252.d:
पूर्वपक्षे ऽधरीभूते भवन्त्युत्तरवादिनः /
सगणश्चेद्विवादः स्यात्तत्र हीनन्तु दापयेत् //
252.m: if the plaintiff's claim is refuted, those of the defendant become [heard]. / If the dispute involves a corporate body, he should make the defeated party pay there.

252.s:
dattaṃ paṇaṃ vasañcaiva dhanino dhanameva ca /
chalannirasya dūtena vyavahārānnayennṛpaḥ //
252.d:
दत्तं पणं वसञ्चैव धनिनो धनमेव च /
छलन्निरस्य दूतेन व्यवहारान्नयेन्नृपः //
252.m: Setting aside deceit by means of an envoy, the king should conduct legal proceedings / regarding the stake, the residence, and the wealth of the creditor.

252.s:
bhūtamapyarthamapyastaṃ hīyate vyavahārataḥ /
nihnute nikhilānekamekadeśavibhāvitam //
252.d:
भूतमप्यर्थमप्यस्तं हीयते व्यवहारतः /
निह्नुते निखिलानेकमेकदेशविभावितम् //
252.m: Even a real claim that is abandoned is lost through judicial procedure. / If one denies the entirety, but one part is proven,

252.s:
dāpyaḥ sarvānnṛpeṇārthānna grāhyastvaniveditaḥ /
smṛtyorvirodhe nyāyastu vallavān vyavahārataḥ //
:p 411
252.d:
दाप्यः सर्वान्नृपेणार्थान्न ग्राह्यस्त्वनिवेदितः /
स्मृत्योर्विरोधे न्यायस्तु वल्लवान् व्यवहारतः //
:प् 411
252.m:
the king must make him pay all claims, but a claim not declared should not be accepted. / When two Smṛtis conflict, reasoned equity is stronger according to legal practice.
[Page 411]

252.s:
arthaśāstrāddhi balavaddharmaśāstramiti sthitiḥ(1) /
pramāṇaṃ likhitaṃ bhuktiḥ sākṣiṇaśceti kirtitam //
252.d:
अर्थशास्त्राद्धि बलवद्धर्मशास्त्रमिति स्थितिः(1) /
प्रमाणं लिखितं भुक्तिः साक्षिणश्चेति किर्तितम् //
252.m: For Dharmaśāstra is stronger than Arthaśāstra; such is the rule. / Means of proof are declared to be documents, possession, and witnesses.

252.s:
eṣāmanyatamābhāve divyānyatamamucyate /
sarveṣveva vivādeṣu balavatyuttarā kriyā //
252.d:
एषामन्यतमाभावे दिव्यान्यतममुच्यते /
सर्वेष्वेव विवादेषु बलवत्युत्तरा क्रिया //
252.m: In the absence of any of these, one of the divine ordeals is prescribed. / In all disputes, the later transaction is stronger;

252.s:
ādhau pratigrahe krīte pūrvā tu balavattarā /
paśyato bruvato bhūmerhānirviṃśativārṣikī //
252.d:
आधौ प्रतिग्रहे क्रीते पूर्वा तु बलवत्तरा /
पश्यतो ब्रुवतो भूमेर्हानिर्विंशतिवार्षिकी //
252.m: but in pledges, gifts, and purchases, the earlier is stronger. / To one who sees and does not speak, the loss of land takes twenty years,

252.s:
pareṇa bhujyamānā yā dhanasya daśavārṣikī /
ādhisaumopaniḥkṣepajaḍabāladhanair vinā //
252.d:
परेण भुज्यमाना या धनस्य दशवार्षिकी /
आधिसौमोपनिःक्षेपजडबालधनैर् विना //
252.m: when it is enjoyed by another, but ten years for movable property; / except for pledges, boundary disputes, open deposits, and property of idiots and minors,

252.s:
tathopanidhirājastrīśrotriyāṇāṃ dhanair api /
ādhyādīnāṃ vihartāraṃ dhanine dāpayeddhanaṃ //
252.d:
तथोपनिधिराजस्त्रीश्रोत्रियाणां धनैर् अपि /
आध्यादीनां विहर्तारं धनिने दापयेद्धनं //
252.m: and likewise sealed deposits, and property of the king, women, and learned Vedic scholars. / The king should cause the appropriator of pledges and the like to pay the property to the creditor,

252.s:
daṇḍyaṃ ca tatsamaṃ rājñe śaktyapekṣyamathāpi vā /
āgamopyadhiko bhuktiṃ vinā pūrvakramāgatāṃ //
252.d:
दण्ड्यं च तत्समं राज्ञे शक्त्यपेक्ष्यमथापि वा /
आगमोप्यधिको भुक्तिं विना पूर्वक्रमागतां //
252.m: and a fine equal to it to the king, or according to his capacity. / Even a title of acquisition is superior, except without possession descended through previous succession.

252.s:
āgamopi balannaiva bhuktiḥ stokāpi yatra na /
āgamena viśuddhena bhogo yāti pramāṇatām //
252.d:
आगमोपि बलन्नैव भुक्तिः स्तोकापि यत्र न /
आगमेन विशुद्धेन भोगो याति प्रमाणताम् //
252.m: Even a title of acquisition has no force where there is not even a slight possession; / enjoyment attains validity through a purified title.

252.s:
aviśuddhāgamo bhogaḥ prāmāṇyaṃ nādhigacchati /
āgamastu kṛto yena so 'bhiyuktastamuddharet //
252.d:
अविशुद्धागमो भोगः प्रामाण्यं नाधिगच्छति /
आगमस्तु कृतो येन सो ऽभियुक्तस्तमुद्धरेत् //
252.m: Enjoyment whose title is unpurified does not attain validity. / He by whom a title was made, when accused, must vindicate it;

252.s:
na tatsutastatsuto vā bhuktistatra garīyasī /
yobhiyuktaḥ paretaḥ syāt tasya ṛkthāttamuddharet //
252.d:
न तत्सुतस्तत्सुतो वा भुक्तिस्तत्र गरीयसी /
योभियुक्तः परेतः स्यात् तस्य ऋक्थात्तमुद्धरेत् //
252.m: not his son, nor his grandson; there possession is weightier. / If he who was accused should die, [his heir] should clear it from his estate;

252.s:
na tatra kāraṇaṃ bhuktirāgamena vinākṛtā /
balopādhivinirvṛttān vyavahārānnivartayet //
252.d:
न तत्र कारणं भुक्तिरागमेन विनाकृता /
बलोपाधिविनिर्वृत्तान् व्यवहारान्निवर्तयेत् //
252.m: possession separated from title is not proof there. / He should annul legal transactions brought about by force or fraudulent conditions,

252.s:
strīnaktamantarāgāravahiḥśatrukṛtas tathā /
mattonmattārtavyasanibālabhītaprayojitaḥ //
:n
1 smṛtiriti gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 412
252.d:
स्त्रीनक्तमन्तरागारवहिःशत्रुकृतस् तथा /
मत्तोन्मत्तार्तव्यसनिबालभीतप्रयोजितः //
:न्
1 स्मृतिरिति घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 412
252.m:
and also those executed by women, at night, inside a house, outside, by enemies, / or undertaken by the intoxicated, insane, distressed, addicted, minors, or frightened.
[Footnote]
1 For sthitiḥ, manuscripts gha and ña read smṛtiḥ.
[Page 412]

252.s:
asambaddhakṛtaś caiva vyavahāro na siddhyati /
pranaṣṭādhiśataṃ deyaṃ nṛpeṇa dhanine dhanaṃ //
252.d:
असम्बद्धकृतश् चैव व्यवहारो न सिद्ध्यति /
प्रनष्टाधिशतं देयं नृपेण धनिने धनं //
252.m: And a legal transaction made by an unauthorized person does not succeed. / The king should return lost property to the owner after showing it for a hundred days;

252.s:
vibhāvayennacelliṅgaistatsamaṃ dātumarhati /
deyañcaurahṛtaṃ dravyaṃ rājñā janapadāya tu //
252.d:
विभावयेन्नचेल्लिङ्गैस्तत्समं दातुमर्हति /
देयञ्चौरहृतं द्रव्यं राज्ञा जनपदाय तु //
252.m: if he does not prove it by marks, he should pay an amount equal to it. / But stolen goods should be returned by the king to the district.

252.s:
aśītibhāgo vṛddhiḥ syānmāsi māsi sabandhake /
varṇakramācchataṃ dvitricatuṣpañcakamanyathā //
252.d:
अशीतिभागो वृद्धिः स्यान्मासि मासि सबन्धके /
वर्णक्रमाच्छतं द्वित्रिचतुष्पञ्चकमन्यथा //
252.m: The interest with a pledge should be an eightieth part month by month; / otherwise, according to caste order, two, three, four, or five percent.

252.s:
saptatistu paśustrīṇāṃ rasasyāṣṭaguṇā parā /
vastradhānyahiraṇyānāṃ catustridviguṇā tathā //
252.d:
सप्ततिस्तु पशुस्त्रीणां रसस्याष्टगुणा परा /
वस्त्रधान्यहिरण्यानां चतुस्त्रिद्विगुणा तथा //
252.m: The increase for livestock and females is an offspring; for liquids it is eightfold at most; / and for textiles, grain, and gold, it is fourfold, threefold, and twofold respectively.

252.s:
grāmāntarāttu daśakaṃ sāmudrādapi viṃśatiṃ /
dadyurvā svakṛtāṃ vṛddhiṃ sarve sarvāsu jātiṣu //
252.d:
ग्रामान्तरात्तु दशकं सामुद्रादपि विंशतिं /
दद्युर्वा स्वकृतां वृद्धिं सर्वे सर्वासु जातिषु //
252.m: From another village, it is ten percent; and from sea-voyages, twenty; / or all castes may pay the interest agreed upon by themselves in all transactions.

252.s:
prapanna sādhayannarthaṃ na vācyā nṛpatirbhavet /
sādhyamāno nṛpaṃ gaccheddaṇḍyo dāpyaś ca taddhanaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe vyavahāro nāma
dvipañcāśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha tripañcāśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
vyavahārakathanaṃ
252.d:
प्रपन्न साधयन्नर्थं न वाच्या नृपतिर्भवेत् /
साध्यमानो नृपं गच्छेद्दण्ड्यो दाप्यश् च तद्धनं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे व्यवहारो नाम
द्विपञ्चाशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ त्रिपञ्चाशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
व्यवहारकथनं
252.m:
One who recovers an agreed debt without coercion is not to be reprimanded by the king; / if he who is being pursued goes to the king, he is to be fined and made to pay that wealth.
Thus ends the two hundred and fifty-second chapter, titled Judicial Procedure, in the Great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the two hundred and fifty-third chapter:
The exposition of judicial procedure.

253.s:
agnir uvāca
gṛhītārthaḥ kramāddāpyo dhanināmadhamarṇikaḥ /
datvā tu brāhmaṇāyādau nṛpatestadanantaram //
:p 413
253.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
गृहीतार्थः क्रमाद्दाप्यो धनिनामधमर्णिकः /
दत्वा तु ब्राह्मणायादौ नृपतेस्तदनन्तरम् //
:प् 413
253.m:
Agni said: / A debtor who has received wealth must be made to pay back his creditors in order, / having paid first to a brāhmaṇa, and after him to the king.
[page 413]

253.s:
rājñādhamarṇiko dāpyaḥ sādhitāddaśakaṃ smṛtam /
pañcakantu śataṃ dāpyaḥ prāptārtho hy uttamarṇakaḥ //
253.d:
राज्ञाधमर्णिको दाप्यः साधिताद्दशकं स्मृतम् /
पञ्चकन्तु शतं दाप्यः प्राप्तार्थो ह्य् उत्तमर्णकः //
253.m: The debtor must be made by the king to pay a tenth part of what has been recovered; / and a creditor who has received his money must be made to pay five percent.

253.s:
hīnajātiṃ parikṣīṇamṛṇārthaṃ karma kārayet /
brāhmaṇastu parikṣīṇaḥ śanair dāpyo yathodayam //
253.d:
हीनजातिं परिक्षीणमृणार्थं कर्म कारयेत् /
ब्राह्मणस्तु परिक्षीणः शनैर् दाप्यो यथोदयम् //
253.m: One of lower caste who is impoverished should be made to perform labour for the debt; / but an impoverished brāhmaṇa must be made to pay gradually, according to his income.

253.s:
dīyamānaṃ na gṛhṇāti prayuktaṃ yaḥ svakandhanam /
madhyasthasthāpitaṃ tatsyādvardhate na tataḥ paraṃ //
253.d:
दीयमानं न गृह्णाति प्रयुक्तं यः स्वकन्धनम् /
मध्यस्थस्थापितं तत्स्याद्वर्धते न ततः परं //
253.m: If a creditor does not accept his own money which has been lent when it is offered, / it should be deposited with an arbitrator; from that time on, it does not accrue interest.

253.s:
ṛkthagrāha ṛṇaṃ dāpyo yoṣidgrāhastathaiva ca /
putro 'nanyāśritadravyaḥ putrahīnasya ṛkthinaḥ //
253.d:
ऋक्थग्राह ऋणं दाप्यो योषिद्ग्राहस्तथैव च /
पुत्रो ऽनन्याश्रितद्रव्यः पुत्रहीनस्य ऋक्थिनः //
253.m: The heir must be made to pay the debt, and likewise the taker of the widow; / the son whose wealth has not passed to another [must pay], or the heirs of a sonless man.

253.s:
avibhuktaiḥ kuṭumbārthaṃ yadṛṇantu kṛtambhavet /
dadyustadṛkthinaḥ prete proṣite vā kuṭumbini //
253.d:
अविभुक्तैः कुटुम्बार्थं यदृणन्तु कृतम्भवेत् /
दद्युस्तदृक्थिनः प्रेते प्रोषिते वा कुटुम्बिनि //
253.m: Any debt that has been contracted by undivided [coparceners] for the sake of the family / the heirs must pay, if the head of the family has died or gone abroad.

253.s:
na yoṣit patiputrābhyāṃ na putreṇa kṛtaṃ pitā /
dadyādṛte kuṭumbārthānna patiḥ strīkṛtaṃ tathā //
253.d:
न योषित् पतिपुत्राभ्यां न पुत्रेण कृतं पिता /
दद्यादृते कुटुम्बार्थान्न पतिः स्त्रीकृतं तथा //
253.m: A woman need not pay what was contracted by her husband and son, nor a father what was contracted by his son, / except if contracted for the sake of the family; nor a husband what was contracted by his wife.

253.s:
gopaśauṇḍikaśainūṣarajakavyādhayoṣitāṃ /
ṛṇaṃ dadyātpatistvāsāṃ yasmādvṛttistadāśrayā //
253.d:
गोपशौण्डिकशैनूषरजकव्याधयोषितां /
ऋणं दद्यात्पतिस्त्वासां यस्माद्वृत्तिस्तदाश्रया //
253.m: The husband of women who are cowherds, vintners, actors, washermen, or hunters / must pay their debt, because their livelihood depends upon them.

253.s:
pratipannaṃ striyā deyaṃ patyā vā saha yat kṛtaṃ /
svayaṃ kṛtaṃ vā yadṛṇaṃ nānyastrī dātumarhati //
253.d:
प्रतिपन्नं स्त्रिया देयं पत्या वा सह यत् कृतं /
स्वयं कृतं वा यदृणं नान्यस्त्री दातुमर्हति //
253.m: A debt agreed to by a woman must be paid, or what was contracted together with her husband, / or a debt contracted by herself; another woman ought not to pay [it].

253.s:
pitari proṣite prete vyasābhiplute 'tha vā(1) /
putrapautrair ṛṇandeyaṃ nihnave sākṣibhāvitam //
253.d:
पितरि प्रोषिते प्रेते व्यसाभिप्लुते ऽथ वा(1) /
पुत्रपौत्रैर् ऋणन्देयं निह्नवे साक्षिभावितम् //
253.m: When the father has gone abroad, has died, or is overwhelmed by distress, / the debt must be paid by his sons and grandsons; in case of denial, [it must be] proved by witnesses.

253.s:
surākāmadyūtakṛtandaṇḍaśulkāvaśiṣṭakam /
vṛthā dānaṃ tathaiveha putro dadyānna paitṛkam //
253.d:
सुराकामद्यूतकृतन्दण्डशुल्कावशिष्टकम् /
वृथा दानं तथैवेह पुत्रो दद्यान्न पैतृकम् //
253.m: A debt incurred for liquor, lust, or gambling, the remainder of a fine or toll, / or an idle gift—the son here need not pay such a paternal debt.

253.s:
bhrātṝṇāmatha dampatyoḥ pituḥ putrasya caiva hi /
:n
1 vyasanābhiplutepi veti kha.. , gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 414
pratibhāvyamṛṇaṃ grāhyamavibhaktena ca smṛtam(1) //
253.d:
भ्रातॄणामथ दम्पत्योः पितुः पुत्रस्य चैव हि /
:न्
1 व्यसनाभिप्लुतेपि वेति ख.. , घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 414
प्रतिभाव्यमृणं ग्राह्यमविभक्तेन च स्मृतम्(1) //
253.m:
Among brothers, or husband and wife, or father and son,
[note]
[note on variant readings] / [page 414]
suretyship, a debt, or [giving] evidence cannot be undertaken while undivided.

253.s:
darśane pratyaye dāne pratibhāvyaṃ vidhīyate /
ādhau tu vitathe dāpyā vitathasya sutā api //
253.d:
दर्शने प्रत्यये दाने प्रतिभाव्यं विधीयते /
आधौ तु वितथे दाप्या वितथस्य सुता अपि //
253.m: Suretyship is ordained for appearance, for confidence, and for payment; / but if the pledge is false, even the sons of the false [surety] must be made to pay.

253.s:
darśanapratibhūryatra mṛtaḥ prātyayiko 'pi vā /
na tatputrā dhanaṃ dadyurdadyurdānāya ye sthitāḥ //
253.d:
दर्शनप्रतिभूर्यत्र मृतः प्रात्ययिको ऽपि वा /
न तत्पुत्रा धनं दद्युर्दद्युर्दानाय ये स्थिताः //
253.m: Where a surety for appearance or one for confidence has died, / his sons need not pay the money; those who stood for payment must pay.

253.s:
bahavaḥ syuryadi svāṃśair dadyuḥ pratibhuvo dhanam /
ekacchāyāśriteṣveṣu dhanikasya yathā ruci //
253.d:
बहवः स्युर्यदि स्वांशैर् दद्युः प्रतिभुवो धनम् /
एकच्छायाश्रितेष्वेषु धनिकस्य यथा रुचि //
253.m: If there are many sureties, they must pay the money in their own shares; / when they are bound under joint liability, [it is recovered] according to the creditor's pleasure.

253.s:
pratibhūrdāpito yatra prakāśaṃ dhanine dhanam /
dviguṇaṃ pratidātavyamṛṇikaistasya tadbhavet //
253.d:
प्रतिभूर्दापितो यत्र प्रकाशं धनिने धनम् /
द्विगुणं प्रतिदातव्यमृणिकैस्तस्य तद्भवेत् //
253.m: Where a surety has been compelled to pay money publicly to the creditor, / twice as much must be repaid to him by the debtor.

253.s:
svasantatistrīpaśavyaṃ dhānyaṃ dviguṇameva ca /
vastraṃ caturguṇaṃ proktaṃ rasaścāṣṭaguṇas tathā //
253.d:
स्वसन्ततिस्त्रीपशव्यं धान्यं द्विगुणमेव च /
वस्त्रं चतुर्गुणं प्रोक्तं रसश्चाष्टगुणस् तथा //
253.m: Female cattle [are repaid] with their offspring; grain is twofold; / cloth is declared fourfold, and liquids eightfold.

253.s:
ādhiḥ praṇaśyet dviguṇe dhane yadi na mokṣyate /
kāle kālakṛtaṃ naśyet phalabhogyo na naśyati //
253.d:
आधिः प्रणश्येत् द्विगुणे धने यदि न मोक्ष्यते /
काले कालकृतं नश्येत् फलभोग्यो न नश्यति //
253.m: A pledge is forfeited when the debt has doubled, if it is not redeemed; / a pledge made for a fixed time is forfeited when the time arrives; a pledge whose usufruct is enjoyed is not forfeited.

253.s:
gopyādhibhogyo nāvṛddhiḥ sopakāre 'tha bhāvite /
naṣṭo deyo vinaṣṭaś ca daivarājakṛtādṛte //
253.d:
गोप्याधिभोग्यो नावृद्धिः सोपकारे ऽथ भाविते /
नष्टो देयो विनष्टश् च दैवराजकृतादृते //
253.m: There is no interest on a pledge to be preserved if it is used, nor if it provides service, once proved; / if lost or ruined, it must be replaced, except if caused by fate or the king.

253.s:
ādheḥ svīkaraṇātsiddhaurakṣamāṇopyasāratām /
yātaścedanya ādheyo dhanabhāg vā dhanī bhavet //
253.d:
आधेः स्वीकरणात्सिद्धौरक्षमाणोप्यसारताम् /
यातश्चेदन्य आधेयो धनभाग् वा धनी भवेत् //
253.m: When the pledge has been established by possession, if, even while being guarded, it has deteriorated / into worthlessness, another must be pledged, or the creditor must receive his money.

253.s:
caritraṃ bandhakakṛtaṃ savṛddhaṃ dāpayedvanaṃ /
satyaṅkārakṛtaṃ dravyaṃ dviguṇaṃ pratidāpayet //
253.d:
चरित्रं बन्धककृतं सवृद्धं दापयेद्वनं /
सत्यङ्कारकृतं द्रव्यं द्विगुणं प्रतिदापयेत् //
253.m: He should make the debtor pay the money secured by a pledge of good character with interest; / an earnest-money deposit must be made to be repaid twofold.

253.s:
upasthitasya moktavya ādhirdaṇḍo 'nyathā bhavet /
prayojake sati dhanaṃ kulenyasyādhimāpnuyāt //
253.d:
उपस्थितस्य मोक्तव्य आधिर्दण्डो ऽन्यथा भवेत् /
प्रयोजके सति धनं कुलेन्यस्याधिमाप्नुयात् //
253.m: A pledge must be released when [the debtor] is present; otherwise there will be a fine; / in the absence of the creditor, one may deposit the money with an arbitrator and recover the pledge,

253.s:
tatkālakṛtamūlyo vā tatra tiṣṭhedavṛddhikaḥ /
:n
1 pratibhāvyamṛṇaṃ sākṣyamavibhaktena tat smṛtamiti kha.. , ga.. ,
gha.. , cha.. , ja.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 415
vinā dhāraṇakādvāpi vikrīṇīte sasākṣikam //
253.d:
तत्कालकृतमूल्यो वा तत्र तिष्ठेदवृद्धिकः /
:न्
1 प्रतिभाव्यमृणं साक्ष्यमविभक्तेन तत् स्मृतमिति ख.. , ग.. ,
घ.. , छ.. , ज.. , ट.. च
:प् 415
विना धारणकाद्वापि विक्रीणीते ससाक्षिकम् //
253.m:
or it may remain there interest-free, valued at the price of that time;
[note]
[note on variant readings] / [page 415]
or [the creditor] may sell it with witnesses, even without the debtor.

253.s:
yadā tu dviguṇībhūtamṛṇamādhau tadā khalu /
mocyaścādhistadutpādya praviṣṭe dviguṇe dhane //
253.d:
यदा तु द्विगुणीभूतमृणमाधौ तदा खलु /
मोच्यश्चाधिस्तदुत्पाद्य प्रविष्टे द्विगुणे धने //
253.m: When indeed the debt has become doubled while on pledge, / then the pledge must be released, when double the amount has entered [the creditor's hands] through its yield.

253.s:
vyasanasthamanākhyāya haste 'nyasya yadarpayet /
dravyaṃ tadaupanidhikaṃ pratideyaṃ tathaiva tat //
253.d:
व्यसनस्थमनाख्याय हस्ते ऽन्यस्य यदर्पयेत् /
द्रव्यं तदौपनिधिकं प्रतिदेयं तथैव तत् //
253.m: When one entrusts property into another's hand without declaring its contents while in distress, / that is an open deposit (aupanidhika); it must be returned in the very same state.

253.s:
na dāpyo 'pahṛtaṃ tattu rājadaivakataskaraiḥ /
preṣaścenmārgite datte dāpyo daṇḍaś ca tatsamam //
253.d:
न दाप्यो ऽपहृतं तत्तु राजदैवकतस्करैः /
प्रेषश्चेन्मार्गिते दत्ते दाप्यो दण्डश् च तत्समम् //
253.m: He cannot be made to pay if it was stolen by the king, an act of god, or thieves; / but if after it was demanded he does not give it, he must be made to pay [it] and an equal fine.

253.s:
ājīvan svecchayā daṇḍyo dāpyastaccāpi sodayaṃ /
yācitāvāhitanyāse nikṣepeṣvapyayaṃ vidhiḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe vyavahāro nāma
tripañcāśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha catuḥpañcāśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
divyapramāṇakathanaṃ
253.d:
आजीवन् स्वेच्छया दण्ड्यो दाप्यस्तच्चापि सोदयं /
याचितावाहितन्यासे निक्षेपेष्वप्ययं विधिः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे व्यवहारो नाम
त्रिपञ्चाशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ चतुःपञ्चाशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
दिव्यप्रमाणकथनं
253.m:
If he uses it for his livelihood of his own accord, he must be fined and made to pay it back with profit; / this same rule applies to borrowed goods, goods deposited for safety, and sealed deposits.
Thus in the great Agni Purāṇa, the two hundred and fifty-third chapter, entitled Judicial Procedure.
Now, the two hundred and fifty-fourth chapter:
Discourse on Divine Proofs.

254.s:
agnir uvāca
tapasvino dānaśīlāḥ kulīnāḥ satyavādinaḥ /
dharmapradhānā ṛjavaḥ putravanto dhanānvitāḥ //
254.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
तपस्विनो दानशीलाः कुलीनाः सत्यवादिनः /
धर्मप्रधाना ऋजवः पुत्रवन्तो धनान्विताः //
254.m: Agni said: / Ascetics, charitable men, those of noble birth, truth-tellers, / dedicated to righteousness, upright, having sons, possessed of wealth,

254.s:
pañcayajñakriyāyuktāḥ sākṣiṇaḥ pañca vā trayaḥ /
yathājāti yathāvarṇa sarve sarveṣu vā smṛtāḥ //
254.d:
पञ्चयज्ञक्रियायुक्ताः साक्षिणः पञ्च वा त्रयः /
यथाजाति यथावर्ण सर्वे सर्वेषु वा स्मृताः //
254.m: engaged in the rites of the five daily sacrifices—such witnesses should be five or three, / or according to their caste and class, or all [may be witnesses] in all cases.

254.s:
strīvṛddhabālakitavamattonmattābhiśastakāḥ /
:p 416
raṅgāvatāripāṣaṇḍikūṭakṛdvikalendriyāḥ //
254.d:
स्त्रीवृद्धबालकितवमत्तोन्मत्ताभिशस्तकाः /
:प् 416
रङ्गावतारिपाषण्डिकूटकृद्विकलेन्द्रियाः //
254.m:
Women, old men, children, gamblers, intoxicated persons, madmen, accused persons,
[page 416]
actors, heretics, forgers, those with defective senses,

254.s:
patitāptānnasambandhisahāyariputaskarāḥ /
amākṣiṇaḥ sarvasākṣī cauryapāruṣyasāhase //
254.d:
पतिताप्तान्नसम्बन्धिसहायरिपुतस्कराः /
अमाक्षिणः सर्वसाक्षी चौर्यपारुष्यसाहसे //
254.m: outcastes, intimate friends, co-diners, relatives, associates, enemies, and thieves / are incompetent witnesses; but anyone may be a witness in cases of theft, defamation, and violence.

254.s:
ubhayānumataḥ sākṣī bhavatyekopi dharmavit /
abruvan hi naraḥ sākṣyamṛṇaṃ sadaśabandhakam //
254.d:
उभयानुमतः साक्षी भवत्येकोपि धर्मवित् /
अब्रुवन् हि नरः साक्ष्यमृणं सदशबन्धकम् //
254.m: Even a single person, knowing the law, may be a witness if approved by both parties. / A man who does not give evidence must pay the whole debt together with a tenth part [as a fine]

254.s:
rājñā sarvaṃ pradāpyaḥ syāt ṣaṭcatvāriṃśake 'hnani /
na dadāti hi yaḥ sākṣyaṃ jānannapi narādhamaḥ //
254.d:
राज्ञा सर्वं प्रदाप्यः स्यात् षट्चत्वारिंशके ऽह्ननि /
न ददाति हि यः साक्ष्यं जानन्नपि नराधमः //
254.m: to the king on the forty-sixth day. / For the vile man who, although knowing, does not give evidence,

254.s:
sa kūṭasākṣiṇāṃ pāpaistulyo daṇḍena caiva hi /
sākṣiṇaḥ śrāvayedvādiprativādisamīpagān //
254.d:
स कूटसाक्षिणां पापैस्तुल्यो दण्डेन चैव हि /
साक्षिणः श्रावयेद्वादिप्रतिवादिसमीपगान् //
254.m: is equal to false witnesses in sins and also in punishment. / One should summon the witnesses close to the plaintiff and defendant and make them hear [the warning]:

254.s:
ye pātakakṛtāṃ lokā mahāpātakināṃ tathā /
agnidānāñca ye lokā ye ca strībālaghātināṃ //
254.d:
ये पातककृतां लोका महापातकिनां तथा /
अग्निदानाञ्च ये लोका ये च स्त्रीबालघातिनां //
254.m: “The worlds that belong to perpetrators of sins, and to perpetrators of mortal sins, / and the worlds that belong to incendiaries, and those who kill women and children,

254.s:
tān sarvān samavāpnoti yaḥ sākṣyamanṛtaṃ vadet /
sukṛtaṃ yattvayā kiñcijjanmāntaraśataiḥ kṛtam //
254.d:
तान् सर्वान् समवाप्नोति यः साक्ष्यमनृतं वदेत् /
सुकृतं यत्त्वया किञ्चिज्जन्मान्तरशतैः कृतम् //
254.m: all those [worlds] are attained by one who speaks false testimony. / Whatever merit was acquired by you in hundreds of other births,

254.s:
tatsarvaṃ tasya jānīhi yaṃ parājayase mṛṣā /
dvaidhe bahūnāṃ vacanaṃ sameṣu guṇināntathā //
254.d:
तत्सर्वं तस्य जानीहि यं पराजयसे मृषा /
द्वैधे बहूनां वचनं समेषु गुणिनान्तथा //
254.m: know that it all belongs to him whom you falsely defeat.” / In case of conflict, the statement of the majority [prevails]; among equal numbers, that of the virtuous;

254.s:
guṇidvaidhe tu vacanaṃ grāhyaṃ ye guṇavattarāḥ /
yasyocuḥ sākṣiṇaḥ satyāṃ pratijñāṃ sa jayī bhavet //
254.d:
गुणिद्वैधे तु वचनं ग्राह्यं ये गुणवत्तराः /
यस्योचुः साक्षिणः सत्यां प्रतिज्ञां स जयी भवेत् //
254.m: in case of conflict among the virtuous, the statement of those who are superior in virtue is to be accepted. / He whose claim the witnesses declare to be true becomes the winner;

254.s:
anyathā vādino yasya dhrūvastasya parājayaḥ /
ukte 'pi sākṣibhiḥ sākṣye yadyanye guṇavattarāḥ //
254.d:
अन्यथा वादिनो यस्य ध्रूवस्तस्य पराजयः /
उक्ते ऽपि साक्षिभिः साक्ष्ये यद्यन्ये गुणवत्तराः //
254.m: otherwise, defeat is certain for that litigant. / Even after testimony has been given by witnesses, if others more virtuous,

254.s:
dviguṇā vānyathā brūyuḥ kūṭāḥ syuḥpūrvasākṣiṇaḥ /
pṛthak pṛthagdaṇḍanīyāḥ kūṭakṛtsākṣiṇas tathā //
254.d:
द्विगुणा वान्यथा ब्रूयुः कूटाः स्युःपूर्वसाक्षिणः /
पृथक् पृथग्दण्डनीयाः कूटकृत्साक्षिणस् तथा //
254.m: or twice as many, speak otherwise, the earlier witnesses become false ones. / The false witnesses are to be punished individually,

254.s:
vivādāddviguṇaṃ daṇḍaṃ vivāsyo brāhmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ /
yaḥ sākṣyaṃ śrāvito 'nyebhyo nihnute tattamovṛtaḥ //
:p 417
254.d:
विवादाद्द्विगुणं दण्डं विवास्यो ब्राह्मणः स्मृतः /
यः साक्ष्यं श्रावितो ऽन्येभ्यो निह्नुते तत्तमोवृतः //
:प् 417
254.m:
with a fine twice that of the suit; a brāhmaṇa is declared to be banished. / He who, having been summoned to testify, denies it to others, overcome by darkness,
[page 417]

254.s:
sa dāpyo 'ṣṭaguṇam daṇḍaṃ brāhmaṇantu vivāsayet /
varṇināṃ hi badho yatra tatra sākṣya.anṛtaṃ vadet //
254.d:
स दाप्यो ऽष्टगुणम् दण्डं ब्राह्मणन्तु विवासयेत् /
वर्णिनां हि बधो यत्र तत्र साक्ष्य.अनृतं वदेत् //
254.m: must be made to pay an eightfold fine, but a brāhmaṇa should be banished. / Where the death of persons of the [twice-born] classes [would result], there one may speak false testimony.

254.s:
yaḥ kaścidartho 'bhimataḥ svarucyā tu parasparaṃ /
lekhyaṃ tu sākṣimat kāryaṃ tasmin dhanikapūrvakam //
254.d:
यः कश्चिदर्थो ऽभिमतः स्वरुच्या तु परस्परं /
लेख्यं तु साक्षिमत् कार्यं तस्मिन् धनिकपूर्वकम् //
254.m: Whatever transaction is mutually agreed upon by their own choice, / a document with witnesses should be made for it, beginning with the creditor's [name].

254.s:
samāmāsatadarhāhar nāmajātisvagotrajaiḥ /
sabrahmacārikātmīyapitṛnāmādicihnitam //
254.d:
समामासतदर्हाहर् नामजातिस्वगोत्रजैः /
सब्रह्मचारिकात्मीयपितृनामादिचिह्नितम् //
254.m: marked with the year, month, fortnight, and day, along with the names, castes, and gotras [of the parties], / and the names of their fellow students, their own names, and the names of their fathers.

254.s:
samāpte 'rthe ṛṇī nāma svahastena niveśayet /
mataṃ me 'mukaputrasya yadatroparilekhitaṃ //
254.d:
समाप्ते ऽर्थे ऋणी नाम स्वहस्तेन निवेशयेत् /
मतं मे ऽमुकपुत्रस्य यदत्रोपरिलेखितं //
254.m: When the matter is concluded, the debtor should write his name with his own hand: / ‘Approved by me, son of so-and-so, whatever has been written above.’

254.s:
sākṣiṇaś ca svahastena pitṛnāmakapūrvakam /
atrāhamamukaḥ sākṣī likheyuriti te samāḥ //
254.d:
साक्षिणश् च स्वहस्तेन पितृनामकपूर्वकम् /
अत्राहममुकः साक्षी लिखेयुरिति ते समाः //
254.m: And the witnesses, in equal number, should write with their own hand, preceded by their fathers’ names: / ‘Here I, so-and-so, am a witness.’

254.s:
alipijña ṛṇī yaḥ syālekayet svamatantu saḥ /
sākṣī vā sākṣiṇānyena sarvasākṣisamīpataḥ //
254.d:
अलिपिज्ञ ऋणी यः स्यालेकयेत् स्वमतन्तु सः /
साक्षी वा साक्षिणान्येन सर्वसाक्षिसमीपतः //
254.m: A debtor who cannot write should cause his approval to be written, / or a witness [should cause it to be written] by another witness, in the presence of all the witnesses.

254.s:
ubhayābhyarthitenaitanmayā hy amukasūnunā /
likhitaṃ hy amukeneti lekhako 'thāntato likhet //
254.d:
उभयाभ्यर्थितेनैतन्मया ह्य् अमुकसूनुना /
लिखितं ह्य् अमुकेनेति लेखको ऽथान्ततो लिखेत् //
254.m: Then at the end the scribe should write: ‘Requested by both, this has been written / by me, so-and-so, son of so-and-so.’

254.s:
vināpi sākṣibhir lekhyaṃ svahastalikhitañca yat /
tat pramāṇaṃ smṛtaṃ sarvaṃ balopadhikṛtādṛte //
254.d:
विनापि साक्षिभिर् लेख्यं स्वहस्तलिखितञ्च यत् /
तत् प्रमाणं स्मृतं सर्वं बलोपधिकृतादृते //
254.m: Even without witnesses, a document written in one's own hand / is considered authoritative in all matters, except when executed through force or fraud.

254.s:
ṛṇaṃ lekhyakṛtaṃ deyaṃ puruṣaistribhireva tu /
ādhistu bhujyate tāvadyāvattanna pradīyate //
254.d:
ऋणं लेख्यकृतं देयं पुरुषैस्त्रिभिरेव तु /
आधिस्तु भुज्यते तावद्यावत्तन्न प्रदीयते //
254.m: A debt contracted by a document must be paid by three generations only; / but a pledge may be enjoyed as long as that [debt] is not repaid.

254.s:
deśāntarasthe durlekhye naṣṭonmṛṣṭe hṛte tathā /
bhinne cchinne tathā dagdhe lekhyamanyattu kārayet //
254.d:
देशान्तरस्थे दुर्लेख्ये नष्टोन्मृष्टे हृते तथा /
भिन्ने च्छिन्ने तथा दग्धे लेख्यमन्यत्तु कारयेत् //
254.m: If it is in another country, illegibly written, lost, effaced, stolen, / broken, torn, or burnt, one should cause another document to be made.

254.s:
sandigdhārthaviśuddhyarthaṃ svahastalikhitantu yat /
yuktiprāptikriyācihnasambandhāgamahetubhiḥ //
254.d:
सन्दिग्धार्थविशुद्ध्यर्थं स्वहस्तलिखितन्तु यत् /
युक्तिप्राप्तिक्रियाचिह्नसम्बन्धागमहेतुभिः //
254.m: To establish the correctness of a disputed matter, that which is written in one's own hand [is settled] / by reasonable inference, possession, the nature of the transaction, distinguishing marks, connection, and origin.

254.s:
lekhyasya pṛṣṭhe 'bhilikhet praviṣṭamadhamarṇinaḥ /
:p 418
dhanī copagataṃ dadyāt svahastaparicihnitam //
254.d:
लेख्यस्य पृष्ठे ऽभिलिखेत् प्रविष्टमधमर्णिनः /
:प् 418
धनी चोपगतं दद्यात् स्वहस्तपरिचिह्नितम् //
254.m:
On the back of the document, one should record what has been paid by the debtor.
[p. 418]
And the creditor should give an acknowledgment marked with his own hand.

254.s:
datvarṇaṃ pāṭayellekhyaṃ śuddhyai cānyattu kārayet /
sākṣimacca bhavedyattu taddātavyaṃ sasākṣikaṃ //
254.d:
दत्वर्णं पाटयेल्लेख्यं शुद्ध्यै चान्यत्तु कारयेत् /
साक्षिमच्च भवेद्यत्तु तद्दातव्यं ससाक्षिकं //
254.m: Having paid the debt, one should tear up the document, and make another for clearance; / and that which was made with witnesses should be repaid before witnesses.

254.s:
tulāgnyāpo viṣaṃ koṣo divyānīha viśuddhaye /
mahābhiyogeṣvetāni śīrṣakasthe 'bhiyoktari //
254.d:
तुलाग्न्यापो विषं कोषो दिव्यानीह विशुद्धये /
महाभियोगेष्वेतानि शीर्षकस्थे ऽभियोक्तरि //
254.m: The balance, fire, water, poison, and consecrated water are the ordeals for purification here; / these apply in cases of grave accusations, when the accuser agrees to bear the penalty.

254.s:
rucyā vānyataraḥ kuryāditaro vartayecchiraḥ /
vināpi śīrṣakāt kuryānnṛpadrohe 'tha pātake //
254.d:
रुच्या वान्यतरः कुर्यादितरो वर्तयेच्छिरः /
विनापि शीर्षकात् कुर्यान्नृपद्रोहे ऽथ पातके //
254.m: Or by choice one may undergo [the ordeal], and the other shall risk his head; / but in treason against the king or in heinous sin, one may perform it even without risking the head.

254.s:
nāsahasrāddharet phālaṃ na tulānna viṣantathā /
nṛpārtheṣvabhiyogeṣu vaheyuḥ śucayaḥ sadā //
254.d:
नासहस्राद्धरेत् फालं न तुलान्न विषन्तथा /
नृपार्थेष्वभियोगेषु वहेयुः शुचयः सदा //
254.m: One should not administer the ploughshare, nor the balance, nor poison for less than a thousand [paṇas]; / in accusations concerning the king's affairs, pure persons should always undergo them.

254.s:
sahasrārthe tulādīni koṣamalpe 'pi dāpayet /
śatārdhaṃ dāpayecchuddhamaśuddho daṇḍabhāg bhavet //
254.d:
सहस्रार्थे तुलादीनि कोषमल्पे ऽपि दापयेत् /
शतार्धं दापयेच्छुद्धमशुद्धो दण्डभाग् भवेत् //
254.m: For a value of a thousand, the balance and the like [are used]; consecrated water may be given even in a minor matter; / one should cause the purified person to be given fifty [paṇas], while the impure one shall incur a fine.

254.s:
sacelasnātamāhūya sūryodaya upoṣitam /
kārayetdarvadivyāni nṛpabrāhmaṇasannidhau //
254.d:
सचेलस्नातमाहूय सूर्योदय उपोषितम् /
कारयेत्दर्वदिव्यानि नृपब्राह्मणसन्निधौ //
254.m: Having summoned [the accused] after he has bathed with his clothes on and fasted at sunrise, / one should cause all ordeals to be performed in the presence of the king and Brahmins.

254.s:
tulā strībālavṛddhāndhapaṅgubrāhmaṇarogiṇāṃ /
agnirjvalaṃ vā śūdrasya yavāḥ sapta viṣasya vā //
254.d:
तुला स्त्रीबालवृद्धान्धपङ्गुब्राह्मणरोगिणां /
अग्निर्ज्वलं वा शूद्रस्य यवाः सप्त विषस्य वा //
254.m: The balance is for women, children, the elderly, the blind, the lame, Brahmins, and the sick; / fire or water is for a Śūdra, or seven barleycorns [in weight] of poison.

254.s:
tulādhāraṇavidvadbhirabhiyuktastulāśritaḥ /
pratimānasamībhūto rekhāṃ kṛtvāvatāritaḥ //
254.d:
तुलाधारणविद्वद्भिरभियुक्तस्तुलाश्रितः /
प्रतिमानसमीभूतो रेखां कृत्वावतारितः //
254.m: Placed on the balance by persons skilled in holding the balance, / made equal to the counterweight, a mark having been made, he is taken down.

254.s:
ādityacandrāvanilo 'nalaś ca dyaurbhūmirāpohṛdayaṃ yamaś ca /
ahaś ca rātriś ca ubhe ca sandhye dharmaś ca jānāti narasya vṛttam //
254.d:
आदित्यचन्द्रावनिलो ऽनलश् च द्यौर्भूमिरापोहृदयं यमश् च /
अहश् च रात्रिश् च उभे च सन्ध्ये धर्मश् च जानाति नरस्य वृत्तम् //
254.m: “The sun and moon, wind and fire, heaven, earth, water, the heart, and Yama, / day and night, both twilights, and Dharma know the conduct of a man.

254.s:
tvaṃ tule satyadhāmāsi purā devair vinirmitā /
satyaṃ vadasva kalyāṇi saṃśayānmāṃ vimocaya //
:p 419
254.d:
त्वं तुले सत्यधामासि पुरा देवैर् विनिर्मिता /
सत्यं वदस्व कल्याणि संशयान्मां विमोचय //
:प् 419
254.m:
You, O balance, are the abode of truth, fashioned of old by the gods; / speak the truth, O auspicious one, and release me from doubt!
[p. 419]

254.s:
yadyasmi pāpakṛnmātastato māṃ tvamadho naya /
śuddhaścedgamayordhvammāṃ tulāmityabhimantrayet //
254.d:
यद्यस्मि पापकृन्मातस्ततो मां त्वमधो नय /
शुद्धश्चेद्गमयोर्ध्वम्मां तुलामित्यभिमन्त्रयेत् //
254.m: If I am an evildoer, O mother, then bring me down; / but if I am pure, raise me up!” Thus he should address the balance.

254.s:
karau vimṛditavrīherlakṣayitvā tato nyaset /
saptāśvaptyasya patrāṇi tāvat sūtreṇa veṣṭayet //
254.d:
करौ विमृदितव्रीहेर्लक्षयित्वा ततो न्यसेत् /
सप्ताश्वप्त्यस्य पत्राणि तावत् सूत्रेण वेष्टयेत् //
254.m: Having inspected his hands after rubbing them with unhusked rice, he should then place / seven leaves of the sacred fig tree [upon them] and wrap them with that many rounds of thread.

254.s:
tvameva sarvabhūtānāmantaś carasi pāvaka /
sākṣivat puṇyapāpebhyo brūhi satyaṅgare mama //
254.d:
त्वमेव सर्वभूतानामन्तश् चरसि पावक /
साक्षिवत् पुण्यपापेभ्यो ब्रूहि सत्यङ्गरे मम //
254.m: “You alone move within all beings, O purifier! / Witness-like to merit and sin, declare the truth in my hand.”

254.s:
tasyetyuktavato lauhaṃ pañcāśatpalikaṃ samam /
agnirvarṇaṃ nyaset piṇḍaṃ hastayorubhayorapi //
254.d:
तस्येत्युक्तवतो लौहं पञ्चाशत्पलिकं समम् /
अग्निर्वर्णं न्यसेत् पिण्डं हस्तयोरुभयोरपि //
254.m: When he has spoken thus, [the judge] should place an iron ball weighing fifty palas, smooth, / glowing like fire, upon both of his hands.

254.s:
sa tamādāya saptaiva maṇḍalāni śatair vrajet /
ṣoḍaśāṅgulakaṃ jñeyaṃ maṇḍalaṃ tāvadantaram //
254.d:
स तमादाय सप्तैव मण्डलानि शतैर् व्रजेत् /
षोडशाङ्गुलकं ज्ञेयं मण्डलं तावदन्तरम् //
254.m: Taking that, he should walk through seven circles with paces; / a circle is to be understood as sixteen aṅgulas, and the interval between them the same.

254.s:
muktvāgniṃ mṛditavrīhiradagdhaḥ śuddhimāpnuyāt /
antarā patite piṇḍe sandehe vā punarharet //
254.d:
मुक्त्वाग्निं मृदितव्रीहिरदग्धः शुद्धिमाप्नुयात् /
अन्तरा पतिते पिण्डे सन्देहे वा पुनर्हरेत् //
254.m: Releasing the fire, if his hands are unburned after rubbing rice, he attains vindication; / if the ball falls in the middle, or if there is doubt, he should carry it again.

254.s:
pavitrāṇāṃ pavitra tvaṃ śodhyaṃ śodhaya pāvana /
satyena mābhirakṣasva varuṇetyabhiśastakam //
254.d:
पवित्राणां पवित्र त्वं शोध्यं शोधय पावन /
सत्येन माभिरक्षस्व वरुणेत्यभिशस्तकम् //
254.m: “Purifier of purifiers, cleanse the one to be cleansed, O purifying one! / Protect me through truth, O Varuṇa!” Thus the accused [prays].

254.s:
nābhidaghnodakasthasya gṛhītvorū jalaṃ viśet /
samakālamiṣuṃ muktamānīyānyo javo naraḥ //
254.d:
नाभिदघ्नोदकस्थस्य गृहीत्वोरू जलं विशेत् /
समकालमिषुं मुक्तमानीयान्यो जवो नरः //
254.m: Standing in navel-deep water, holding the thighs [of another], he should enter the water; / at the very same time an arrow is shot, another swift man brings it back.

254.s:
yadi tasminnimagnāṅgaṃ paśyecca śuddhimāpnuyāt /
tvaṃ viṣa brahmaṇaḥ putra satyadharme vyavasthita //
254.d:
यदि तस्मिन्निमग्नाङ्गं पश्येच्च शुद्धिमाप्नुयात् /
त्वं विष ब्रह्मणः पुत्र सत्यधर्मे व्यवस्थित //
254.m: If he sees him with his limbs submerged when he returns, he attains vindication. / “O poison, son of Brahmā, established in truth and righteousness,

254.s:
trāyasvāsmādabhīśāpāt satyena bhava me 'mṛtam /
evamuktvā viṣaṃ sārṅgaṃ bhakṣayeddhimaśailajaṃ //
254.d:
त्रायस्वास्मादभीशापात् सत्येन भव मे ऽमृतम् /
एवमुक्त्वा विषं सार्ङ्गं भक्षयेद्धिमशैलजं //
254.m: save me from this accusation; through truth become nectar to me!” / Having spoken thus, he should eat the horned poison born of the snowy mountain.

254.s:
yasya vegair vinā jīrṇaṃ śuddhiṃ tasya vinirdiśet /
devānugrān samabhyarcya tatsnānodakamāharet //
254.d:
यस्य वेगैर् विना जीर्णं शुद्धिं तस्य विनिर्दिशेत् /
देवानुग्रान् समभ्यर्च्य तत्स्नानोदकमाहरेत् //
254.m: If it is digested by him without violent fits, one should declare his purity. / Having worshipped the fierce deities, one should take the water of their bathing;

254.s:
saṃśrāvya pāpayettasmājjalāttu prasṛtitrayam /
:p 420
ācaturdaśamādahno yasya no rājadaivikam //
254.d:
संश्राव्य पापयेत्तस्माज्जलात्तु प्रसृतित्रयम् /
:प् 420
आचतुर्दशमादह्नो यस्य नो राजदैविकम् //
254.m:
having made him hear the oath, he should make him drink three palmfuls of that water.
[p. 420]
For whom up to the fourteenth day no royal or divine

254.s:
vyasanaṃ jāyate ghoraṃ sa śuddhaḥ syādasaṃśayam /
satyavāhanaśastrāṇi govījakanakāni ca //
254.d:
व्यसनं जायते घोरं स शुद्धः स्यादसंशयम् /
सत्यवाहनशस्त्राणि गोवीजकनकानि च //
254.m: terrible calamity occurs, he is pure beyond doubt. / [Swearing by] truth, vehicles, weapons, cattle, grain, and gold,

254.s:
devatāgurupādāś ca iṣṭāpūrtakṛtāni ca /
ityete sukarāḥ proktāḥ śapathāḥ svalpasaṃśaye //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe divyāni pramāṇāni nāma
catuḥpañcāśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha pañcapañcāśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
dāyavibhāgakathanam
254.d:
देवतागुरुपादाश् च इष्टापूर्तकृतानि च /
इत्येते सुकराः प्रोक्ताः शपथाः स्वल्पसंशये //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे दिव्यानि प्रमाणानि नाम
चतुःपञ्चाशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ पञ्चपञ्चाशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
दायविभागकथनम्
254.m:
the feet of deities and gurus, and the merit of sacrifices and charitable works— / these are declared easy oaths in cases of minor doubt.
Thus in the great Agni Purāṇa, the two hundred and fifty-fourth chapter, entitled “Ordeals as Means of Proof.”
Now, the two hundred and fifty-fifth chapter.
The exposition of partition of inheritance.

255.s:
agnir uvāca
vibhāgañcet pitā kuryādicchayā vibhajet sutān /
jyeṣṭhaṃ vā śreṣṭhabhāgena sarve vā syuḥ samāṃśinaḥ //
255.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
विभागञ्चेत् पिता कुर्यादिच्छया विभजेत् सुतान् /
ज्येष्ठं वा श्रेष्ठभागेन सर्वे वा स्युः समांशिनः //
255.m: Agni said: / If a father makes a partition, he may divide [the property among] his sons at his pleasure, / or [give] the eldest the best share, or all may receive equal shares.

255.s:
yadi dadyāt samānaṃśān kāryāḥ patnyaḥ samāṃśikāḥ /
na dattaṃ strīdhanaṃ yāsāṃ bhartrā vā śvaśurena vā //
255.d:
यदि दद्यात् समानंशान् कार्याः पत्न्यः समांशिकाः /
न दत्तं स्त्रीधनं यासां भर्त्रा वा श्वशुरेन वा //
255.m: If he gives equal shares, his wives must be made equal sharers, / [provided] woman’s property has not been given to them by the husband or father-in-law.

255.s:
śaktasthānīhamānasya kiñciddatvā pṛthak kriyā /
nyūnādhikavibhaktānāṃ dharmyaś ca pitṛnā kṛtaḥ //
255.d:
शक्तस्थानीहमानस्य किञ्चिद्दत्वा पृथक् क्रिया /
न्यूनाधिकविभक्तानां धर्म्यश् च पितृना कृतः //
255.m: For an able [son] who does not desire [a share], separation is made by giving something small; / and a partition made by the father, whether [shares be] less or more, is lawful.

255.s:
vibhajeyuḥ sutāḥ pitrorūrdhvamṛkthamṛṇaṃ samam /
māturduhitaraḥ śeṣamṛṇāttābhya ṛte 'nnayaḥ //
255.d:
विभजेयुः सुताः पित्रोरूर्ध्वमृक्थमृणं समम् /
मातुर्दुहितरः शेषमृणात्ताभ्य ऋते ऽन्नयः //
255.m: After the parents, the sons should divide equally the inheritance and the debt; / daughters [receive] what remains of the mother's [property] after [paying] the debt, and in their absence, the male descendants.

255.s:
pitṛdravyāvināśena yadanyat svayamarjayet /
maitramaudvāhikañcaiva dāyādānānna tadbhavet //
255.d:
पितृद्रव्याविनाशेन यदन्यत् स्वयमर्जयेत् /
मैत्रमौद्वाहिकञ्चैव दायादानान्न तद्भवेत् //
255.m: Whatever else one acquires by oneself without detriment to the ancestral wealth, / [such as] a gift from a friend or through marriage, shall not belong to the co-heirs.

255.s:
sāmānyārthasamutthāne vibhāgastu samaḥ smṛtaḥ /
:p 421
anekapitṛkāṇāntu pitṛto bhāgakalpanā //
255.d:
सामान्यार्थसमुत्थाने विभागस्तु समः स्मृतः /
:प् 421
अनेकपितृकाणान्तु पितृतो भागकल्पना //
255.m:
When an increase arises from common property, the division is considered equal.
[p. 421]
Among those having different fathers, however, the determination of the share is through the father.

255.s:
bhūryāpitā mahopāttā nibandho dravyameva vā /
tatra syāt sadṛśaṃ svāmyaṃ pituḥ putrasya cobhayoḥ //
255.d:
भूर्यापिता महोपात्ता निबन्धो द्रव्यमेव वा /
तत्र स्यात् सदृशं स्वाम्यं पितुः पुत्रस्य चोभयोः //
255.m: Land, a corrody, or property acquired by the grandfather: / in that, the ownership of both the father and the son is equal.

255.s:
vibhakteṣu suto jātaḥ savarṇāyāṃ vibhāgabhāk /
dṛśyādvā tadvibhāgaḥ syādāyavyayaviśodhitāt //
255.d:
विभक्तेषु सुतो जातः सवर्णायां विभागभाक् /
दृश्याद्वा तद्विभागः स्यादायव्ययविशोधितात् //
255.m: A son born of a woman of the same caste after partition is a participant in the partition, / or his share may be taken from the visible property, cleared of receipts and expenses.

255.s:
kramādabhyāgataṃ dravyaṃ hṛtamabhyuddharecca yaḥ /
dāyādebhyo na taddadyādvidyayā labdhameva ca //
255.d:
क्रमादभ्यागतं द्रव्यं हृतमभ्युद्धरेच्च यः /
दायादेभ्यो न तद्दद्याद्विद्यया लब्धमेव च //
255.m: And whoever recovers ancestral property that had been seized / shall not give that to the co-heirs; and likewise what is acquired through learning.

255.s:
pitṛbhyāṃ yasya yaddattaṃ tattasyaiva dhanaṃ bhavet /
piturūrdhvaṃ vibhajatāṃ mātāpyaṃśaṃ samaṃ haret //
255.d:
पितृभ्यां यस्य यद्दत्तं तत्तस्यैव धनं भवेत् /
पितुरूर्ध्वं विभजतां माताप्यंशं समं हरेत् //
255.m: Whatever is given to someone by the parents shall belong to that person alone; / among those dividing after the father, the mother also should take an equal share.

255.s:
asaṃskṛtāstu saṃskāryā bhrātṛbhiḥ pūrvasaṃskṛtaiḥ /
bhāginyaś ca nijādaṃśāddatvāṃśantu turīyakaṃ //
255.d:
असंस्कृतास्तु संस्कार्या भ्रातृभिः पूर्वसंस्कृतैः /
भागिन्यश् च निजादंशाद्दत्वांशन्तु तुरीयकं //
255.m: Uninitiated [brothers] are to be initiated by the brothers who have already been initiated, / and sisters [are provided for] by each giving a fourth share from their own share.

255.s:
catuḥstridvyekabhāgāḥ syurvarṇaśo brāhmaṇātmajāḥ /
kṣatrajāstridvyekabhāgā viḍjāstu dvyekabhāginaḥ //
255.d:
चतुःस्त्रिद्व्येकभागाः स्युर्वर्णशो ब्राह्मणात्मजाः /
क्षत्रजास्त्रिद्व्येकभागा विड्जास्तु द्व्येकभागिनः //
255.m: Sons of a Brāhmaṇa according to caste shall have four, three, two, and one shares; / sons born of a Kṣatriyā shall have three, two, and one shares; while those born of a Vaiśyā shall have two and one shares.

255.s:
anyonyāpahṛtaṃ dravyaṃ vibhakte yattu dṛśyate /
tat punaste samair aṃśair vibhajeranniti sthitiḥ //
255.d:
अन्योन्यापहृतं द्रव्यं विभक्ते यत्तु दृश्यते /
तत् पुनस्ते समैर् अंशैर् विभजेरन्निति स्थितिः //
255.m: Property concealed from one another that is discovered after partition / they should divide again among themselves in equal shares; this is the established rule.

255.s:
aputreṇa parakṣetre niyogotpāditaḥ sutaḥ /
ubhayorapyasāvṛkthī piṇḍadātā ca dharmataḥ //
255.d:
अपुत्रेण परक्षेत्रे नियोगोत्पादितः सुतः /
उभयोरप्यसावृक्थी पिण्डदाता च धर्मतः //
255.m: A son begotten through appointment (niyoga) by a sonless man upon another's wife / is lawfully an heir and an offerer of the funeral cake (piṇḍa) to both men.

255.s:
auraso dharmapatnījastatsamaḥ putrikāsutaḥ /
kṣetrajaḥ kṣetrajātastu sagotreṇetareṇa vā //
255.d:
औरसो धर्मपत्नीजस्तत्समः पुत्रिकासुतः /
क्षेत्रजः क्षेत्रजातस्तु सगोत्रेणेतरेण वा //
255.m: The son born of a lawful wife is the aurasa (body-born), and equal to him is the son of an appointed daughter; / the kṣetraja (field-born) is one begotten on the wife by a man of the same family or by another.

255.s:
gṛhe pracchanna utpanno gūḍhajastu sutaḥ smṛtaḥ /
kānīnaḥ kanyakājāto mātāmahasuto mataḥ //
255.d:
गृहे प्रच्छन्न उत्पन्नो गूढजस्तु सुतः स्मृतः /
कानीनः कन्यकाजातो मातामहसुतो मतः //
255.m: A son born secretly in the house is considered a gūḍhaja (secretly-born); / the kānīna (maiden-born) is born of an unmarried girl and is regarded as the son of the maternal grandfather.

255.s:
kṣatāyāmakṣatāyāṃ vā jātaḥ paunarbhavaḥ sutaḥ /
dadyānmātā pitā vā yaṃ sa putrī dattako bhavet //
:p 422
255.d:
क्षतायामक्षतायां वा जातः पौनर्भवः सुतः /
दद्यान्माता पिता वा यं स पुत्री दत्तको भवेत् //
:प् 422
255.m:
A son born of a woman whose marriage has or has not been consummated is a paunarbhava (son of a remarried woman); / he whom the mother or father gives becomes an adopted son (dattaka).
[Page 422]

255.s:
krītaś ca tābhyāṃ vikrītaḥ kṛtrimaḥ syāt svyaṃ kṛtaḥ /
dattātmā tu svayaṃ datto garbhe vittaḥ sahoḍhajaḥ //
255.d:
क्रीतश् च ताभ्यां विक्रीतः कृत्रिमः स्यात् स्व्यं कृतः /
दत्तात्मा तु स्वयं दत्तो गर्भे वित्तः सहोढजः //
255.m: A bought son (krīta) is one sold by both parents; an artificial son (kṛtrima) is one made by oneself; / a self-given son (dattātmā) is one who gives himself; one received while in the womb is a sahoḍhaja.

255.s:
utsṛṣṭo gṛhyate yastu sopaviddho bhavet sutaḥ /
piṇḍado 'ṃśaharaś caiṣāṃ pūrvābhāve paraḥ paraḥ //
255.d:
उत्सृष्टो गृह्यते यस्तु सोपविद्धो भवेत् सुतः /
पिण्डदो ऽंशहरश् चैषां पूर्वाभावे परः परः //
255.m: One who is abandoned and taken in becomes an apaviddha (cast-off) son; / each subsequent one among these offers the funeral cake and takes a share only in the absence of the preceding.

255.s:
sajātīyeṣvayaṃ proktastanayeṣu mayā vidhiḥ /
jāto 'pi dāsyāṃ śūdrasya kāmato 'ṃśaharo bhavet //
255.d:
सजातीयेष्वयं प्रोक्तस्तनयेषु मया विधिः /
जातो ऽपि दास्यां शूद्रस्य कामतो ऽंशहरो भवेत् //
255.m: This rule has been declared by me in respect of sons belonging to the same caste. / Even a son born to a Śūdra by a female slave may take a share at [the father's] pleasure.

255.s:
mṛte pitari kuryustaṃ bhrātarastvardhabhāgikaṃ /
abhrātṛko haret sarvaṃ duhitṝṇāṃ sutādṛte //
255.d:
मृते पितरि कुर्युस्तं भ्रातरस्त्वर्धभागिकं /
अभ्रातृको हरेत् सर्वं दुहितॄणां सुतादृते //
255.m: When the father is dead, the brothers should allot him half a share; / if he has no brothers, he may take the whole, except when there are sons of daughters.

255.s:
patnī duhitaraś caiva pitaro bhrātaras tathā /
tatsuto gotrajo bandhuḥ śiṣyaḥ sabrahmacāriṇaḥ //
255.d:
पत्नी दुहितरश् चैव पितरो भ्रातरस् तथा /
तत्सुतो गोत्रजो बन्धुः शिष्यः सब्रह्मचारिणः //
255.m: The wife, daughters, parents, brothers, / their sons, agnates (gotraja), cognates (bandhu), a pupil, and fellow students—

255.s:
eṣāmabhāve pūvasya dhanabhāguttarottaraḥ /
svaryātsya hy aputrasya sarvavarṇeṣvayaṃ vidhiḥ //
255.d:
एषामभावे पूवस्य धनभागुत्तरोत्तरः /
स्वर्यात्स्य ह्य् अपुत्रस्य सर्ववर्णेष्वयं विधिः //
255.m: in the absence of each preceding one, the next in order inherits the property / of a deceased man who has gone to heaven leaving no son; this is the rule for all castes.

255.s:
vānaprasthayatibrahmacāriṇāmṛkthabhāginaḥ /
krameṇācāryasacchiṣyadharmabhrātrekatīrthinaḥ //
255.d:
वानप्रस्थयतिब्रह्मचारिणामृक्थभागिनः /
क्रमेणाचार्यसच्छिष्यधर्मभ्रात्रेकतीर्थिनः //
255.m: The inheritors of the estate of a forest hermit (vānaprastha), an ascetic (yati), and a student (brahmacārin) / are, in order, the teacher, the virtuous pupil, and a spiritual brother belonging to the same hermitage.

255.s:
saṃsṛṣṭinastu saṃsṛṣṭī sodarasya tu sodaraḥ /
dadyāccāpahereccāṃśaṃ jātasya ca mṛtasya ca //
255.d:
संसृष्टिनस्तु संसृष्टी सोदरस्य तु सोदरः /
दद्याच्चापहेरेच्चांशं जातस्य च मृतस्य च //
255.m: A reunited coparcener belongs to a reunited coparcener, and a full brother to a full brother; / [a coparcener] should give a share to one born and take the share of one deceased.

255.s:
anyodaryastu saṃsṛṣṭī nānyodaryadhanaṃ haret /
asaṃsṛṣtyapi cādadyātsodaryo nānyamānṛjaḥ //
255.d:
अन्योदर्यस्तु संसृष्टी नान्योदर्यधनं हरेत् /
असंसृष्त्यपि चादद्यात्सोदर्यो नान्यमानृजः //
255.m: A half-brother who is reunited does not take the wealth of a half-brother; / even if unreunited, a full brother should take it, but not a son born of another mother.

255.s:
patitastatsutaḥ klīvaḥ paṅgurunmattako jaḍaḥ /
andho 'cikitsyarogādyā bhartavyāstu niraṃśakāḥ //
255.d:
पतितस्तत्सुतः क्लीवः पङ्गुरुन्मत्तको जडः /
अन्धो ऽचिकित्स्यरोगाद्या भर्तव्यास्तु निरंशकाः //
255.m: An outcaste and his son, a eunuch, a lame man, a madman, an idiot, / a blind man, and those afflicted with incurable diseases are shareless, but must be maintained.

255.s:
aurasāḥ kṣetrajāstveṣāṃ nirdoṣā bhāgahāriṇaḥ /
sutāś caiṣāṃ prabhartavyā yāvadvai bhartṛsātkṛtāḥ //
255.d:
औरसाः क्षेत्रजास्त्वेषां निर्दोषा भागहारिणः /
सुताश् चैषां प्रभर्तव्या यावद्वै भर्तृसात्कृताः //
255.m: However, their body-born (aurasa) and field-born (kṣetraja) sons who are free from defect are entitled to shares, / and their daughters must be maintained until they are given away to husbands.

255.s:
aputrā yoṣitaś caiṣāṃ bhartavyāḥ sādhuvṛttayaḥ /
:p 423
nirvāsyā vyabhicāriṇyaḥ pratikūlāstathaiva ca //
255.d:
अपुत्रा योषितश् चैषां भर्तव्याः साधुवृत्तयः /
:प् 423
निर्वास्या व्यभिचारिण्यः प्रतिकूलास्तथैव च //

255.s:
pitṛmātṛpatibhrātṛdattamadhyagnyupāgataṃ /
ādhivedanikuñcaiva strīdhanaṃ parikīrtitaṃ //
255.d:
पितृमातृपतिभ्रातृदत्तमध्यग्न्युपागतं /
आधिवेदनिकुञ्चैव स्त्रीधनं परिकीर्तितं //
255.m: What is given by father, mother, husband, or brother, what is received before the nuptial fire, / and the gift on supersession (ādhivedanika)—this is declared to be woman's property (strīdhana).

255.s:
bandhudattaṃ tathā śulkamanvādheyakameva ca /
aprajāyāmatītāyāṃ bāndhavāstadavāpnuyuḥ //
255.d:
बन्धुदत्तं तथा शुल्कमन्वाधेयकमेव च /
अप्रजायामतीतायां बान्धवास्तदवाप्नुयुः //
255.m: Likewise, a gift from relatives, the bride-price (śulka), and the post-marital gift (anvādheyaka)— / if she dies without offspring, her relatives shall obtain it.

255.s:
aprajāstrīdhanaṃ bhratturbrāhmyādiṣu caturṣvapi /
duhitṛṇāṃ prasūtā cecchreṣe tu pitṛgāmi tat //
255.d:
अप्रजास्त्रीधनं भ्रत्तुर्ब्राह्म्यादिषु चतुर्ष्वपि /
दुहितृणां प्रसूता चेच्छ्रेषे तु पितृगामि तत् //
255.m: The property of a woman dying without offspring goes to the husband in the first four forms of marriage beginning with Brāhma; / if she has offspring, it belongs to the daughters; in the remaining forms, it goes to the father.

255.s:
datvā kanyāṃ haran daṇḍyo vyayaṃ dadyācca sodayam /
mṛtāyāṃ dattamādadyāt pariśodhyobhayavyayam //
255.d:
दत्वा कन्यां हरन् दण्ड्यो व्ययं दद्याच्च सोदयम् /
मृतायां दत्तमादद्यात् परिशोध्योभयव्ययम् //
255.m: One who takes back a girl after giving her away should be punished and must pay the expenses with interest; / if she dies, he may take back what was given after deducting the expenses incurred by both sides.

255.s:
durbhikṣe dharmakārye ca vyādhau saṃpratirodhake /
gṛhītaṃ strīdhanaṃ bhartā na striye dātumarhati //
255.d:
दुर्भिक्षे धर्मकार्ये च व्याधौ संप्रतिरोधके /
गृहीतं स्त्रीधनं भर्ता न स्त्रिये दातुमर्हति //
255.m: In famine, for religious acts, in sickness, or during confinement under arrest, / a husband who has taken woman's property is not obliged to return it to the woman.

255.s:
adhivittastriyai dadyādadhivedanikaṃ samam /
na dattaṃ srīdhanaṃ yasyai datte tvardhaṃ prakīrtitam //
255.d:
अधिवित्तस्त्रियै दद्यादधिवेदनिकं समम् /
