न दत्तं स्रीधनं यस्यै दत्ते त्वर्धं प्रकीर्तितम् //
255.m: To a superseded wife, [the husband] should give an equal amount as the supersession compensation / if no woman's property was given to her; but if it was given, half of that amount is prescribed.

255.s:
vibhāganihnave jñātibandhusākṣyabhilekhitaiḥ /
vibhāgabhāvanā jñeyā gṛhakṣetraiś ca yautikaiḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe dāyavibhāgo nāma
pañcapañcāśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:p 424
:ś atha ṣaṭpañcāśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
sīmāvivādādinirṇayaḥ
255.d:
विभागनिह्नवे ज्ञातिबन्धुसाक्ष्यभिलेखितैः /
विभागभावना ज्ञेया गृहक्षेत्रैश् च यौतिकैः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे दायविभागो नाम
पञ्चपञ्चाशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:प् 424
:श् अथ षट्पञ्चाशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
सीमाविवादादिनिर्णयः
255.m:
When partition is denied, knowledge of partition is to be ascertained through kinsmen, relatives, witnesses, documents, / and separately held houses and lands.
Thus ends the two hundred and fifty-fifth chapter, entitled 'Partition of Inheritance', in the great Agni Purāṇa.
[Page 424]
Now begins the two hundred and fifty-sixth chapter:
Settlement of Boundary Disputes and Related Matters.

256.s:
agnir uvāca
sīmno vivāde kṣetrasya sāmantāḥ sthavirā gaṇāḥ /
gopāḥ sīmākṛṣāṇā ye sarve ca vanagocarāḥ //
256.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
सीम्नो विवादे क्षेत्रस्य सामन्ताः स्थविरा गणाः /
गोपाः सीमाकृषाणा ये सर्वे च वनगोचराः //
256.m: Agni said: / In a dispute over the boundary of a field, neighboring landholders, elderly men, corporations, / cowherds, cultivators working on the boundary, and all forest dwellers

256.s:
nayeyurete sīmānaṃ sthalāṅgāratuṣadrumaiḥ /
setuvalmīkanimnāsthicaityādyair upalakṣitām //
256.d:
नयेयुरेते सीमानं स्थलाङ्गारतुषद्रुमैः /
सेतुवल्मीकनिम्नास्थिचैत्याद्यैर् उपलक्षिताम् //
256.m: should trace the boundary marked out by mounds, charcoal, chaff, trees, / dikes, anthills, depressions, bones, sacred trees, and the like.

256.s:
sāmantā vā samaṃgrāmāś catvāro 'ṣṭau daśāpi vā(1) /
raktasragvasanāḥ sīmānnayeyuḥ kṣitidhāriṇaḥ //
256.d:
सामन्ता वा समंग्रामाश् चत्वारो ऽष्टौ दशापि वा(1) /
रक्तस्रग्वसनाः सीमान्नयेयुः क्षितिधारिणः //
256.m: Or the neighboring residents of the village—four, eight, or even ten— / wearing red garlands and garments, bearing earth, should determine the boundary.

256.s:
anṛte tu pṛthagdaṇḍyā rājñā madhyamasāhasam /
abhāve jñātṛcihnānāṃ rājā sīmnaḥ pravattakaḥ //
256.d:
अनृते तु पृथग्दण्ड्या राज्ञा मध्यमसाहसम् /
अभावे ज्ञातृचिह्नानां राजा सीम्नः प्रवत्तकः //
256.m: If they speak falsely, however, they are to be punished individually by the king with the middle fine for violence; / in the absence of witnesses and markers, the king shall establish the boundary.

256.s:
ārāmāyatanagrāmanipānodyānaveśmasu /
eṣa eva vidhirjñeyo varṣāmvupravaheṣu ca //
256.d:
आरामायतनग्रामनिपानोद्यानवेश्मसु /
एष एव विधिर्ज्ञेयो वर्षाम्वुप्रवहेषु च //
256.m: In disputes concerning groves, temples, villages, watering stations, pleasure gardens, houses, / and the courses of rainwater runoffs, this very same rule is to be observed.

256.s:
maryādāyāḥ prabhedeṣu kṣetrasya haraṇe tathā /
maryādāyāś ca daṇḍyāḥ syuradhamottamamadhyamāḥ //
256.d:
मर्यादायाः प्रभेदेषु क्षेत्रस्य हरणे तथा /
मर्यादायाश् च दण्ड्याः स्युरधमोत्तममध्यमाः //
256.m: In breaking boundary marks and likewise in seizing a field / or boundary, they should be fined the lowest, highest, and middle fines.

256.s:
na niṣedhyo 'lpabādhastu setuḥ kalyāṇakārakaḥ /
parabhūmiṃ haran kūpaḥ svalpakṣetro bahūdakaḥ //
256.d:
न निषेध्यो ऽल्पबाधस्तु सेतुः कल्याणकारकः /
परभूमिं हरन् कूपः स्वल्पक्षेत्रो बहूदकः //
256.m: A dam that causes little injury but brings welfare should not be prohibited, / nor a well encroaching on another's land that occupies little ground but yields abundant water.

256.s:
svāmine yo 'nivedyaiva kṣetre setuṃ prakalpayet /
utpanne svāmino bhogastadabhāve mahīpateḥ //
256.d:
स्वामिने यो ऽनिवेद्यैव क्षेत्रे सेतुं प्रकल्पयेत् /
उत्पन्ने स्वामिनो भोगस्तदभावे महीपतेः //
256.m: If someone builds a dam on a field without informing the owner, / when it yields produce, the enjoyment belongs to the owner; in his absence, to the king.

256.s:
phālāhatamapi kṣetraṃ yo na kuryānna kārayet /
:n
1 catvāro 'tha daśāpi veti kha.. , ga.. , ña.. ca
:p 425
sa pradāpyo 'kṛṣṭaphalaṃ kṣetramanyena kārayet //
256.d:
फालाहतमपि क्षेत्रं यो न कुर्यान्न कारयेत् /
:न्
1 चत्वारो ऽथ दशापि वेति ख.. , ग.. , ञ.. च
:प् 425
स प्रदाप्यो ऽकृष्टफलं क्षेत्रमन्येन कारयेत् //
256.m:
If a man neither cultivates nor causes to be cultivated a field that has even been touched by the plow,
[Note]
1. 'catvāro 'tha daśāpi vā' in manuscripts kha, ga, and ña. / [Page 425]
he should be made to pay the value of the unharvested produce, and the field should be caused to be tilled by another.

256.s:
māsānaṣṭau tu mahiṣī satyaghātasya kāriṇī /
daṇḍanīyā tadardhantu gaustadardhamajāvikaṃ //
256.d:
मासानष्टौ तु महिषी सत्यघातस्य कारिणी /
दण्डनीया तदर्धन्तु गौस्तदर्धमजाविकं //
256.m: A female buffalo destroying standing crops should be fined eight māṣas; / a cow half of that; and a goat or sheep half of that again.

256.s:
bhakṣayitvopaviṣṭānāṃ yathoktād dviguṇo damaḥ /
samameṣāṃ vivītepi svarāṣṭraṃ mahiṣīsamam //
256.d:
भक्षयित्वोपविष्टानां यथोक्ताद् द्विगुणो दमः /
सममेषां विवीतेपि स्वराष्ट्रं महिषीसमम् //
256.m: For animals that sit down after eating, the fine is twice what has been stated; / the fine is the same for them in an enclosed pasture; an ass or a camel is treated like a female buffalo.

256.s:
yāvat satyaṃ vinaṣṭantu tāvat kṣetrī phalaṃ labhet /
pālastāḍyo 'tha gosvāmī pūrvoktaṃ daṇḍamarhati //
256.d:
यावत् सत्यं विनष्टन्तु तावत् क्षेत्री फलं लभेत् /
पालस्ताड्यो ऽथ गोस्वामी पूर्वोक्तं दण्डमर्हति //
256.m: The field owner should receive produce equal to the crop that was destroyed; / the herdsman should be flogged, while the owner of the cattle deserves the aforementioned fine.

256.s:
pathi grāmavivītānte kṣetre doṣo na vidyate /
akāmataḥ kāmacāre cauravaddaṇḍamarhati //
256.d:
पथि ग्रामविवीतान्ते क्षेत्रे दोषो न विद्यते /
अकामतः कामचारे चौरवद्दण्डमर्हति //
256.m: No fault attaches to damage on a path, near a village, or at the edge of pastureland / done unintentionally; but if wandering at will, [the owner] deserves punishment like a thief.

256.s:
mahotkṣotsṛṣṭapaśavaḥ sūtikāgantukā ca gauḥ /
pālo yeṣāntu mocyā daivarājapariplutāḥ //
256.d:
महोत्क्षोत्सृष्टपशवः सूतिकागन्तुका च गौः /
पालो येषान्तु मोच्या दैवराजपरिप्लुताः //
256.m: A breeding bull, dedicated cattle, a cow recently calved, a stray animal, / and those afflicted by an act of God or the king are to be released, even if they have a keeper.

256.s:
yathārpitān paśūn gopoḥ sāyaṃ pratyarpayettathā /
pramādamṛtanaṣṭāṃś ca pradāpyaḥ kṛtavetanaḥ //
256.d:
यथार्पितान् पशून् गोपोः सायं प्रत्यर्पयेत्तथा /
प्रमादमृतनष्टांश् च प्रदाप्यः कृतवेतनः //
256.m: A cowherd must return the cattle in the evening just as they were entrusted to him; / if any die or are lost through his negligence, he who receives wages must be made to replace them.

256.s:
pāladoṣavināśe tu pāle daṇḍo vidhīyate /
ardhatrayodaśapaṇaḥ svāmino dravyameva ca //
256.d:
पालदोषविनाशे तु पाले दण्डो विधीयते /
अर्धत्रयोदशपणः स्वामिनो द्रव्यमेव च //
256.m: If loss occurs through the keeper's fault, a fine is prescribed for the keeper / amounting to twelve and a half paṇas, and he must restore the animal itself to the owner.

256.s:
grāmecchayā gopracāro bhūmirājavaśena vā /
dvijastṛṇaidhaḥpuṣpāṇi sarvataḥ svavadāharet //
256.d:
ग्रामेच्छया गोप्रचारो भूमिराजवशेन वा /
द्विजस्तृणैधःपुष्पाणि सर्वतः स्ववदाहरेत् //
256.m: Pastureland for cows depends on the wish of the village or the authority of the king. / A twice-born man may take grass, firewood, and flowers from anywhere as if they were his own.

256.s:
dhanuḥśataṃ parīṇāho grāmakṣetrāntaraṃ bhavet /
dve śate kharvaṭasya syānnagarasya catuḥśatam //
256.d:
धनुःशतं परीणाहो ग्रामक्षेत्रान्तरं भवेत् /
द्वे शते खर्वटस्य स्यान्नगरस्य चतुःशतम् //
256.m: The intervening space between a village and fields should be an extent of one hundred bows; / it should be two hundred bows for a market town (kharvaṭa), and four hundred for a city.

256.s:
svaṃ labhetānyavikrītaṃ kreturdoṣo 'prakāśite /
hīnādraho hīnamūlye velāhīne ca taskaraḥ //
256.d:
स्वं लभेतान्यविक्रीतं क्रेतुर्दोषो ऽप्रकाशिते /
हीनाद्रहो हीनमूल्ये वेलाहीने च तस्करः //
256.m: One may recover one's property sold by another; fault attaches to the buyer in a secret purchase: / from a disreputable person, in secret, at an inadequate price, or at an unseasonable time, he is deemed a thief.

256.s:
naṣṭāpahṛtamāsādya hartāraṃ grāhayennaram /
deśakālātipattau vā gṛhītvā svayamarpayet //
:p 426
256.d:
नष्टापहृतमासाद्य हर्तारं ग्राहयेन्नरम् /
देशकालातिपत्तौ वा गृहीत्वा स्वयमर्पयेत् //
:प् 426
256.m:
Having found lost or stolen property, a man should cause the thief to be arrested; / or, if prevented by considerations of place and time, he may seize him himself and deliver him.
[Page 426]

256.s:
vikreturdarśanācchuddhiḥ svāmī dravyaṃ nṛpo damam /
kretā mūlyaṃ samāpnoti tasmādyastatra vikrayī //
256.d:
विक्रेतुर्दर्शनाच्छुद्धिः स्वामी द्रव्यं नृपो दमम् /
क्रेता मूल्यं समाप्नोति तस्माद्यस्तत्र विक्रयी //
256.m: By producing the seller, the buyer's clearance is effected; the owner recovers his property, and the king [imposes] a fine. / The buyer receives back his purchase price from whoever was the seller there.

256.s:
āgamenopabhogena naṣṭaṃ bhāvyamato 'nyathā /
pañcabandho damastasya rājñe tenāpyabhāvite //
256.d:
आगमेनोपभोगेन नष्टं भाव्यमतो ऽन्यथा /
पञ्चबन्धो दमस्तस्य राज्ञे तेनाप्यभाविते //
256.m: Lost property must be established through legal acquisition and enjoyment; otherwise, / if it is not so established, he incurs a fine of one-fifth to the king.

256.s:
hṛtaṃ pranaṣṭaṃ yo dravyaṃ parahastādavāpnuyāt /
anivedya nṛpe daṇḍyaḥ sa tu ṣannayatiṃ paṇān //
256.d:
हृतं प्रनष्टं यो द्रव्यं परहस्तादवाप्नुयात् /
अनिवेद्य नृपे दण्ड्यः स तु षन्नयतिं पणान् //
256.m: One who recovers lost or stolen property from another's hand / without reporting it to the king, however, should be fined ninety-six paṇas.

256.s:
śaulkikaiḥ sthānapālair vā naṣṭāpahṛtamāhṛtaṃ /
arvāk saṃvatsarāt svāmī labhate parato nṛpaḥ //
256.d:
शौल्किकैः स्थानपालैर् वा नष्टापहृतमाहृतं /
अर्वाक् संवत्सरात् स्वामी लभते परतो नृपः //
256.m: Lost or stolen property brought in by toll-collectors or guards of the post, / the owner receives within a year; after that, it belongs to the king.

256.s:
paṇānekaśaphe dadyāccaturaḥ pañca mānuṣe /
mahiṣoṣṭragavāṃ dvau dvau pādaṃ pādamajāvike //
256.d:
पणानेकशफे दद्याच्चतुरः पञ्च मानुषे /
महिषोष्ट्रगवां द्वौ द्वौ पादं पादमजाविके //
256.m: He should give [as salvage fee] four paṇas for a single-hoofed animal, five for a human, / two each for buffaloes, camels, and cattle, and a quarter of a paṇa each for goats and sheep.

256.s:
svakuṭumbāvirodhena deyaṃ dārasutādṛte /
nānvaye sati sarvasvaṃ deyaṃ yaccānyasaṃśrutam //
256.d:
स्वकुटुम्बाविरोधेन देयं दारसुतादृते /
नान्वये सति सर्वस्वं देयं यच्चान्यसंश्रुतम् //
256.m: A gift may be made without detriment to one's family, excluding wife and son; / when lineage exists, one's entire property may not be given, nor what has been promised to another.

256.s:
pratigrahaḥ prakāśaḥ syāt sthāvarasya viśeṣataḥ /
deyaṃ pratiśrutañcaiva datvā nāpaharet punaḥ //
256.d:
प्रतिग्रहः प्रकाशः स्यात् स्थावरस्य विशेषतः /
देयं प्रतिश्रुतञ्चैव दत्वा नापहरेत् पुनः //
256.m: Acceptance should be public, especially of immovable property; / what has been promised must indeed be given, and once given, one may not take it back.

256.s:
daśaikapañcasaptāhamāsatryahārdhamāsikaṃ /
vījāyovāhyaratnastrīdohyapuṃsāṃ pratīkṣaṇam //
256.d:
दशैकपञ्चसप्ताहमासत्र्यहार्धमासिकं /
वीजायोवाह्यरत्नस्त्रीदोह्यपुंसां प्रतीक्षणम् //
256.m: The trial period for seeds, iron, beasts of burden, gems, female slaves, / milch cattle, and male slaves is ten days, one day, five, seven, a month, three days, and half a month respectively.

256.s:
agnau suvarṇamakṣīṇaṃ dvipalaṃ rajate śate /
aṣṭau trapuṇi sīse ca tāmre pañcadaśāyasi //
256.d:
अग्नौ सुवर्णमक्षीणं द्विपलं रजते शते /
अष्टौ त्रपुणि सीसे च ताम्रे पञ्चदशायसि //
256.m: Gold suffers no loss in fire; on a hundred [palas] of silver, [loss is] two palas; / on tin and lead, eight; on copper, five; and on iron, ten.

256.s:
śate daśapalāvṛddhiraurṇe kārpāsike tathā /
madhye pañcapalā jñeyā sūkṣme tu tripalā matā //
256.d:
शते दशपलावृद्धिरौर्णे कार्पासिके तथा /
मध्ये पञ्चपला ज्ञेया सूक्ष्मे तु त्रिपला मता //
256.m: An increase of ten palas per hundred is recognized for wool and cotton; / for medium cloth, it should be known as five palas; but for fine, it is considered three palas.

256.s:
kārmike romabaddhe ca triṃśadbhāgaḥ kṣayo mataḥ /
na kṣayo na ca vṛddhistu kauśeye valkaleṣu ca //
256.d:
कार्मिके रोमबद्धे च त्रिंशद्भागः क्षयो मतः /
न क्षयो न च वृद्धिस्तु कौशेये वल्कलेषु च //
256.m: For embroidered cloth and that interwoven with fur, a loss of a thirtieth part is recognized; / but for silk and bark garments there is neither loss nor increase.

256.s:
deśaṃ kālañca bhogañca jñātvā naṣṭe balābalam /
:p 427
dravyāṇāṃ kuśalā brūyuryattaddāpyamasaṃśayam //
256.d:
देशं कालञ्च भोगञ्च ज्ञात्वा नष्टे बलाबलम् /
:प् 427
द्रव्याणां कुशला ब्रूयुर्यत्तद्दाप्यमसंशयम् //
256.m:
Knowing the place, time, and wear, as well as the relative strength in case of destruction,
:p 427
experts in materials shall declare what compensation must be paid beyond doubt.

256.s:
balāddāsīkṛtaś caurair vikrītaścāpi mucyate /
svāmiprāṇaprado bhaktatyāgāttanniṣkrayādapi //
256.d:
बलाद्दासीकृतश् चौरैर् विक्रीतश्चापि मुच्यते /
स्वामिप्राणप्रदो भक्तत्यागात्तन्निष्क्रयादपि //
256.m: One enslaved by force or sold by thieves is released, / as also one who saves his master's life, by relinquishing his maintenance, or through ransom.

256.s:
pravrajyāvasito rājño dāsa āmaraṇāntikaḥ /
varṇānāmānulomyena dāsyaṃ na pratilomataḥ //
256.d:
प्रव्रज्यावसितो राज्ञो दास आमरणान्तिकः /
वर्णानामानुलोम्येन दास्यं न प्रतिलोमतः //
256.m: An apostate from asceticism becomes the king's slave until death; / slavery proceeds in the direct order of the castes, never in the reverse order.

256.s:
kṛtaśilpopi nivaset kṛtakālaṃ gurorgṛhe /
antevāsī guruprāptabhojanastratphalaptadaḥ //
256.d:
कृतशिल्पोपि निवसेत् कृतकालं गुरोर्गृहे /
अन्तेवासी गुरुप्राप्तभोजनस्त्रत्फलप्तदः //
256.m: An apprentice, even having acquired his craft, shall dwell in his teacher's house for the agreed time; / receiving his food from the teacher, he shall deliver the fruit [of his work] there.

256.s:
rājā kṛtvā pure sthānaṃ brāhmaṇānnyasya tatra tu /
traividyaṃ vṛttimadbrūyāt svadharmaḥ pālyatāmiti //
256.d:
राजा कृत्वा पुरे स्थानं ब्राह्मणान्न्यस्य तत्र तु /
त्रैविद्यं वृत्तिमद्ब्रूयात् स्वधर्मः पाल्यतामिति //
256.m: The king, having established a settlement in the city and settled brāhmaṇas there, / endowed with livelihoods and proficient in the three Vedas, should declare: "Let your own duty be maintained."

256.s:
nijadharmāvirodhena yastu sāmayiko bhavet /
so 'pi yatnena saṃrakṣyo dharmo rājakṛtaś ca yaḥ //
256.d:
निजधर्माविरोधेन यस्तु सामयिको भवेत् /
सो ऽपि यत्नेन संरक्ष्यो धर्मो राजकृतश् च यः //
256.m: Whatever conventional rule exists that does not conflict with one's own duty, / that too must be zealously guarded, as also any decree established by the king.

256.s:
gaṇadravyaṃ haredyastu saṃvidaṃ laṅghayecca yaḥ /
sarvasvaharaṇaṃ kṛtvā taṃ rāṣṭrādvipravāsayet //
256.d:
गणद्रव्यं हरेद्यस्तु संविदं लङ्घयेच्च यः /
सर्वस्वहरणं कृत्वा तं राष्ट्राद्विप्रवासयेत् //
256.m: He who steals the property of a corporation or violates an agreement / should be banished from the realm after confiscating all his property.

256.s:
kartavyaṃ vacanaṃ sarvaiḥ samūhahitavādibhiḥ /
yastatra viparītaḥ syātsa dāpyaḥ prathamaṃ damam //
256.d:
कर्तव्यं वचनं सर्वैः समूहहितवादिभिः /
यस्तत्र विपरीतः स्यात्स दाप्यः प्रथमं दमम् //
256.m: The word of those who speak for the welfare of the assembly must be obeyed by all; / he who acts contrary thereto should be made to pay the first fine.

256.s:
samūhakāryaprahito yallabhettattadarpayet /
ekādaśaguṇaṃ dāpyo yadyasau nārpayet svayam //
256.d:
समूहकार्यप्रहितो यल्लभेत्तत्तदर्पयेत् /
एकादशगुणं दाप्यो यद्यसौ नार्पयेत् स्वयम् //
256.m: One dispatched on the business of the assembly shall surrender whatever he acquires; / if he does not surrender it himself, he should be made to pay eleven times as much.

256.s:
vedajñāḥ śucayo 'lubdhā bhaveyuḥ kāryacintakāḥ /
kartavyaṃ vacanaṃ teṣāṃ samūhahitavādināṃ //
256.d:
वेदज्ञाः शुचयो ऽलुब्धा भवेयुः कार्यचिन्तकाः /
कर्तव्यं वचनं तेषां समूहहितवादिनां //
256.m: Those who manage affairs should be knowers of the Vedas, pure, and free from greed; / the word of these who speak for the welfare of the assembly must be obeyed.

256.s:
śreṇinaigamapākhaṇḍigaṇānāmapyayaṃ vidhiḥ /
bhedañcaiṣāṃ nṛpo rakṣet pūrvavṛttiñca pālayet //
256.d:
श्रेणिनैगमपाखण्डिगणानामप्ययं विधिः /
भेदञ्चैषां नृपो रक्षेत् पूर्ववृत्तिञ्च पालयेत् //
256.m: This rule also applies to guilds, mercantile associations, heterodox sects, and corporations; / the king should prevent dissension among them and protect their previous customs.

256.s:
gṛhītavetanaḥ karma tyajan dviguṇamāvahet /
agṛhīte samaṃ dāpyo bhṛtyai rakṣya upaskaraḥ //
:p 428
256.d:
गृहीतवेतनः कर्म त्यजन् द्विगुणमावहेत् /
अगृहीते समं दाप्यो भृत्यै रक्ष्य उपस्करः //
:प् 428
256.m:
A laborer who has received his wages and abandons the work shall pay twice as much; / if he has not received wages, he should be made to pay an equal amount; implements must be protected by the servants.
:p 428

256.s:
dāpyastu daśamaṃ bhāgaṃ bāṇijyapaśusasyataḥ /
aniścitya bhṛtiṃ yastu kārayetsa mahīkṣitā //
256.d:
दाप्यस्तु दशमं भागं बाणिज्यपशुसस्यतः /
अनिश्चित्य भृतिं यस्तु कारयेत्स महीक्षिता //
256.m: One who employs a worker without fixing the wages, however, / should be made by the king to pay a tenth part of the trade, cattle, or crops.

256.s:
deśaṃ kālañca yo 'tīyāt karma kuryācca yo 'nyathā /
tatra tu svāminaśchando 'dhikaṃ deyaṃ kṛte 'dhike //
256.d:
देशं कालञ्च यो ऽतीयात् कर्म कुर्याच्च यो ऽन्यथा /
तत्र तु स्वामिनश्छन्दो ऽधिकं देयं कृते ऽधिके //
256.m: If someone exceeds the place and time, or performs the work differently, / the master's choice prevails there; more must be given if more work has been done.

256.s:
yo yāvat kurute karma tāvattasya tu vetanam /
ubhayorapyasādhyañcet sādhye kuryādyathāśrutam //
256.d:
यो यावत् कुरुते कर्म तावत्तस्य तु वेतनम् /
उभयोरप्यसाध्यञ्चेत् साध्ये कुर्याद्यथाश्रुतम् //
256.m: Whoever performs work, his wage is commensurate with that much; / if it becomes impossible for both, he should perform what is possible as agreed.

256.s:
arājadaivikannaṣṭaṃ bhāṇḍaṃ dāpyastu vāhakaḥ /
prasthānavighnakṛccaiva pradāpyo dviguṇāṃ bhṛtim //
256.d:
अराजदैविकन्नष्टं भाण्डं दाप्यस्तु वाहकः /
प्रस्थानविघ्नकृच्चैव प्रदाप्यो द्विगुणां भृतिम् //
256.m: A carrier must make good any merchandise lost through causes other than the king or an act of god; / and one who creates an obstacle at the departure must be made to pay double wages.

256.s:
prakrānte saptamaṃ bhāgaṃ caturthaṃ pathi saṃtyajan /
bhṛtimardhapathe sarvāṃ pradāpyastyājakoapi ca //
256.d:
प्रक्रान्ते सप्तमं भागं चतुर्थं पथि संत्यजन् /
भृतिमर्धपथे सर्वां प्रदाप्यस्त्याजकोअपि च //
256.m: One who abandons [the load] at departure shall forfeit a seventh part; along the road, a fourth; / and at the midway point, the whole wage; one who dismisses the carrier must also be made to pay [similarly].

256.s:
glahe śatikavṛddhestu sabhikaḥ pañcakaṃ gataṃ /
gṛhṇīyāddhūrtakitavāditarāddaśakaṃ śataṃ //
256.d:
ग्लहे शतिकवृद्धेस्तु सभिकः पञ्चकं गतं /
गृह्णीयाद्धूर्तकितवादितराद्दशकं शतं //
256.m: On a stake with an increase of a hundred, the keeper of the gambling house may take / five percent from a cunning gambler, and ten percent from another.

256.s:
sa samyakpālito dadyādrājñe bhāgaṃ yathākṛtaṃ /
jitamudgrāhayejjetre dadyātsatyaṃ vacaḥ kṣamī //
256.d:
स सम्यक्पालितो दद्याद्राज्ञे भागं यथाकृतं /
जितमुद्ग्राहयेज्जेत्रे दद्यात्सत्यं वचः क्षमी //
256.m: Protected properly, he should give to the king the share as fixed; / being patient, he should collect the winnings for the winner and speak true words.

256.s:
prāpte nṛpatinā bhāge prasiddhe dhūrtamaṇḍale /
jitaṃ saśabhike sthāne dāpayedanyathā na tu //
256.d:
प्राप्ते नृपतिना भागे प्रसिद्धे धूर्तमण्डले /
जितं सशभिके स्थाने दापयेदन्यथा न तु //
256.m: When the king's share has been received in a recognized circle of gamblers, / he should cause payment of the winnings in a place provided with a gambling house keeper, not otherwise.

256.s:
draṣṭāro vyavahārāṇāṃ sākṣiṇaś ca ta eva hi /
rājñā sacihnā nirvāsyāḥ kūṭākṣopadhidevinaḥ //
256.d:
द्रष्टारो व्यवहाराणां साक्षिणश् च त एव हि /
राज्ञा सचिह्ना निर्वास्याः कूटाक्षोपधिदेविनः //
256.m: They alone are the judges of disputes and the witnesses; / those who gamble with false dice or trickery should be branded and banished by the king.

256.s:
dyūtamekamukhaṃ kāryaṃ taskarajñānakāraṇāt /
eṣa eva vidhirjñeyaḥ prāṇidyūte samāhvaye //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe sīmāvivādādinirṇayo nāma
ṣaṭpañcāśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:p 429
:ś atha saptapañcāśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
vākpāruṣyādiprakaraṇam
256.d:
द्यूतमेकमुखं कार्यं तस्करज्ञानकारणात् /
एष एव विधिर्ज्ञेयः प्राणिद्यूते समाह्वये //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे सीमाविवादादिनिर्णयो नाम
षट्पञ्चाशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:प् 429
:श् अथ सप्तपञ्चाशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
वाक्पारुष्यादिप्रकरणम्
256.m:
Gambling should be centralized under one authority for the purpose of identifying thieves; / this very same rule is to be understood in the betting on living creatures.
Thus in the Great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and fifty-sixth chapter, entitled "The Adjudication of Boundary Disputes and Other Matters."
:p 429
Now, the two hundred and fifty-seventh chapter:
The Section on Verbal Abuse and Related Matters.

257.s:
agnir uvāca
satyāsatyānyathā stotrair nyūnāṅgendriyarogiṇāṃ /
kṣepaṃ karoti ceddaṇḍyaḥ paṇānardhatrayodaśa //
257.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
सत्यासत्यान्यथा स्तोत्रैर् न्यूनाङ्गेन्द्रियरोगिणां /
क्षेपं करोति चेद्दण्ड्यः पणानर्धत्रयोदश //
257.m: Agni said: / If one insults those defective in limbs, senses, or suffering from diseases, / whether by true, false, or ironical statements, he is punishable with twelve and a half paṇas.

257.s:
abhigantāsmi bhaginīmmātaraṃ vā taveti ca /
śapantaṃ dāpayedrājā pañcaviṃśatikaṃ damaṃ //
257.d:
अभिगन्तास्मि भगिनीम्मातरं वा तवेति च /
शपन्तं दापयेद्राजा पञ्चविंशतिकं दमं //
257.m: And if one swears, "I will violate your sister or your mother," / the king should make him pay a fine of twenty-five [paṇas].

257.s:
ardho 'dhameṣu dviguṇaḥ parastrīṣūttameṣu ca /
daṇḍapraṇayanaṃ kāryaṃ varṇajātyuttarādharaiḥ //
257.d:
अर्धो ऽधमेषु द्विगुणः परस्त्रीषूत्तमेषु च /
दण्डप्रणयनं कार्यं वर्णजात्युत्तराधरैः //
257.m: Half [is the fine] against low persons, double against others' wives and superior persons; / the infliction of punishment should be carried out according to the higher and lower status of castes and classes.

257.s:
prātilomyāpavādeṣu dviguṇatriguṇā damāḥ /
varṇānāmānulomyena tasmādevārdhahānitaḥ //
257.d:
प्रातिलोम्यापवादेषु द्विगुणत्रिगुणा दमाः /
वर्णानामानुलोम्येन तस्मादेवार्धहानितः //
257.m: In defaming against the social order, fines are double and triple; / in the regular order of castes, [they decrease] by half reductions accordingly.

257.s:
vāhugrīvānetrasakthivināśe vācike damaḥ /
śatyastato 'rdhikaḥ pādanāsākarṇikarādiṣu //
257.d:
वाहुग्रीवानेत्रसक्थिविनाशे वाचिके दमः /
शत्यस्ततो ऽर्धिकः पादनासाकर्णिकरादिषु //
257.m: For verbal threat of destroying an arm, neck, eye, or thigh, the fine is / one hundred [paṇas]; half of that in the case of a foot, nose, ear, hand, and so forth.

257.s:
aśaktastu vadannevandaṇḍanīyaḥ paṇān daśa /
tathā śaktaḥ pratibhuvaṃ dadyāt kṣemāya tasya tu(1) //
257.d:
अशक्तस्तु वदन्नेवन्दण्डनीयः पणान् दश /
तथा शक्तः प्रतिभुवं दद्यात् क्षेमाय तस्य तु(1) //
257.m: If incapable [of doing so], one saying such should be fined ten paṇas; / but if capable, he should give a surety for the other's safety.

257.s:
patanīyakṛte kṣepe daṇḍī madhyamasāhasaḥ /
upapātakayukte tu dāpyaḥ prathamasāhasaṃ //
257.d:
पतनीयकृते क्षेपे दण्डी मध्यमसाहसः /
उपपातकयुक्ते तु दाप्यः प्रथमसाहसं //
257.m: For an insult charging a sin causing fall from caste, he incurs the middle fine for violence; / but for one involving a minor sin, he should be made to pay the first fine for violence.

257.s:
traividyanṛpadevānāṃ kṣepa uttamasāhasaḥ /
:n
1 dadyādityatra dāpya iti pāṭho bhavituṃ yuktaḥ
:p 430
madhyamo jñātipūgānāṃ prathamo grāmadeśayoḥ //
257.d:
त्रैविद्यनृपदेवानां क्षेप उत्तमसाहसः /
:न्
1 दद्यादित्यत्र दाप्य इति पाठो भवितुं युक्तः
:प् 430
मध्यमो ज्ञातिपूगानां प्रथमो ग्रामदेशयोः //
257.m:
Insulting those versed in the three Vedas, the king, or the gods warrants the highest fine for violence;
:n
1. In place of dadyāt ("should give"), dāpyaḥ ("should be made to give") seems to be the proper reading. / :p 430
[the fine is] the middle one against kinsmen and caste corporations, and the first against a village or a country.

257.s:
asākṣikahate cihnair yuktibhinnāgamena ca /
draṣṭavyo vyavahārastu kūṭacihnakṛtādbhayāt //
257.d:
असाक्षिकहते चिह्नैर् युक्तिभिन्नागमेन च /
द्रष्टव्यो व्यवहारस्तु कूटचिह्नकृताद्भयात् //
257.m: In a case of battery without witnesses, the suit must be investigated / through signs, circumstantial evidence, and legal title, out of fear of forged marks.

257.s:
bhasmapaṅkarajaḥsparśe daṇḍo daśapaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ /
amedhyapārṣṇiniṣṭhyūtasparśane dviguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ //
257.d:
भस्मपङ्करजःस्पर्शे दण्डो दशपणः स्मृतः /
अमेध्यपार्ष्णिनिष्ठ्यूतस्पर्शने द्विगुणः स्मृतः //
257.m: For touching with ashes, mud, or dust, the fine is declared to be ten paṇas; / for touching with unholy substances, the heel, or spittle, it is declared to be double.

257.s:
sameṣvevaṃ parastrīṣu dviguṇastūttameṣu ca /
hīneṣvardhaṃ damo mohamadādibhiradaṇḍanam //
257.d:
समेष्वेवं परस्त्रीषु द्विगुणस्तूत्तमेषु च /
हीनेष्वर्धं दमो मोहमदादिभिरदण्डनम् //
257.m: Such is the rule among equals; it is double against another's wife and superiors, / and half the fine against inferiors; there is no punishment if done through delusion, intoxication, and the like.

257.s:
viprapīḍākaraṃ cchedyamaṅgamabrāhmaṇasya tu /
udgūrṇe prathamo daṇḍaḥ saṃsparśe tu tadardhikaḥ //
257.d:
विप्रपीडाकरं च्छेद्यमङ्गमब्राह्मणस्य तु /
उद्गूर्णे प्रथमो दण्डः संस्पर्शे तु तदर्धिकः //
257.m: The limb of a non-brāhmaṇa that causes injury to a brāhmaṇa should be cut off; / for raising a weapon, the first fine [is prescribed]; but for mere touch, half of that.

257.s:
udgūrṇe hastapāde tu daśaviṃśatikau damau /
parasparantu sarveṣāṃ śāstre madhyamasāhasaḥ //
257.d:
उद्गूर्णे हस्तपादे तु दशविंशतिकौ दमौ /
परस्परन्तु सर्वेषां शास्त्रे मध्यमसाहसः //
257.m: When a hand or a foot is raised [to strike], the fines are ten and twenty [paṇas] respectively; / but among all of them, the middle degree of violence [fine is imposed] for [raising] a weapon.

257.s:
pādakeśāṃśukakarolluñcaneṣu paṇān daśa /
pīḍākarṣāṃ śukāveṣṭapādādhyāse śatandamaḥ //
257.d:
पादकेशांशुककरोल्लुञ्चनेषु पणान् दश /
पीडाकर्षां शुकावेष्टपादाध्यासे शतन्दमः //
257.m: For pulling a foot, hair, clothing, or a hand, ten paṇas [is the fine]; / for inflicting pain by pulling, binding with cloth, or treading on [another’s] foot, the fine is one hundred.

257.s:
śoṇitena vinā duḥsvaṅkurvan kāṣṭhādibhirnaraḥ /
dvātriṃśataṃ paṇān(1) dāpyo dviguṇaṃ darśane 'sṛjaḥ //
257.d:
शोणितेन विना दुःस्वङ्कुर्वन् काष्ठादिभिर्नरः /
द्वात्रिंशतं पणान्(1) दाप्यो द्विगुणं दर्शने ऽसृजः //
257.m: A man causing pain without [shedding] blood by means of wood and the like / must be made to pay thirty-two paṇas, and double that if blood is seen.

257.s:
karapādadato bhaṅge cchedane karṇanāsayoḥ /
madhyo daṇḍo vraṇodbhede mṛtakalpahate tathā //
257.d:
करपाददतो भङ्गे च्छेदने कर्णनासयोः /
मध्यो दण्डो व्रणोद्भेदे मृतकल्पहते तथा //
257.m: In breaking a hand, a foot, or a tooth, in cutting off ears or the nose, / the fine is the middle one; likewise in opening an [healed] ulcer, and in beating [someone] almost to death.

257.s:
ceṣṭābhojanavāgrodhe netrādipratibhedane /
kandharābāhusakthyāñca bhaṅge madhyamasāhasaḥ //
257.d:
चेष्टाभोजनवाग्रोधे नेत्रादिप्रतिभेदने /
कन्धराबाहुसक्थ्याञ्च भङ्गे मध्यमसाहसः //
257.m: For obstructing movement, eating, or speech, for piercing an eye and the like, / and for breaking the neck, an arm, or a thigh, the middle degree of violence [fine is imposed].

257.s:
ekaṃ ghnatāṃ bahūnāñca yathoktāddviguṇā damāḥ /
kalahāpahṛtaṃ deyaṃ daṇḍastu dviguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ //
257.d:
एकं घ्नतां बहूनाञ्च यथोक्ताद्द्विगुणा दमाः /
कलहापहृतं देयं दण्डस्तु द्विगुणः स्मृतः //
257.m: For many [persons] beating a single [person], the fines are double those stated; / that which was snatched away in the brawl must be restored, and the fine is recorded as double [the value].

257.s:
duḥkhamutpādayedyastu sa samutthānajaṃ vyayam /
:n
1 dvāviṃśatipaṇāmiti kha..
:p 431
dāpyo daṇḍañca yo yasmin kalahe samudāhṛtaḥ //
257.d:
दुःखमुत्पादयेद्यस्तु स समुत्थानजं व्ययम् /
:न्
1 द्वाविंशतिपणामिति ख..
:प् 431
दाप्यो दण्डञ्च यो यस्मिन् कलहे समुदाहृतः //
257.m:
Whoever causes injury must [pay] the expense arising from recovery,
[Footnote]
1. Manuscript Kha reads: “twenty-two paṇas”. / [Page 431]
and he must be made to pay the fine that is declared for that respective assault.

257.s:
tarikaḥ sthalajaṃ śulkaṃ gṛhnan daṇḍyaḥ paṇāndaśa /
brāhmaṇaprātiveśyānāmetadevānimantraṇe //
257.d:
तरिकः स्थलजं शुल्कं गृह्नन् दण्ड्यः पणान्दश /
ब्राह्मणप्रातिवेश्यानामेतदेवानिमन्त्रणे //
257.m: A ferryman who collects land-tax is to be fined ten paṇas; / this same [fine is prescribed] for not inviting brāhmaṇa neighbours.

257.s:
abhighāte tathā bhede cchede buddhyāvapātane /
paṇāndāpyaḥ pañcadaśaviṃśatiṃ tattrayantathā //
257.d:
अभिघाते तथा भेदे च्छेदे बुद्ध्यावपातने /
पणान्दाप्यः पञ्चदशविंशतिं तत्त्रयन्तथा //
257.m: For striking, piercing, cutting, and intentionally felling [trees], / he should be made to pay paṇas: fifteen, twenty, and then those two combined [i.e. thirty-five], respectively.

257.s:
duḥsvotpādigṛhe dravyaṃ kṣipan prāṇaharaṃ tathā /
ṣāḍaśādyaṃ paṇāt dāpyo dvitīyo madhyamandamam //
257.d:
दुःस्वोत्पादिगृहे द्रव्यं क्षिपन् प्राणहरं तथा /
षाडशाद्यं पणात् दाप्यो द्वितीयो मध्यमन्दमम् //
257.m: One who throws into [another’s] house a substance causing distress, or likewise one that takes life, / should be made to pay sixteen paṇas for the first; for the second, the middle fine.

257.s:
duḥkhe ca śoṇitotpāde śākhāṅgacchedane tathā /
daṇḍaḥ kṣudrapaśūnāṃ syāddvipaṇaprabhṛtiḥ kramāt //
257.d:
दुःखे च शोणितोत्पादे शाखाङ्गच्छेदने तथा /
दण्डः क्षुद्रपशूनां स्याद्द्विपणप्रभृतिः क्रमात् //
257.m: In inflicting pain, causing blood to flow, and cutting off limbs or branches / of small animals, the fine should begin with two paṇas in order.

257.s:
liṅgasya cchedane mṛttau madhyamo mūlyameva ca /
mahāpaśūnāmeteṣu sthāneṣu dviguṇā damāḥ //
257.d:
लिङ्गस्य च्छेदने मृत्तौ मध्यमो मूल्यमेव च /
महापशूनामेतेषु स्थानेषु द्विगुणा दमाः //
257.m: For cutting off the generative organ or causing death, the middle [fine] and the actual value [must be paid]; / in these same cases regarding large animals, the fines are double.

257.s:
prarohiśākhināṃ śākhāskandhasarvavidāraṇe /
upajīvyadrumāṇāntu viṃśaterdviguṇā damāḥ(1) //
257.d:
प्ररोहिशाखिनां शाखास्कन्धसर्वविदारणे /
उपजीव्यद्रुमाणान्तु विंशतेर्द्विगुणा दमाः(1) //
257.m: For breaking branches, the trunk, or the whole of spreading trees, / and [especially] for trees that provide a livelihood, the fines are double twenty [paṇas].

257.s:
yaḥ sāhasaṅkārayati sa dāpyo dviguṇandamam /
yastvevamuktvāhaṃ dātā kārayet sa caturguṇam //
257.d:
यः साहसङ्कारयति स दाप्यो द्विगुणन्दमम् /
यस्त्वेवमुक्त्वाहं दाता कारयेत् स चतुर्गुणम् //
257.m: He who incites an act of violence must be made to pay double the fine; / but he who incites it by saying, “I will pay [the fine],” [must be made to pay] fourfold.

257.s:
āryākrośātikramakṛdbhrātṛjāyāprahāradaḥ /
sandiṣṭasyāpradātā ca samudragṛhabhedakaḥ //
257.d:
आर्याक्रोशातिक्रमकृद्भ्रातृजायाप्रहारदः /
सन्दिष्टस्याप्रदाता च समुद्रगृहभेदकः //
257.m: One who reviles or insults noble persons, one who strikes a brother's wife, / one who does not deliver a entrusted message, one who breaks open a sealed house,

257.s:
sāmantakulikādīnāmapakārasya kārakaḥ /
pañcāśatpaṇiko daṇḍa eṣāmiti viniś cayaḥ //
257.d:
सामन्तकुलिकादीनामपकारस्य कारकः /
पञ्चाशत्पणिको दण्ड एषामिति विनिश् चयः //
257.m: and one who causes harm to neighbours, eminent family heads, and others— / the fine for these is fifty paṇas; this is the settled rule.

257.s:
svacchandavidhavāgāmī vikruṣṭe nābhidhāvakaḥ /
akāraṇe ca vikroṣṭā caṇḍālaścottamān spṛśan //
257.d:
स्वच्छन्दविधवागामी विक्रुष्टे नाभिधावकः /
अकारणे च विक्रोष्टा चण्डालश्चोत्तमान् स्पृशन् //
257.m: One who cohabits with an independent widow, one who does not run to help upon a cry for help, / one who cries out without cause, and a caṇḍāla who touches higher-caste persons,

257.s:
śūdraḥ pravrajitānāñca daive paitrye ca bhojakaḥ /
:n
1 prarohiśākhināmityādirviṃśaterdviguṇā damā ity antaḥ
pāṭhaḥ kha.. pustake nāsti
:p 432
ayuktaṃ śapathaṃ kurvannayogyo yogyakarmakṛt //
257.d:
शूद्रः प्रव्रजितानाञ्च दैवे पैत्र्ये च भोजकः /
:न्
1 प्ररोहिशाखिनामित्यादिर्विंशतेर्द्विगुणा दमा इत्य् अन्तः
पाठः ख.. पुस्तके नास्ति
:प् 432
अयुक्तं शपथं कुर्वन्नयोग्यो योग्यकर्मकृत् //
257.m:
a śūdra who feeds ascetics in rites to the gods or to the ancestors,
[Footnote]
1. The passage from “prarohiśākhinām” to “viṃśaterdviguṇā damāḥ” is absent in manuscript Kha. / [Page 432]
one who takes an improper oath, one who is unqualified but performs a qualified person's duty,

257.s:
vṛṣakṣudrapaśūnāñca pūṃstvasya pratighātakṛt /
sādhāraṇasyāpalopī dāsīgarbhavināśakṛt //
257.d:
वृषक्षुद्रपशूनाञ्च पूंस्त्वस्य प्रतिघातकृत् /
साधारणस्यापलोपी दासीगर्भविनाशकृत् //
257.m: one who destroys the virility of a bull or of small animals, / one who conceals common property, one who causes an abortion in a female slave,

257.s:
pitāputrasvasṛbhrātṛdampatyācāryaśiṣyakāḥ /
eṣāmapatitānyonyatyāgī ca śatadaṇḍabhāk //
257.d:
पितापुत्रस्वसृभ्रातृदम्पत्याचार्यशिष्यकाः /
एषामपतितान्योन्यत्यागी च शतदण्डभाक् //
257.m: and among father, son, sister, brother, husband and wife, or teacher and student, / whoever abandons the other when not fallen [from caste]—shall incur a fine of one hundred [paṇas].

257.s:
vasānastrīn paṇān daṇḍyo nejakastu parāṃśukam /
vikrayāvakrayādhānayāciteṣu paṇān daśa //
257.d:
वसानस्त्रीन् पणान् दण्ड्यो नेजकस्तु परांशुकम् /
विक्रयावक्रयाधानयाचितेषु पणान् दश //
257.m: A washerman who wears another's garment is to be fined three paṇas; / [and for] selling, renting, pawning, or lending it out, ten paṇas.

257.s:
tulāśāsanamānānāṃ kūṭakṛnnāṇakasya ca /
ebhiś ca vyavahartā yaḥ sa dāpyo daṇḍamuttamam //
257.d:
तुलाशासनमानानां कूटकृन्नाणकस्य च /
एभिश् च व्यवहर्ता यः स दाप्यो दण्डमुत्तमम् //
257.m: A maker of false balances, royal edicts, measures, or coins, / and whoever trades with these, must be made to pay the highest fine.

257.s:
akūṭaṃ kūṭakaṃ brūte kūṭaṃ yaścāpyakūṭakam /
sa nāṇakaparīkṣī tu dāpyaḥ prathamasāhasam //
257.d:
अकूटं कूटकं ब्रूते कूटं यश्चाप्यकूटकम् /
स नाणकपरीक्षी तु दाप्यः प्रथमसाहसम् //
257.m: An examiner of coins who declares what is genuine to be counterfeit, or what is counterfeit to be genuine, / must be made to pay the first degree of violence [fine].

257.s:
bhiṣaṅmithyācaran dāpyastiryakṣu prathamaṃ damam /
mānuṣe madhyamaṃ rājamānuṣeṣūttamantathā //
257.d:
भिषङ्मिथ्याचरन् दाप्यस्तिर्यक्षु प्रथमं दमम् /
मानुषे मध्यमं राजमानुषेषूत्तमन्तथा //
257.m: A physician acting improperly must be made to pay the first fine in the case of animals, / the middle one in the case of human beings, and the highest in the case of royal officials.

257.s:
abadhyaṃ yaś ca badhnāti badhyaṃ yaś ca pramuñcati /
aprāptavyavahārañca sa dāpyo damamuttamam //
257.d:
अबध्यं यश् च बध्नाति बध्यं यश् च प्रमुञ्चति /
अप्राप्तव्यवहारञ्च स दाप्यो दममुत्तमम् //
257.m: He who binds one who should not be bound, and he who releases one who should be bound, / or [he who prosecutes] one who has not reached legal maturity, must be made to pay the highest fine.

257.s:
mānena tulayā vāpi yo 'ṃśamaṣṭamakaṃ haret /
dvāviṃśatipaṇān dāpyo vṛddhau hānau ca kalpitam //
257.d:
मानेन तुलया वापि यो ऽंशमष्टमकं हरेत् /
द्वाविंशतिपणान् दाप्यो वृद्धौ हानौ च कल्पितम् //
257.m: Whoever takes away an eighth part by [false] measure or balance / must be made to pay twenty-two paṇas; [the fine] is determined in proportion to the increase or decrease.

257.s:
bheṣajasnehalavaṇagandhānyaguḍādiṣu /
paṇyeṣu prakṣipan hīnaṃ paṇāndāpyastu ṣoḍaśa //
257.d:
भेषजस्नेहलवणगन्धान्यगुडादिषु /
पण्येषु प्रक्षिपन् हीनं पणान्दाप्यस्तु षोडश //
257.m: In the case of commodities such as medicine, oil, salt, perfumes, corn, and molasses, / one who throws in inferior [substances] must be made to pay sixteen paṇas.

257.s:
sambhūya kurvatāmarghaṃ sabādhaṃ kāruśilpināṃ /
arthasya hrāsaḥ vṛddhiṃ vā sahasro daṇḍa ucyate //
257.d:
सम्भूय कुर्वतामर्घं सबाधं कारुशिल्पिनां /
अर्थस्य ह्रासः वृद्धिं वा सहस्रो दण्ड उच्यते //
257.m: For artisans and craftsmen who conspire together to fix a obstructing price / that causes the diminution or inflation of goods, a fine of one thousand is declared.

257.s:
rājāni sthāpyate yo 'rthaḥ pratyahaṃ tena vikrayaḥ /
krayo vā nisravastasmādbaṇijāṃ lābhakṛt smṛtaḥ //
:p 433
257.d:
राजानि स्थाप्यते यो ऽर्थः प्रत्यहं तेन विक्रयः /
क्रयो वा निस्रवस्तस्माद्बणिजां लाभकृत् स्मृतः //
:प् 433
257.m:
The value that is fixed daily by the king—by that the selling / or purchasing should proceed; the profit remaining from that is recorded as the merchant's gain.
[Page 433]

257.s:
svadeśapaṇye tu śataṃ baṇij gṛhṇīta pañcakaṃ /
daśakaṃ pāradeśye tu yaḥ sadyaḥ krayavikrayau //
257.d:
स्वदेशपण्ये तु शतं बणिज् गृह्णीत पञ्चकं /
दशकं पारदेश्ये तु यः सद्यः क्रयविक्रयौ //
257.m: On merchandise of one's own country, the merchant may take five percent, / but ten percent on foreign goods, when purchase and sale are immediate.

257.s:
paṇyasyopari saṃsthāpya vyayaṃ paṇyasamudbhavaṃ /
artho 'nugrahakṛt kāryaḥ kreturvikretureva ca //
257.d:
पण्यस्योपरि संस्थाप्य व्ययं पण्यसमुद्भवं /
अर्थो ऽनुग्रहकृत् कार्यः क्रेतुर्विक्रेतुरेव च //
257.m: Adding onto the commodity the expenses arising from the commodity, / a price beneficial to both buyer and seller should be fixed.

257.s:
gṛhītamūlyaṃ yaḥ paṇyaṃ kreturnaiva prayacchati /
sodayantasya dāpyo 'sau diglābhaṃ vā digāgate //
257.d:
गृहीतमूल्यं यः पण्यं क्रेतुर्नैव प्रयच्छति /
सोदयन्तस्य दाप्यो ऽसौ दिग्लाभं वा दिगागते //
257.m: He who does not deliver the merchandise to the buyer after receiving the payment / must be made to deliver it to him with interest, or with the foreign profit if it has arrived from another country.

257.s:
vikrītamapi vikreyaṃ pūrve kretaryagṛhṇati /
hāniścet kretṛdoṣeṇa kretureva hi sā bhavet //
257.d:
विक्रीतमपि विक्रेयं पूर्वे क्रेतर्यगृह्णति /
हानिश्चेत् क्रेतृदोषेण क्रेतुरेव हि सा भवेत् //
257.m: Even if sold, [the goods] may be resold if the first buyer does not accept [them]; / if loss occurs through the fault of the buyer, that loss indeed falls upon the buyer alone.

257.s:
rājadaivopaghātena paṇye doṣamupāgate /
hānirvikreturevāsau yācitasyāprayacchataḥ //
257.d:
राजदैवोपघातेन पण्ये दोषमुपागते /
हानिर्विक्रेतुरेवासौ याचितस्याप्रयच्छतः //
257.m: When a defect occurs in a commodity through royal or divine accident, / that loss belongs to the seller alone if he did not deliver it when demanded.

257.s:
anyahaste ca vikrītaṃ duṣṭaṃ vā duṣṭavadyadi /
vikrīnīte damastatra tanmūlyādadviguṇo bhavet //
257.d:
अन्यहस्ते च विक्रीतं दुष्टं वा दुष्टवद्यदि /
विक्रीनीते दमस्तत्र तन्मूल्यादद्विगुणो भवेत् //
257.m: If one sells into another's hand what has already been sold, or sells a defective item as non-defective, / the fine in that case should be double its value.

257.s:
kṣayaṃ vṛddhiñca baṇijā paṇyānāmavijānatā /
krītvā nānuśayaḥ kāryaḥ kurvan ṣaḍ bhāgadaṇḍabhāk //
257.d:
क्षयं वृद्धिञ्च बणिजा पण्यानामविजानता /
क्रीत्वा नानुशयः कार्यः कुर्वन् षड् भागदण्डभाक् //
257.m: A merchant who does not know the rise and fall [in value] of commodities / should not entertain regret after buying; if he does, he incurs a fine of the sixth share.

257.s:
samavāyena baṇijāṃ lābhārthaṃ karma kurvatāṃ /
labhālābhau yathā dravyaṃ yathā vā saṃvidā kṛtau //
257.d:
समवायेन बणिजां लाभार्थं कर्म कुर्वतां /
लभालाभौ यथा द्रव्यं यथा वा संविदा कृतौ //
257.m: For merchants carrying on business in partnership for the sake of profit, / the gain and loss are in proportion to the capital or as agreed by contract.

257.s:
pratiṣiddhamanādiṣṭaṃ pramādādyacca nāśitaṃ /
sa taddayādvipravācca rakṣitāddaśamāṃśabhāk //
257.d:
प्रतिषिद्धमनादिष्टं प्रमादाद्यच्च नाशितं /
स तद्दयाद्विप्रवाच्च रक्षिताद्दशमांशभाक् //
257.m: What is destroyed through negligence, forbidden, or unauthorised, / he must make good; and from what is preserved against danger he is entitled to a tenth share.

257.s:
arthaprekṣapaṇādviṃśaṃ bhāgaṃ śulkaṃ nṛpā haret /
vyāsiddhaṃ rājayogyañca vikrītaṃ rājagāmi tat //
257.d:
अर्थप्रेक्षपणाद्विंशं भागं शुल्कं नृपा हरेत् /
व्यासिद्धं राजयोग्यञ्च विक्रीतं राजगामि तत् //
257.m: The king should take a twentieth share as toll upon inspecting the value [of the goods]; / that which is prohibited and that which is fit for the king, if sold, shall go to the king.

257.s:
mithyā vadan parīmāṇaṃ śulkasthānādapakraman /
dāpyastvaṣṭaguṇaṃ yaś ca savyājakrayavikrayau //
257.d:
मिथ्या वदन् परीमाणं शुल्कस्थानादपक्रमन् /
दाप्यस्त्वष्टगुणं यश् च सव्याजक्रयविक्रयौ //
257.m: One who states a false measurement or evades the toll-house, / and whoever makes a fraudulent purchase or sale, must be made to pay eight times [the toll].

257.s:
deśantaragate prete dravyaṃ dāyādabāndhavāḥ /
:p 434
jñātayo vā hareyustadāgatāstair vinā nṛpaḥ //
257.d:
देशन्तरगते प्रेते द्रव्यं दायादबान्धवाः /
:प् 434
ज्ञातयो वा हरेयुस्तदागतास्तैर् विना नृपः //
257.m:
When [a person] has died while in another country, heirs, relatives,
[Page 434]
or kinsmen who have arrived may take that property; in their absence, the king [takes it].

257.s:
jihmaṃ tyajeyurnirlobhamaśakto 'nyena kārayet /
anena vidhirākhyāta ṛtvikkarṣakarmiṇāṃ //
257.d:
जिह्मं त्यजेयुर्निर्लोभमशक्तो ऽन्येन कारयेत् /
अनेन विधिराख्यात ऋत्विक्कर्षकर्मिणां //
257.m: [Partners] may abandon a dishonest member without giving him profit; one unable [to work] may have it done by another; / by this, the rule for officiating priests, cultivators, and artisans is declared.

257.s:
grāhakair gṛhyate cauro loptreṇātha padena vā /
pūrvakarmāparādhī vā tathaivāśuddhavāsakaḥ //
257.d:
ग्राहकैर् गृह्यते चौरो लोप्त्रेणाथ पदेन वा /
पूर्वकर्मापराधी वा तथैवाशुद्धवासकः //
257.m: A thief is caught by arresting officers either by the stolen goods or by footprints, / or by being an offender in past actions, or likewise by living in an impure manner.

257.s:
anye 'pi śaṅkayā grāhyā jātināmādinihnavaiḥ /
dyūtastrīpānaśaktāś ca śuṣkabhinnamukhasvarāḥ //
257.d:
अन्ये ऽपि शङ्कया ग्राह्या जातिनामादिनिह्नवैः /
द्यूतस्त्रीपानशक्ताश् च शुष्कभिन्नमुखस्वराः //
257.m: Others also may be seized on suspicion by their concealing their caste, name, and the like, / by their addiction to gambling, women, and drink, and by having a dry or broken face and voice,

257.s:
paradravyagṛhāṇāñca pṛcchakā gūḍhacāriṇaḥ /
nirāyā vyayavantaś ca vinaṣṭa dravyavikrayāḥ //
257.d:
परद्रव्यगृहाणाञ्च पृच्छका गूढचारिणः /
निराया व्ययवन्तश् च विनष्ट द्रव्यविक्रयाः //
257.m: by inquiring into the wealth and houses of others, moving about secretly, / spending without having income, and selling lost or stolen articles.

257.s:
gṛhītaḥ śaṅkayā cauryenātmānañcedviśodhayet /
dāpayitvā hṛtaṃ dravyaṃ cauradaṇḍena daṇḍayet //
257.d:
गृहीतः शङ्कया चौर्येनात्मानञ्चेद्विशोधयेत् /
दापयित्वा हृतं द्रव्यं चौरदण्डेन दण्डयेत् //
257.m: If one seized on suspicion of theft does not clear himself, / having made him restore the stolen property, [the king] should punish him with the punishment for a thief.

257.s:
cauraṃ pradāpyāpahṛtaṃ ghātayedvividhair budhaiḥ /
sacihnaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ kṛtvā svarāṣṭrādvipravāsayet //
257.d:
चौरं प्रदाप्यापहृतं घातयेद्विविधैर् बुधैः /
सचिह्नं ब्राह्मणं कृत्वा स्वराष्ट्राद्विप्रवासयेत् //
257.m: Having made the thief restore what was stolen, [the king] should have him executed by various [means deemed fit by] the wise. / Having branded a brāhmaṇa with a mark, he should banish him from his kingdom.

257.s:
ghātite 'pahṛte doṣo grāmabharturanirgate /
svasīmni dadyādgrāmastu padaṃ vā yatra gacchati //
257.d:
घातिते ऽपहृते दोषो ग्रामभर्तुरनिर्गते /
स्वसीम्नि दद्याद्ग्रामस्तु पदं वा यत्र गच्छति //
257.m: If [someone] is killed or [property] stolen without having left [the village], the fault belongs to the village head. / But the village must make it good within its own boundary, or wherever the footprint leads.

257.s:
pañcagrāmī vahiḥ krośāddaśagrāmya.atha vā punaḥ /
vandigrāhāṃs tathā vājikuñjarāṇāñca hāriṇaḥ //
257.d:
पञ्चग्रामी वहिः क्रोशाद्दशग्राम्य.अथ वा पुनः /
वन्दिग्राहांस् तथा वाजिकुञ्जराणाञ्च हारिणः //
257.m: Beyond a krośa, a group of five villages [is responsible], or again a group of ten villages. / So too, kidnappers of prisoners and those who steal horses and elephants,

257.s:
prasahya ghātinaś caiva śūlamāropayennarān /
utkṣepakagranthibhedau karasandaṃśahīnakau //
257.d:
प्रसह्य घातिनश् चैव शूलमारोपयेन्नरान् /
उत्क्षेपकग्रन्थिभेदौ करसन्दंशहीनकौ //
257.m: And men who kill by violence, he should impale on a stake. / A pickpocket and a cutpurse should have their thumb and index finger cut off;

257.s:
kāryau dvitīyāparādhe karapādaikahīnakau /
bhaktāvakāśāgnyudakamantrāpakaraṇavyayān //
257.d:
कार्यौ द्वितीयापराधे करपादैकहीनकौ /
भक्तावकाशाग्न्युदकमन्त्रापकरणव्ययान् //
257.m: For a second offence, they are to be deprived of one hand and one foot. / He who provides food, shelter, fire, water, counsel, implements, or expense money

257.s:
dattvā caurasya hanturvā jānato dama uttamaḥ /
śastrāvapāte garbhasya pātane cottamo damaḥ //
:p 435
257.d:
दत्त्वा चौरस्य हन्तुर्वा जानतो दम उत्तमः /
शस्त्रावपाते गर्भस्य पातने चोत्तमो दमः //
:प् 435
257.m:
To a thief or a murderer, knowing [who they are], incurs the highest fine. / For striking with a weapon, and for causing an abortion, the fine is also the highest.
[Page 435]

257.s:
uttamo vādhamo vāpi puruṣastrīpramāpaṇe /
śilāṃ baddhvā kṣipedapsu naraghnīṃ viṣadāṃ striyaṃ //
257.d:
उत्तमो वाधमो वापि पुरुषस्त्रीप्रमापणे /
शिलां बद्ध्वा क्षिपेदप्सु नरघ्नीं विषदां स्त्रियं //
257.m: Whether the highest or the lowest [fine applies] in the killing of a man or a woman. / Tying a stone [to her], one should cast into the water a woman who has murdered a man or administered poison.

257.s:
viṣāgnidāṃ nijagurunijāpatyapramāpaṇīṃ /
vikarṇakaranāsauṣṭhīṃ kṛtvā gobhiḥ pramāpayet //
257.d:
विषाग्निदां निजगुरुनिजापत्यप्रमापणीं /
विकर्णकरनासौष्ठीं कृत्वा गोभिः प्रमापयेत् //
257.m: A woman who administers poison or sets fire, or who murders her own elders or her own offspring, / he should deprive of ears, hands, nose, and lips, and cause to be killed by cattle.

257.s:
kṣetraveśmavanagrāmavivītakhaladāhakāḥ /
rājapatny abhigāmī ca dagdhavyāstu kaṭāgninā //
257.d:
क्षेत्रवेश्मवनग्रामविवीतखलदाहकाः /
राजपत्न्य् अभिगामी च दग्धव्यास्तु कटाग्निना //
257.m: Those who burn fields, houses, forests, villages, pastures, and threshing-floors, / and one who approaches the king's wife, are to be burned with a straw fire.

257.s:
pumān saṃgrahaṇe grāhyaḥ keśākeśiparastriyāḥ /
svajātāvuttamo daṇḍa ānulomye tu madhyamaḥ //
257.d:
पुमान् संग्रहणे ग्राह्यः केशाकेशिपरस्त्रियाः /
स्वजातावुत्तमो दण्ड आनुलोम्ये तु मध्यमः //
257.m: A man is caught in adultery by hair-pulling with another's wife. / In [the case of woman of] one's own caste, the punishment is the highest [fine]; but with a woman of a lower caste, it is the middle [fine].

257.s:
prātilomye badhaḥ puṃsāṃ nāryāḥ karṇāvakartanam /
nīvīstanaprāvaraṇanābhikeśāvamardanam //
257.d:
प्रातिलोम्ये बधः पुंसां नार्याः कर्णावकर्तनम् /
नीवीस्तनप्रावरणनाभिकेशावमर्दनम् //
257.m: In the inverse order of castes, there is death for men, and cutting off the ears for a woman. / Touching the waist-knot, breasts, upper garment, navel, or hair,

257.s:
adeśakālasambhāṣaṃ sahāvasthānameva ca /
strī niṣedhe śataṃ dadyād dviśatantu damaṃ pumān //
257.d:
अदेशकालसम्भाषं सहावस्थानमेव च /
स्त्री निषेधे शतं दद्याद् द्विशतन्तु दमं पुमान् //
257.m: Conversing at an unseasonable time or place, and staying together— / if forbidden [to do so], the woman should pay a fine of one hundred [paṇas], and the man two hundred.

257.s:
pratiṣedhe tayordaṇḍo yathā saṃgrahaṇe tathā /
paśūn gacchaṃśchataṃ dāpyo hīnāṃ strīṃ gāś ca madhyamam //
257.d:
प्रतिषेधे तयोर्दण्डो यथा संग्रहणे तथा /
पशून् गच्छंश्छतं दाप्यो हीनां स्त्रीं गाश् च मध्यमम् //
257.m: If forbidden by both, the punishment is the same as for adultery. / One who has intercourse with animals should be made to pay one hundred [paṇas]; with a low-caste woman or a cow, the middle [fine].

257.s:
avaruddhāsu dāsīṣu bhujiṣyāsu tathaiva ca /
gamyāsvapi pumāndāpyaḥ pañcāśat paṇikandamam //
257.d:
अवरुद्धासु दासीषु भुजिष्यासु तथैव च /
गम्यास्वपि पुमान्दाप्यः पञ्चाशत् पणिकन्दमम् //
257.m: With kept female slaves, and likewise with female servants, / even if accessible, a man should be made to pay a fine of fifty paṇas.

257.s:
prasahya dāsyabhigame daṇḍo daśapaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ /
kubandhenāṅkya gamayedantyāpravrajitāgame //
257.d:
प्रसह्य दास्यभिगमे दण्डो दशपणः स्मृतः /
कुबन्धेनाङ्क्य गमयेदन्त्याप्रव्रजितागमे //
257.m: For forcibly approaching a female slave, a fine of ten paṇas is prescribed. / If one approaches a woman of the lowest caste or a female ascetic, [the king] should banish him after branding him with an ignominious mark.

257.s:
nyūnaṃ vāpyadhikaṃ vāpi likhedyo rājaśāsanam /
pāradārikacauraṃ vā muñcato daṇḍa uttamaḥ //
257.d:
न्यूनं वाप्यधिकं वापि लिखेद्यो राजशासनम् /
पारदारिकचौरं वा मुञ्चतो दण्ड उत्तमः //
257.m: He who writes a royal edict with less or more [than ordered], / or releases an adulterer or a thief, incurs the highest fine.

257.s:
abhakṣair dūṣayan vipraṃ daṇḍa uttamasāhasam /
kūṭasvarṇavyavahārī vimāṃsasya ca vikrayī //
257.d:
अभक्षैर् दूषयन् विप्रं दण्ड उत्तमसाहसम् /
कूटस्वर्णव्यवहारी विमांसस्य च विक्रयी //
257.m: Defiling a brāhmaṇa with uneatables incurs the fine of the highest degree of violence. / A dealer in counterfeit gold and a seller of forbidden meat

257.s:
aṅgahīnaś ca kartavyo dāpyaścottamasāhasaṃ /
:p 436
śakto hy amokṣayan svāmī daṃṣṭriṇaḥ śṛṅgiṇas tathā //
257.d:
अङ्गहीनश् च कर्तव्यो दाप्यश्चोत्तमसाहसं /
:प् 436
शक्तो ह्य् अमोक्षयन् स्वामी दंष्ट्रिणः शृङ्गिणस् तथा //
257.m:
Should be mutilated of a limb and made to pay the highest fine.
[Page 436]
An owner, though capable, who does not restrain an animal with tusks or horns,

257.s:
prathamaṃ sāhasaṃ dadyādvikruṣṭe dviguṇaṃ tathā /
acaurañcaure 'bhivadan dāpyaḥ pañcaśataṃ damaṃ //
257.d:
प्रथमं साहसं दद्याद्विक्रुष्टे द्विगुणं तथा /
अचौरञ्चौरे ऽभिवदन् दाप्यः पञ्चशतं दमं //
257.m: Should pay the first degree of violence; and twice as much if a cry for help was raised. / Accusing a non-thief of being a thief, one should be made to pay a fine of five hundred [paṇas].

257.s:
rājño 'niṣṭapravaktāraṃ tasyaivākrośakaṃ tathā /
mṛtāṅgalagnavikreturgurostāḍayitus tathā //
257.d:
राज्ञो ऽनिष्टप्रवक्तारं तस्यैवाक्रोशकं तथा /
मृताङ्गलग्नविक्रेतुर्गुरोस्ताडयितुस् तथा //
257.m: One who speaks what is unwelcome to the king, one who reviles him, / a seller of what was attached to a dead body, and one who strikes a teacher,

257.s:
tanmantrasya ca bhettāraṃ chittvā jihvāṃ pravāsayet /
rājayānāsanāroḍhurdaṇḍo madhyamasāhasaḥ //
257.d:
तन्मन्त्रस्य च भेत्तारं छित्त्वा जिह्वां प्रवासयेत् /
राजयानासनारोढुर्दण्डो मध्यमसाहसः //
257.m: And one who betrays his secrets—having cut out [his] tongue, he should banish him. / For one who mounts the king's conveyance or seat, the punishment is the middle degree of violence.

257.s:
dvinetrabhedino rājadviṣṭādeśakṛtas tathā /
vipratvena ca śūdrasya jīvato 'ṣṭaśato damaḥ //
257.d:
द्विनेत्रभेदिनो राजद्विष्टादेशकृतस् तथा /
विप्रत्वेन च शूद्रस्य जीवतो ऽष्टशतो दमः //
257.m: For one who gouges out both eyes, one who carries out what the king hates, / and for a śūdra living by posing as a brāhmaṇa, the fine is eight hundred [paṇas].

257.s:
yo manyetājito 'smīti nyāyenābhiparājitaḥ /
tamāyāntaṃ punarjitvā daṇḍayeddviguṇaṃ damaṃ //
257.d:
यो मन्येताजितो ऽस्मीति न्यायेनाभिपराजितः /
तमायान्तं पुनर्जित्वा दण्डयेद्द्विगुणं दमं //
257.m: He who, having been legally defeated, thinks, 'I am not defeated'— / when he returns, having defeated him again, [the king] should fine him double the penalty.

257.s:
rājñānyāyena yo daṇḍo gṛhīto varuṇāyataṃ /
vivedya dadyādviprebhyaḥ svayaṃ triṃśadguṇīkṛtaṃ //
257.d:
राज्ञान्यायेन यो दण्डो गृहीतो वरुणायतं /
विवेद्य दद्याद्विप्रेभ्यः स्वयं त्रिंशद्गुणीकृतं //
257.m: A fine that has been unlawfully collected by the king, he should dedicate to Varuṇa / and give to brāhmaṇas himself, multiplied thirtyfold.

257.s:
dharmaścārthaś ca kīrtiñca lokapaṅktirupagrahaḥ /
prajābhyo bahumānañca svargasthānañca śāśvatam //
257.d:
धर्मश्चार्थश् च कीर्तिञ्च लोकपङ्क्तिरुपग्रहः /
प्रजाभ्यो बहुमानञ्च स्वर्गस्थानञ्च शाश्वतम् //
257.m: Righteousness, wealth, fame, the respect of the world, conciliation, / high esteem from his subjects, and an eternal place in heaven—

257.s:
paśyato vyavahārāṃś ca guṇāḥ syuḥ sapta bhūpateḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe vākpāruṣyādiprakaraṇaṃ nāma
saptapañcāśadadhikadviśatatmo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:p 437
:ś athāṣṭapañcāśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
ṛgvidhānaṃ
257.d:
पश्यतो व्यवहारांश् च गुणाः स्युः सप्त भूपतेः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे वाक्पारुष्यादिप्रकरणं नाम
सप्तपञ्चाशदधिकद्विशतत्मो ऽध्यायः ||
:प् 437
:श् अथाष्टपञ्चाशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
ऋग्विधानं
257.m:
These seven merits accrue to a king who properly investigates legal proceedings.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the chapter titled 'Section on Verbal Abuse and Other Offences', the two hundred and fifty-seventh chapter.
[Page 437]
Now, the two hundred and fifty-eighth chapter:
The Application of the Ṛgveda.

258.s:
agnir uvāca
ṛgyajuḥsāmātharvavidhānaṃ puṣkaroditam /
bhuktimuktikaraṃ japyāddhomādrāmāya tadvade //
258.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
ऋग्यजुःसामाथर्वविधानं पुष्करोदितम् /
भुक्तिमुक्तिकरं जप्याद्धोमाद्रामाय तद्वदे //
258.m: Agni said: / The applications of the Ṛg-, Yajur-, Sāma-, and Atharva-[vedas] spoken by Puṣkara, / which bestow worldly enjoyment and liberation through recitation and fire oblation, I shall declare to you, O Rāma.

258.s:
puṣkara uvāca
prativedantu karmāṇi kāryāṇi pravadāmi te /
prathamaṃ ṛgvidhānaṃ vai śṛṇu tvaṃ bhuktimuktidam //
258.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
प्रतिवेदन्तु कर्माणि कार्याणि प्रवदामि ते /
प्रथमं ऋग्विधानं वै शृणु त्वं भुक्तिमुक्तिदम् //
258.m: Puṣkara said: / I shall declare to you the rites to be performed according to each Veda. / First, hear the application of the Ṛgveda, which bestows worldly enjoyment and liberation.

258.s:
antarjale tathā home japatī manasepsitam /
kāmaṃ karoti gāyatrī prāṇāyāmādviśeṣataḥ //
258.d:
अन्तर्जले तथा होमे जपती मनसेप्सितम् /
कामं करोति गायत्री प्राणायामाद्विशेषतः //
258.m: Recited under water or in a fire oblation, the Gāyatrī fulfills any desire / cherished in the mind, especially through breath control.

258.s:
gāyatryā daśasāhasro japo naktāśano dvija /
bahusnātasya tatraiva sarvakalmaṣanāśanaḥ //
258.d:
गायत्र्या दशसाहस्रो जपो नक्ताशनो द्विज /
बहुस्नातस्य तत्रैव सर्वकल्मषनाशनः //
258.m: A recitation of ten thousand times of the Gāyatrī, eating only at night, O twice-born, / destroys all sins for one who bathes frequently right there.

258.s:
daśāyutāni japtvātha haviṣyāśī sa muktibhāk /
praṇavo hi paraṃ brahma tajjapaḥ sarvapāpahā //
258.d:
दशायुतानि जप्त्वाथ हविष्याशी स मुक्तिभाक् /
प्रणवो हि परं ब्रह्म तज्जपः सर्वपापहा //
258.m: Having recited [it] one hundred thousand times while eating sacrificial food, one attains liberation. / The praṇava is indeed the supreme Brahman; its recitation destroys all sins.

258.s:
oṃkāraśatajaptantu nābhimātrodake sthitaḥ /
jalaṃ pivet sa sarvaistu pāpair vai(1) vipramucyate //
258.d:
ओंकारशतजप्तन्तु नाभिमात्रोदके स्थितः /
जलं पिवेत् स सर्वैस्तु पापैर् वै(1) विप्रमुच्यते //
258.m: Standing in water up to the navel, he who drinks water / over which the syllable Om has been recited one hundred times is freed from all sins.

258.s:
mātrātrayaṃ trayo vedāstrayo devāstrayo 'gnayaḥ /
mahāvyāhṛtayaḥ sapta lokā homo 'khilāghahā //
258.d:
मात्रात्रयं त्रयो वेदास्त्रयो देवास्त्रयो ऽग्नयः /
महाव्याहृतयः सप्त लोका होमो ऽखिलाघहा //
258.m: Its three morae are the three Vedas, the three gods, the three fires. / The seven great sacred utterances are the seven worlds; a fire oblation [with them] destroys all sin.

258.s:
gāyatrī paramā jāpyā mahāvyāhṛtayas tathā /
antarjale tathā rāma proktaś caivāghamarṣaṇaḥ //
258.d:
गायत्री परमा जाप्या महाव्याहृतयस् तथा /
अन्तर्जले तथा राम प्रोक्तश् चैवाघमर्षणः //
258.m: The supreme Gāyatrī is to be recited, as well as the great sacred utterances; / and likewise, O Rāma, the Aghamarṣaṇa hymn is declared [to be recited] under water.

258.s:
agnimīle purohitaṃ sūtko 'yaṃ vahnidaivataḥ /
:n
1 pāpair hi vipramucyata iti ga.. , gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 438
śirasā dhārayan vahniṃ yo japetparivatsaram //
258.d:
अग्निमीले पुरोहितं सूत्को ऽयं वह्निदैवतः /
:न्
1 पापैर् हि विप्रमुच्यत इति ग.. , घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 438
शिरसा धारयन् वह्निं यो जपेत्परिवत्सरम् //
258.m:
This hymn, 'I praise Agni the priest,' has the fire-god as its deity.
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: ‘is freed indeed from sins’ according to manuscripts ga, gha, and ña.] / [Page 438]
He who, holding fire upon his head, should recite it for a full year,

258.s:
homaṃ triṣavaṇaṃ bhaikṣyamanagnijvalanañcaret /
ataḥ paramṛcaḥ sapta vāyvādyā yāḥ prakīrtitāḥ //
258.d:
होमं त्रिषवणं भैक्ष्यमनग्निज्वलनञ्चरेत् /
अतः परमृचः सप्त वाय्वाद्या याः प्रकीर्तिताः //
258.m: Performing fire oblation, [bathing at] the three divisions of the day, subsisting on alms, and abstaining from lighting [other] fires; / subsequent to this are the seven verses declared to have Vāyu and others [as deities];

258.s:
tā japan prayato nityamiṣṭān kāmān samaśnute /
medhākāmo japennityaṃ sadasanyamiti tyacam //
258.d:
ता जपन् प्रयतो नित्यमिष्टान् कामान् समश्नुते /
मेधाकामो जपेन्नित्यं सदसन्यमिति त्यचम् //
258.m: Reciting them constantly with restraint, one attains his desired wishes. / One desiring intellect should daily recite the triplet beginning with 'sadasaspatim'.

258.s:
anvayo yannimāḥ proktāḥ navarco mṛtyunāśanāḥ /
śunaḥśephamṛṣiṃ baddhaḥ sanniruddho 'tha vā(1) japet //
258.d:
अन्वयो यन्निमाः प्रोक्ताः नवर्चो मृत्युनाशनाः /
शुनःशेफमृषिं बद्धः सन्निरुद्धो ऽथ वा(1) जपेत् //
258.m: These nine verses are declared to be 'anvaya', destroying death. / One who is bound or imprisoned should recite [the hymn to] the sage Śunaḥśepha;

258.s:
mucyate sarvapāpebhyo gadī vāpyagado bhavet /
ya icchecchāśvataṃ kāmaṃ mitraṃ prājñaṃ purandaraṃ //
258.d:
मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो गदी वाप्यगदो भवेत् /
य इच्छेच्छाश्वतं कामं मित्रं प्राज्ञं पुरन्दरं //
258.m: He is freed from all sins, or if diseased, he becomes free from disease. / He who desires enduring love, a wise friend, or Indra,

258.s:
ṛgbhiḥ ṣoḍśabhiḥ kuryādindriyasyeti dine dine /
hiraṇyastūpamityetajjapan śatrūn prabādhate //
258.d:
ऋग्भिः षोड्शभिः कुर्यादिन्द्रियस्येति दिने दिने /
हिरण्यस्तूपमित्येतज्जपन् शत्रून् प्रबाधते //
258.m: Should [recite] day after day with the sixteen verses beginning with 'indriyasya'. / Reciting this [hymn] beginning with 'hiraṇyastūpa', he overcomes enemies.

258.s:
kṣemī bhavati cādhvāno ye te panthā japan naraḥ /
raudrībhiḥṣaḍbhirīśānaṃ stūyādyo vai dine dine //
258.d:
क्षेमी भवति चाध्वानो ये ते पन्था जपन् नरः /
रौद्रीभिःषड्भिरीशानं स्तूयाद्यो वै दिने दिने //
258.m: A man reciting 'ye te panthāḥ' ('Those paths of yours') fares safely on journeys. / He who praises Īśāna daily with the six Rudra verses,

258.s:
caruṃ vā kalpayedraudraṃ tasya śāntiḥ parā bhavet /
udityudantamādityamupatiṣṭhan dine dine //
258.d:
चरुं वा कल्पयेद्रौद्रं तस्य शान्तिः परा भवेत् /
उदित्युदन्तमादित्यमुपतिष्ठन् दिने दिने //
258.m: Or prepares a Rudra sacrificial cooked offering, attains supreme peace. / Paying homage day after day to the sun rising in the sky,

258.s:
kṣipejjalāñjalīn sapta manoduḥkhavināśanaṃ /
dviṣantamityathārdharcaṃ yadviprāntaṃ japan smaret //
258.d:
क्षिपेज्जलाञ्जलीन् सप्त मनोदुःखविनाशनं /
द्विषन्तमित्यथार्धर्चं यद्विप्रान्तं जपन् स्मरेत् //
258.m: He should offer seven handfuls of water, which destroys mental sorrow. / Reciting the half-verse beginning with 'dviṣantam' ('He who hates') up to the word 'vipra', if he contemplates [an enemy],

258.s:
āgaskṛt saptarātreṇa vidveṣamadhigacchati /
ārogyakāmī rogī vā praskannasyottamaṃ japet //
258.d:
आगस्कृत् सप्तरात्रेण विद्वेषमधिगच्छति /
आरोग्यकामी रोगी वा प्रस्कन्नस्योत्तमं जपेत् //
258.m: That wrongdoer incurs hatred within seven nights. / One desiring health, or one who is sick, should recite the highest [verse] of Praskaṇva.

258.s:
uttamastasya cārdharco japedvai vividhāsane /
udayatyāyurakṣyayyaṃ tejo madhyandine japet //
:n
1 sannibaddho 'theti ka.. , kha.. , ja.. ca
:p 439
258.d:
उत्तमस्तस्य चार्धर्चो जपेद्वै विविधासने /
उदयत्यायुरक्ष्यय्यं तेजो मध्यन्दिने जपेत् //
:न्
1 सन्निबद्धो ऽथेति क.. , ख.. , ज.. च
:प् 439
258.m:
One should recite the highest half-verse of it while in various postures. / Reciting it at midday, imperishable vitality and radiance arise.
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: ‘sannibaddho 'tha’ according to manuscripts ka, kha, and ja.] / [Page 439]

258.s:
astaṃ pratigate sūrye dviṣantaṃ pratibādhate /
na vayaśceti sūktāni japan śatrūnniyacchati //
258.d:
अस्तं प्रतिगते सूर्ये द्विषन्तं प्रतिबाधते /
न वयश्चेति सूक्तानि जपन् शत्रून्नियच्छति //
258.m: When the sun has set, he repels the enemy; / reciting the hymns beginning with “na vayaḥ,” he restrains his foes.

258.s:
ekādaśa suparṇasya sarvakāmānvinirdiśet /
ādhyātmikīḥ ka ity etā japanmokṣamavāpnuyāt //
258.d:
एकादश सुपर्णस्य सर्वकामान्विनिर्दिशेत् /
आध्यात्मिकीः क इत्य् एता जपन्मोक्षमवाप्नुयात् //
258.m: With the eleven [verses] of Suparṇa, he may appoint all desires. / Reciting these spiritual verses beginning with “kaḥ,” he attains liberation.

258.s:
ā no bhadrā ity anena dīrghamāyuravāpnuyāt /
tvaṃ someti ca sūktena navaṃ paśyenniśākaraṃ //
258.d:
आ नो भद्रा इत्य् अनेन दीर्घमायुरवाप्नुयात् /
त्वं सोमेति च सूक्तेन नवं पश्येन्निशाकरं //
258.m: With the [verse] “ā no bhadrāḥ,” he attains long life. / And with the hymn “tvaṃ soma,” he should gaze upon the new moon.

258.s:
upatiṣṭhet samitpāṇirvāsāṃsyāpnotyasaṃśayaṃ /
āyurīpsannimamiti kautsa sūktaṃ sadā japet //
258.d:
उपतिष्ठेत् समित्पाणिर्वासांस्याप्नोत्यसंशयं /
आयुरीप्सन्निममिति कौत्स सूक्तं सदा जपेत् //
258.m: Holding sacrificial faggots in hand, he should worship; he obtains garments, without doubt. / Desiring life, he should constantly recite the hymn of Kutsa beginning with “imam.”

258.s:
āpanaḥ śośucaditi stutvā madhye divākaraṃ /
yathā muñcati ceṣokāṃ tathā pāpaṃ pramuñcati //
258.d:
आपनः शोशुचदिति स्तुत्वा मध्ये दिवाकरं /
यथा मुञ्चति चेषोकां तथा पापं प्रमुञ्चति //
258.m: Having praised the sun at midday with “apa naḥ śośucat,” / just as [the reed] sheds its stalk, so he sheds sin.

258.s:
jātavedasa ity etajjapet svastyayanaṃ pathi /
bhayair vimucyate sarvaiḥ svastimānāpnuyāt gṛhān //
258.d:
जातवेदस इत्य् एतज्जपेत् स्वस्त्ययनं पथि /
भयैर् विमुच्यते सर्वैः स्वस्तिमानाप्नुयात् गृहान् //
258.m: He should recite the auspicious [verse] “jātavedase” on a journey; / he is freed from all fears and reaches home safe and sound.

258.s:
vyuṣṭāyāñca tathā rātryāmetadduḥsvapnanāśanaṃ /
pramandineti sūyantyā japedgarbhavimocanaṃ //
258.d:
व्युष्टायाञ्च तथा रात्र्यामेतद्दुःस्वप्ननाशनं /
प्रमन्दिनेति सूयन्त्या जपेद्गर्भविमोचनं //
258.m: And at dawn of day, this destroys nightmares. / For a woman in labour, one should recite “pramandinaḥ” to release the fetus.

258.s:
japannindramiti snāto vaiśyadevantu saptakaṃ /
muñcatyājyaṃ tathā juhvat sakalaṃ kilviṣaṃ naraḥ //
258.d:
जपन्निन्द्रमिति स्नातो वैश्यदेवन्तु सप्तकं /
मुञ्चत्याज्यं तथा जुह्वत् सकलं किल्विषं नरः //
258.m: Bathed and reciting “indram,” the set of seven verses addressed to the Viśvedevas, / and likewise offering clarified butter into the fire, a man casts off all sin.

258.s:
imāmiti japan śaśvat kāmānāpnotyabhīpsitān /
mānastoka iti dvābhyāṃ trirātropoṣitaḥ śuciḥ //
258.d:
इमामिति जपन् शश्वत् कामानाप्नोत्यभीप्सितान् /
मानस्तोक इति द्वाभ्यां त्रिरात्रोपोषितः शुचिः //
258.m: Constantly reciting “imām,” he obtains desired wishes. / Pure, having fasted for three nights, with the two verses beginning with “mā nas toke,”

258.s:
auḍumbarīś ca juhuyātsamidhaścājyasaṃskṛtāḥ /
chittvā sarvānmṛtyupāśān jīvedrogavivarjitaḥ //
258.d:
औडुम्बरीश् च जुहुयात्समिधश्चाज्यसंस्कृताः /
छित्त्वा सर्वान्मृत्युपाशान् जीवेद्रोगविवर्जितः //
258.m: he should offer faggots of *udumbara* wood prepared with clarified butter; / having cut through all the nooses of death, he lives free from disease.

258.s:
ūrdhvabāhuranenaiva stutvā sambhuṃ tathaiva ca /
mānastoketi ca ṛcā śikhābandhe kṛte naraḥ //
258.d:
ऊर्ध्वबाहुरनेनैव स्तुत्वा सम्भुं तथैव च /
मानस्तोकेति च ऋचा शिखाबन्धे कृते नरः //
258.m: With raised arms, having praised Sambhu with this very [hymn], / and when the tying of the topknot is performed with the verse “mā nas toke,” a man

258.s:
aghṛṣyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ jāyate saṃśayaṃ vinā /
:p 440
citramityupatiṣṭheta trisandhyaṃ bhāskaraṃ tathā //
258.d:
अघृष्यः सर्वभूतानां जायते संशयं विना /
:प् 440
चित्रमित्युपतिष्ठेत त्रिसन्ध्यं भास्करं तथा //
258.m:
becomes unassailable by all beings, without a doubt.
[p. 440]
He should worship the sun at the three junctures of the day with the verse “citram.”

258.s:
samitpāṇirnaro nityamīpsitaṃ dhanamāpnuyāt /
atha svapneti ca japan prātarmadhyandine dine //
258.d:
समित्पाणिर्नरो नित्यमीप्सितं धनमाप्नुयात् /
अथ स्वप्नेति च जपन् प्रातर्मध्यन्दिने दिने //
258.m: With sacrificial faggots in hand, a man constantly obtains desired wealth. / And reciting “atha svapna,” in the morning and at midday every day,

258.s:
duḥsvapnañcārhate kṛtsnaṃ bhojanañcāpnuyācchubham(1) /
ubhe pumāniti tathā rakṣoghnaḥ parikīrtitaḥ //
258.d:
दुःस्वप्नञ्चार्हते कृत्स्नं भोजनञ्चाप्नुयाच्छुभम्(1) /
उभे पुमानिति तथा रक्षोघ्नः परिकीर्तितः //
258.m: he destroys every bad dream and obtains wholesome food. / Likewise, the verse “ubhe pumān” is declared to be a destroyer of demons.

258.s:
ubhe vāsā iti ṛco japan kāmānavāpnuyāt /
na sāganniti ca japan mucyate cātatāyinaḥ //
258.d:
उभे वासा इति ऋचो जपन् कामानवाप्नुयात् /
न सागन्निति च जपन् मुच्यते चाततायिनः //
258.m: Reciting the verses beginning with “ubhe vāsaḥ,” he obtains desires. / And reciting “na sā gāt,” he is released from an assailant.

258.s:
kayā śubheti ca japan jātiśraiṣṭhamavāpnuyāt /
imannṛsomamityetat sarvān kāmānavāpnuyāt //
258.d:
कया शुभेति च जपन् जातिश्रैष्ठमवाप्नुयात् /
इमन्नृसोममित्येतत् सर्वान् कामानवाप्नुयात् //
258.m: Reciting “kayā śubhā,” he attains pre-eminence in his caste. / With this verse “iman nu somam,” he attains all desires.

258.s:
pitarityupatiṣṭheta nityamarthamupasthitaṃ(2) /
agne nayeti sūktena ghṛtahomaś ca mārgagaḥ //
258.d:
पितरित्युपतिष्ठेत नित्यमर्थमुपस्थितं(2) /
अग्ने नयेति सूक्तेन घृतहोमश् च मार्गगः //
258.m: With “pitaḥ,” he should constantly attend upon wealth that has arrived. / With the hymn “agne naya,” an oblation of clarified butter is made by one on a journey.

258.s:
vīrānnayamavāpnoti suślokaṃ yo japet sadā /
kaṅkato neti sūktena viṣān sarvān vyapohati //
258.d:
वीरान्नयमवाप्नोति सुश्लोकं यो जपेत् सदा /
कङ्कतो नेति सूक्तेन विषान् सर्वान् व्यपोहति //
258.m: He who constantly recites the well-known verse obtains the leading of heroes. / With the hymn “kaṅkato na,” he expels all poisons.

258.s:
yo jāta iti sūktena sarvān kāmānavāpnuyāt /
gaṇānāmiti sūktena śnigdhamāpnotyanuttamaṃ //
258.d:
यो जात इति सूक्तेन सर्वान् कामानवाप्नुयात् /
गणानामिति सूक्तेन श्निग्धमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमं //
258.m: With the hymn “yo jātaḥ,” he attains all desires. / With the hymn “gaṇānām,” he obtains unequalled affection.

258.s:
yo me rājannitīmāntu duḥsvapnaśamanīmṛcaṃ /
adhvani prasthito yastu paśyecchatrūṃ samutthitaṃ //
258.d:
यो मे राजन्नितीमान्तु दुःस्वप्नशमनीमृचं /
अध्वनि प्रस्थितो यस्तु पश्येच्छत्रूं समुत्थितं //
258.m: The verse “yo me rājan” pacifies nightmares. / When one who has set out on a journey sees enemies arise,

258.s:
apraśastaṃ praśastaṃ vā kuvidaṅga imaṃ japet /
dvāviṃśakaṃ japan sūktamādhyātmikamanuttamaṃ //
258.d:
अप्रशस्तं प्रशस्तं वा कुविदङ्ग इमं जपेत् /
द्वाविंशकं जपन् सूक्तमाध्यात्मिकमनुत्तमं //
258.m: whether unpropitious or propitious, he should recite this verse “kuvid aṅga.” / Reciting the twenty-second spiritual hymn, which is unequalled,

258.s:
parvasu prayato nityamiṣṭān kāmān samaśnute /
kṛṇuṣveti japan sūktaṃ juhvadājyaṃ samāhitaḥ //
:n
1 bhojanañcāpnuyācchatamiti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ja.. ca
2 nityamannamupasthitamiti ka.. , cha.. ca
:p 441
258.d:
पर्वसु प्रयतो नित्यमिष्टान् कामान् समश्नुते /
कृणुष्वेति जपन् सूक्तं जुह्वदाज्यं समाहितः //
:न्
1 भोजनञ्चाप्नुयाच्छतमिति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ज.. च
2 नित्यमन्नमुपस्थितमिति क.. , छ.. च
:प् 441
258.m:
restrained on new- and full-moon days, he constantly attains cherished desires. / Reciting the hymn “kṛṇuṣva,” offering clarified butter with concentrated mind,
[Footnote]
1 [Variant reading:] “bhojanañcāpnuyācchatam” according to kha, ga, gha, and ja.
2 [Variant reading:] “nityamannamupasthitam” according to ka and cha. / [p. 441]

258.s:
ārātīnāṃ haret prāṇān rakṣāṃsyapi vināśayet /
upatiṣṭhet svayaṃ vahniṃ parityṛcā dine dine //
258.d:
आरातीनां हरेत् प्राणान् रक्षांस्यपि विनाशयेत् /
उपतिष्ठेत् स्वयं वह्निं परित्यृचा दिने दिने //
258.m: he takes away the lives of his enemies and also destroys demons. / He should himself worship fire day after day with the verse “pari.”

258.s:
taṃ rakṣati svayaṃ vahnirviśvato viśvatomukhaḥ /
haṃsaḥ śuciḥ sadityetacchucirīkṣeddivākaraṃ //
258.d:
तं रक्षति स्वयं वह्निर्विश्वतो विश्वतोमुखः /
हंसः शुचिः सदित्येतच्छुचिरीक्षेद्दिवाकरं //
258.m: Fire himself, facing in all directions, protects him on every side. / Pure, he should gaze at the sun with this verse: “haṃsaḥ śucisad.”

258.s:
kṛṣiṃ prapadyamānastu sthālīpākaṃ yathāvidhi /
juhuyāt kṣetramadhye tu svanīsvāhāstu pañcabhiḥ //
258.d:
कृषिं प्रपद्यमानस्तु स्थालीपाकं यथाविधि /
जुहुयात् क्षेत्रमध्ये तु स्वनीस्वाहास्तु पञ्चभिः //
258.m: Undertaking agriculture, he should offer a cooked domestic oblation according to rule / in the middle of the field with the five mantras ending in “svanīsvāhā”:

258.s:
indrāya ca marudbhyastu parjanyāya bhagāya ca /
yathāliṅgantu viharellāṅgalantu kṛṣībalaḥ //
258.d:
इन्द्राय च मरुद्भ्यस्तु पर्जन्याय भगाय च /
यथालिङ्गन्तु विहरेल्लाङ्गलन्तु कृषीबलः //
258.m: to Indra, the Maruts, Parjanya, and Bhaga. / The farmer should drive the plough according to the textual indications;

258.s:
yukto dhānyāya sītāyai sunāsīramathottaraṃ /
gandhamālyair namaskārair yajedetāś ca devatāḥ //
258.d:
युक्तो धान्याय सीतायै सुनासीरमथोत्तरं /
गन्धमाल्यैर् नमस्कारैर् यजेदेताश् च देवताः //
258.m: yoked, he should worship these deities with perfumes, garlands, and obeisances / for grain, Sītā, and then Sunāsīra afterwards.

258.s:
pravāpane pralavane khalasītāpahārayoḥ /
amoghaṅkarma bhavati vardhate sarvadā kṛṣiḥ //
258.d:
प्रवापने प्रलवने खलसीतापहारयोः /
अमोघङ्कर्म भवति वर्धते सर्वदा कृषिः //
258.m: At the sowing, reaping, and gathering at the threshing floor and furrow, / the rite becomes fruitful and agriculture always thrives.

258.s:
samudrāditi sūktena kāmānāpnoti pāvakāt /
viśvānara iti dvābhyāṃ ya ṛgbhyāṃ vahnimarhati //
258.d:
समुद्रादिति सूक्तेन कामानाप्नोति पावकात् /
विश्वानर इति द्वाभ्यां य ऋग्भ्यां वह्निमर्हति //
258.m: With the hymn “samudrāt,” he attains desires from the fire. / He who worships the fire with the two verses beginning with “viśvānara”

258.s:
sa taratyāpadaḥ sarvā yaśaḥ prāpnoti cākṣayaṃ /
vipulāṃ śriyamāpnoti jayaṃ prāpnotyanuttamaṃ //
258.d:
स तरत्यापदः सर्वा यशः प्राप्नोति चाक्षयं /
विपुलां श्रियमाप्नोति जयं प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमं //
258.m: crosses over all misfortunes and attains imperishable fame; / he obtains vast prosperity and attains unequalled victory.

258.s:
agne tvamiti ca stutvā dhanamāpnoti vāñchitaṃ /
prajākāmo japennityaṃ varuṇadaivatatrayaṃ //
258.d:
अग्ने त्वमिति च स्तुत्वा धनमाप्नोति वाञ्छितं /
प्रजाकामो जपेन्नित्यं वरुणदैवतत्रयं //
258.m: Having praised [Agni] with “agne tvam,” he obtains desired wealth. / Desiring offspring, he should constantly recite the triad addressed to Varuṇa.

258.s:
svastyā trayaṃ japet prātaḥ sadā svastyayanaṃ mahat /
svasti panthā iti procya svastimān vrajate 'dhvani //
258.d:
स्वस्त्या त्रयं जपेत् प्रातः सदा स्वस्त्ययनं महत् /
स्वस्ति पन्था इति प्रोच्य स्वस्तिमान् व्रजते ऽध्वनि //
258.m: He should recite the auspicious triad in the morning, always a great protection. / Having uttered “svasti panthāḥ,” he travels safely on the road.

258.s:
vijigīṣurvanaspate śatrūṇāṃ vyādhitaṃ bhavet(1) /
striyā garbhapramūḍhāyā garbhamokṣaṇamuttamaṃ //
:n
1 vyādhikambhavaditi ṭa..
:p 442
258.d:
विजिगीषुर्वनस्पते शत्रूणां व्याधितं भवेत्(1) /
स्त्रिया गर्भप्रमूढाया गर्भमोक्षणमुत्तमं //
:न्
1 व्याधिकम्भवदिति ट..
:प् 442
258.m:
Wishing to conquer, with “vanaspate,” enemies become afflicted with disease. / It is the best release of the fetus for a woman whose labor is obstructed.
[Footnote]
1 [Variant reading:] “vyādhikambhavat” according to ṭa. / [p. 442]

258.s:
acchāvadeti sūktañca vṛṣṭikāmaḥ prayiojayet /
nirāhāraḥ klinnavāsā na cireṇa pravarṣati //
258.d:
अच्छावदेति सूक्तञ्च वृष्टिकामः प्रयिओजयेत् /
निराहारः क्लिन्नवासा न चिरेण प्रवर्षति //
258.m: One desiring rain should employ the hymn “acchā vada”; / fasting and with wet clothes, it rains before long.

258.s:
manasaḥ kāma ity etāṃ paśukāmo naro japet /
kardamena iti snāyātprajākāmaḥ śucivrataḥ //
258.d:
मनसः काम इत्य् एतां पशुकामो नरो जपेत् /
कर्दमेन इति स्नायात्प्रजाकामः शुचिव्रतः //
258.m: A man desiring cattle should recite the verse “manasaḥ kāmaḥ.” / Desiring offspring, pure in observance, he should bathe with “kardamena.”

258.s:
aśvapūrvā iti snāyādrājyakāmastu mānavaḥ /
rāhite carmaṇi snāyāt brāhmaṇastu yathāvidhi //
258.d:
अश्वपूर्वा इति स्नायाद्राज्यकामस्तु मानवः /
राहिते चर्मणि स्नायात् ब्राह्मणस्तु यथाविधि //
258.m: A man desiring kingship should bathe with “aśvapūrvām.” / A brāhmaṇa should bathe according to rule on a red hide,

258.s:
rājā carmaṇi vaiyāghre chāge vaiśyastathaiva ca /
daśasāhasriko homaḥ pratyekaṃ parikīrtitaḥ //
258.d:
राजा चर्मणि वैयाघ्रे छागे वैश्यस्तथैव च /
दशसाहस्रिको होमः प्रत्येकं परिकीर्तितः //
258.m: a king on a tiger's skin, and a vaiśya likewise on a goat's skin. / A fire oblation of ten thousand offerings is prescribed for each.

258.s:
āgāra iti sūktena goṣṭhe gāṃ lokamātaraṃ /
upatiṣṭhedvrajeccaiva yadicchettāḥ sadākṣayāḥ //
258.d:
आगार इति सूक्तेन गोष्ठे गां लोकमातरं /
उपतिष्ठेद्व्रजेच्चैव यदिच्छेत्ताः सदाक्षयाः //
258.m: With the hymn “āgāraḥ,” he should approach and attend upon a cow, the mother of the world, / in the cow-pen, if he wishes them to be ever imperishable.

258.s:
upetitisṛbhīrājño dundubhimabhimantrayet /
tejo bakañca prāpnoti śatruñcaiva niyacchati //
258.d:
उपेतितिसृभीराज्ञो दुन्दुभिमभिमन्त्रयेत् /
तेजो बकञ्च प्राप्नोति शत्रुञ्चैव नियच्छति //
258.m: With the three verses beginning with “upeta,” he should consecrate the king's war-drum; / he attains splendour and strength, and he restrains the enemy.

258.s:
tṛṇapāṇirjapetsūktuṃ rakṣoghnaṃ dasyunbhirvṛtaḥ /
ye ke ca umetyṛcaṃ japtvā dīrghamāyurāpnuyāt(1) //
258.d:
तृणपाणिर्जपेत्सूक्तुं रक्षोघ्नं दस्युन्भिर्वृतः /
ये के च उमेत्यृचं जप्त्वा दीर्घमायुराप्नुयात्(1) //
258.m: Holding grass in hand, surrounded by bandits, he should recite the demon-slaying hymn. / Having recited the verse “ye ke ca uma,” he attains long life.

258.s:
jīmūtasūktena tathā senāṅgānyabhimantrayet /
yadhā liṅgaṃ tato rājā vinihanti raṇe ripūn //
258.d:
जीमूतसूक्तेन तथा सेनाङ्गान्यभिमन्त्रयेत् /
यधा लिङ्गं ततो राजा विनिहन्ति रणे रिपून् //
258.m: Likewise, he should consecrate the divisions of the army with the Jīmūta hymn; / according to the textual indications, the king then slays enemies in battle.

258.s:
āgneyeti tribhiḥsūktair dhanamāpnoti cākṣayaṃ /
amīvaheti sūktena bhūtāni sthāpayenniśi //
258.d:
आग्नेयेति त्रिभिःसूक्तैर् धनमाप्नोति चाक्षयं /
अमीवहेति सूक्तेन भूतानि स्थापयेन्निशि //
258.m: With the three hymns addressed to Agni, he attains imperishable wealth. / With the hymn “amīvahā,” he should quiet spirits at night.

258.s:
sabādhe viṣame durge bandhā vā nirgataḥ kvacit /
palāyan vā gṛhīto vā sūktametattathā japet //
258.d:
सबाधे विषमे दुर्गे बन्धा वा निर्गतः क्वचित् /
पलायन् वा गृहीतो वा सूक्तमेतत्तथा जपेत् //
258.m: When distressed, in difficult terrain, in an inaccessible stronghold, or gone forth from captivity anywhere, / fleeing or captured, he should likewise recite this hymn.

258.s:
trirātraṃ niyatopoṣya śrāpayet pāyasañcaruṃ /
tenāhutiśataṃ pūrṇaṃ juhuyāt tryambaketyṛcā //
:n
1 avāptavāniti ṭa..
:p 443
258.d:
त्रिरात्रं नियतोपोष्य श्रापयेत् पायसञ्चरुं /
तेनाहुतिशतं पूर्णं जुहुयात् त्र्यम्बकेत्यृचा //
:न्
1 अवाप्तवानिति ट..
:प् 443
258.m:
Having observed a fast for three nights with restraint, he should cook a boiled rice-milk offering; / with that, he should offer a full hundred oblations with the verse “tryambakam.”
[Footnote]
1 [Variant reading:] “avāptavān” according to ṭa. / [p. 443]

258.s:
samuddiśya mahādevaṃ jīvedabdaśataṃ sukhaṃ /
taccakṣurityṛcā snāta upatiṣṭheddivākaraṃ //
258.d:
समुद्दिश्य महादेवं जीवेदब्दशतं सुखं /
तच्चक्षुरित्यृचा स्नात उपतिष्ठेद्दिवाकरं //
258.m: Addressing Mahādeva, he lives happily for a hundred years. / Bathed, with the verse “tac cakṣuḥ,” he should worship the sun

258.s:
udyantaṃ madhyagañcaiva dīrghamāyurjijīviṣuḥ /
indrā someti sūktantu kathitaṃ śatrunāśanaṃ //
258.d:
उद्यन्तं मध्यगञ्चैव दीर्घमायुर्जिजीविषुः /
इन्द्रा सोमेति सूक्तन्तु कथितं शत्रुनाशनं //
258.m: rising and at the meridian, if he desires to live a long life. / The hymn “indrāsomā” is proclaimed to destroy enemies.

258.s:
yasya luptaṃ vrataṃ mohādvrātyair vā saṃsṛjetsaha /
upoṣyājyaṃ sa juhuyāttvamagne vratapā iti //
258.d:
यस्य लुप्तं व्रतं मोहाद्व्रात्यैर् वा संसृजेत्सह /
उपोष्याज्यं स जुहुयात्त्वमग्ने व्रतपा इति //
258.m: If one's votive observance has lapsed through delusion or if one has associated with outcasts, / having fasted, he should offer clarified butter with the verse, "You, O Agni, are the protector of votive observances" (tvamagne vratapāḥ).

258.s:
ādityetyṛk ca samrājaṃ(1) japtvā vāde jayī bhavet /
mahīti ca catuṣkeṇa mucyate mahato bhayāt //
258.d:
आदित्येत्यृक् च सम्राजं(1) जप्त्वा वादे जयी भवेत् /
महीति च चतुष्केण मुच्यते महतो भयात् //
258.m: Having recited the verse, "O Āditya, [the supreme ruler]" (āditya...), one will be victorious in debate. / And by the quatrain "The great [earth]" (mahī...), one is freed from great danger.

258.s:
ṛcaṃ mahīti japtvā yadi hy etat sarvakāmānavāpnuyāt /
dvācatvāriṃśatiṃ caindraṃ japtvā nāśayate ripūn //
258.d:
ऋचं महीति जप्त्वा यदि ह्य् एतत् सर्वकामानवाप्नुयात् /
द्वाचत्वारिंशतिं चैन्द्रं जप्त्वा नाशयते रिपून् //
258.m: If one recites the verse "The great [earth]" (mahī...), he attains all desires. / And having recited the forty-two verses addressed to Indra, he destroys his enemies.

258.s:
vācaṃ mahīti japtvā ca prāpnotyārogyameva ca /
śanno bhaveti dvābhyāntu bhuktvānnaṃ prayataḥ śuciḥ //
258.d:
वाचं महीति जप्त्वा च प्राप्नोत्यारोग्यमेव च /
शन्नो भवेति द्वाभ्यान्तु भुक्त्वान्नं प्रयतः शुचिः //
258.m: Having recited "The great speech" (vācaṃ mahīm...), one also attains health. / Having eaten food, attentive and pure, with the two verses beginning "May there be peace for us" (śanno bhava...),

258.s:
hṛdayaṃ pāṇinā spṛṣṭvā vyādhibhir nābhibhūyate /
uttamedamiti snāto huttvā śatruṃ pramāpayet //
258.d:
हृदयं पाणिना स्पृष्ट्वा व्याधिभिर् नाभिभूयते /
उत्तमेदमिति स्नातो हुत्त्वा शत्रुं प्रमापयेत् //
