258.m: and touching his heart with his hand, he is not overcome by diseases. / Having bathed and made fire oblations with "This supreme [word]" (uttamedam...), he destroys an enemy.

258.s:
śannogna iti sūktena hutenānnamavāpnuyāt /
kanyā vārarṣisūktena digdoṣādvipramucyate //
258.d:
शन्नोग्न इति सूक्तेन हुतेनान्नमवाप्नुयात् /
कन्या वारर्षिसूक्तेन दिग्दोषाद्विप्रमुच्यते //
258.m: By offering fire oblations with the hymn "May Agni be auspicious to us" (śannognaḥ...), he attains food. / A maiden is completely freed from defects of direction by the hymn of the supreme seer (vārarṣisūkta).

258.s:
yadatya kavyetyudite japte 'vaśyaṃ jagadbhavet /
yadvāgiti ca japtena vāṇī bhavati saṃskṛtā(2) //
258.d:
यदत्य कव्येत्युदिते जप्ते ऽवश्यं जगद्भवेत् /
यद्वागिति च जप्तेन वाणी भवति संस्कृता(2) //
258.m: When the sun has risen, if "Whatever food today..." (yadatya kavya...) is recited, the world will surely come under his control. / Reciting "The speech which..." (yadvāk...), his speech becomes refined.

258.s:
vāco viditamiti tvetāṃ japan vācaṃ samaśnute /
pavitrāṇāṃ pavitrantu pāvamānyetyṛco matāḥ //
258.d:
वाचो विदितमिति त्वेतां जपन् वाचं समश्नुते /
पवित्राणां पवित्रन्तु पावमान्येत्यृचो मताः //
258.m: Reciting this verse, "Known of speech" (vāco viditam...), he masters speech. / The verses of the Pāvamānī hymns are considered the purifier of purifiers.

258.s:
vaikhānasā ṛcastriṃśatpavitrāḥ paramā matāḥ /
:n
1 ādityeti prasaṃmrājamiti ga.. , gha.. , ña..
2 saṃsthiteti ka.. , cha.. , ca..
:p 444
ṛco dviṣaṣṭiḥ proktāś ca parasvetyṛṣisattama //
258.d:
वैखानसा ऋचस्त्रिंशत्पवित्राः परमा मताः /
:न्
1 आदित्येति प्रसंम्राजमिति ग.. , घ.. , ञ..
2 संस्थितेति क.. , छ.. , च..
:प् 444
ऋचो द्विषष्टिः प्रोक्ताश् च परस्वेत्यृषिसत्तम //
258.m:
The thirty Vaikhānasa verses are considered supremely purifying.
[Footnote]
1 [variant reading in manuscripts ga, gha, ña: ādityeti prasaṃmrājam]
2 [variant reading in manuscripts ka, cha, ca: saṃsthitā]
[page 444]
Sixty-two verses are declared [beginning with] "Purify..." (parasva...), O best of seers,

258.s:
sarvakalmaṣanāśāya pāvanāya śivāya ca /
svādiṣṭayetisūktānāṃ saptaṣaṣṭirudāhṛtā //
258.d:
सर्वकल्मषनाशाय पावनाय शिवाय च /
स्वादिष्टयेतिसूक्तानां सप्तषष्टिरुदाहृता //
258.m: for the destruction of all sins, for purification, and for auspiciousness. / Sixty-seven hymns beginning with "The sweetest..." (svādiṣṭhayā...) are taught.

258.s:
daśottarāṇyṛcāñcaitāḥ pāvamānyaḥ śatāni ṣaṭ /
etajjapaṃś ca juhvacca ghoraṃ mṛtyubhayaṃ jayet //
258.d:
दशोत्तराण्यृचाञ्चैताः पावमान्यः शतानि षट् /
एतज्जपंश् च जुह्वच्च घोरं मृत्युभयं जयेत् //
258.m: These Pāvamānī verses number six hundred and ten. / Reciting this and offering fire oblations, one conquers the terrifying fear of death.

258.s:
āpohiṣṭeti vāristho japetpāpabhayārdane /
pradevanneti niyato japecca marudhanvasu //
258.d:
आपोहिष्टेति वारिस्थो जपेत्पापभयार्दने /
प्रदेवन्नेति नियतो जपेच्च मरुधन्वसु //
258.m: Standing in water, one should recite "Waters indeed are..." (āpo hi ṣṭhā...) when afflicted by fear of sin. / Restrained, one should recite "Not playing..." (pradevann...) in a waterless desert.

258.s:
prāṇāntike bhaye prāpte kṣipramāyustu vindati /
prāveyāmityṛcamekāṃ japecca manasā niśi //
258.d:
प्राणान्तिके भये प्राप्ते क्षिप्रमायुस्तु विन्दति /
प्रावेयामित्यृचमेकां जपेच्च मनसा निशि //
258.m: When a life-threatening danger has arrived, he swiftly finds life. / One should recite mentally at night the single verse "May I enter..." (prāveyām...).

258.s:
vyuṣṭāyāmudite sūrye dyūte jayamavāpnuyāt /
mā pragāmeti mūḍhaś ca panthānaṃ pathi vindati //
258.d:
व्युष्टायामुदिते सूर्ये द्यूते जयमवाप्नुयात् /
मा प्रगामेति मूढश् च पन्थानं पथि विन्दति //
258.m: At dawn, when the sun has risen, he obtains victory in gambling. / And a bewildered person finds the path on a journey with "May we not wander..." (mā pragāma...).

258.s:
kṣīṇāyuriti manyeta yaṅkañcit suhṛdaṃ priyaṃ /
yatteyamiti tu snātastasya mūrdhānamālabhet //
258.d:
क्षीणायुरिति मन्येत यङ्कञ्चित् सुहृदं प्रियं /
यत्तेयमिति तु स्नातस्तस्य मूर्धानमालभेत् //
258.m: If he thinks any dear friend to have a depleted life span, / having bathed, he should touch his head with "That of yours..." (yatteyam...).

258.s:
sahasrakṛtvaḥ pañcāhaṃ tenāyurvindate mahat /
idaṃ medhyeti juhuyāt ghṛtaṃ prājñaḥ sahasraśaḥ //
258.d:
सहस्रकृत्वः पञ्चाहं तेनायुर्विन्दते महत् /
इदं मेध्येति जुहुयात् घृतं प्राज्ञः सहस्रशः //
258.m: He should do this a thousand times for five days; through that [friend] attains a long life. / A wise man should offer clarified butter thousands of times with "This sacrificial..." (idaṃ medhya...).

258.s:
paśukāmo gavāṃ goṣṭhe arthakāmaś catuṣpathe /
vayaḥ suparṇa ity etāṃ japan vai vindate śriyaṃ //
258.d:
पशुकामो गवां गोष्ठे अर्थकामश् चतुष्पथे /
वयः सुपर्ण इत्य् एतां जपन् वै विन्दते श्रियं //
258.m: Desiring cattle, [he should offer] in a cowpen; desiring wealth, at a crossroads. / Reciting "The fair-winged bird" (vayaḥ suparṇaḥ...), he indeed attains fortune.

258.s:
haviṣyantīyamabhyasya sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate /
tasya rogā vinaśyanti kāyāgnirvardhate tathā //
258.d:
हविष्यन्तीयमभ्यस्य सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते /
तस्य रोगा विनश्यन्ति कायाग्निर्वर्धते तथा //
258.m: Practicing the recitation of the Haviṣyantī verse, he is freed from all sins; / his diseases perish, and his digestive fire increases.

258.s:
yā oṣadhayaḥ svastyayanaṃ sarvavyādhivināśanaṃ /
vṛhaspate atītyetadvṛṣṭikāmaḥ prayojayet //
258.d:
या ओषधयः स्वस्त्ययनं सर्वव्याधिविनाशनं /
वृहस्पते अतीत्येतद्वृष्टिकामः प्रयोजयेत् //
258.m: "The herbs which..." (yā oṣadhayaḥ...) is an auspicious rite that destroys all diseases. / Desiring rain, one should employ "O Bṛhaspati, surpassing..." (vṛhaspate ati...).

258.s:
sarvatreti parā śāntirjñeyā pratirathas tathā /
sūta sāṃkāśyapannityaṃ prajākāmasya kīrtitaṃ //
:p 445
258.d:
सर्वत्रेति परा शान्तिर्ज्ञेया प्रतिरथस् तथा /
सूत सांकाश्यपन्नित्यं प्रजाकामस्य कीर्तितं //
:प् 445
258.m:
"Everywhere..." (sarvatra...) should be known as supreme pacification, and likewise the Pratiratha hymn. / Sūta, the Sāṃkāśyapa hymn is declared for one who always desires offspring.
[page 445]

258.s:
ahaṃ rudreti etadvāgmī bhavati mānavaḥ /
na yonau jāyate vidvān japanrātrīti rātriṣu //
258.d:
अहं रुद्रेति एतद्वाग्मी भवति मानवः /
न योनौ जायते विद्वान् जपन्रात्रीति रात्रिषु //
258.m: With "I, through the Rudras..." (ahaṃ rudrebhiḥ...), a man becomes eloquent. / Reciting "O night..." (rātri...) during the nights, the wise man is not reborn in a womb.

258.s:
rātrisūktaṃ japannrātrī rātriṃ kṣemī jayennaraḥ /
kalpayantīti ca japannityaṃ kṛttvārināśanaṃ //
258.d:
रात्रिसूक्तं जपन्न्रात्री रात्रिं क्षेमी जयेन्नरः /
कल्पयन्तीति च जपन्नित्यं कृत्त्वारिनाशनं //
258.m: Reciting the Rātrisūkta at night, a man securely overcomes the night. / Reciting "They fashion..." (kalpayanti...) daily, he brings about the destruction of enemies.

258.s:
āyuṣyañcaiva varcasyaṃ sūktaṃ dākṣāyaṇaṃ mahat /
uta devā iti japedāmayaghnaṃ dhṛtavrataḥ //
258.d:
आयुष्यञ्चैव वर्चस्यं सूक्तं दाक्षायणं महत् /
उत देवा इति जपेदामयघ्नं धृतव्रतः //
258.m: The great Dākṣāyaṇa hymn brings longevity and spiritual lustre. / Steadfast in his vow, he should recite "Even the gods..." (uta devāḥ...) to destroy disease.

258.s:
ayamagne janityetajjapedagnibhaye sati /
araṇyānītyaraṇyeṣu japettadbhayanāśanaṃ //
258.d:
अयमग्ने जनित्येतज्जपेदग्निभये सति /
अरण्यानीत्यरण्येषु जपेत्तद्भयनाशनं //
258.m: When there is fear of fire, he should recite "This, O Agni, birth..." (ayamagne janī...). / In forests, he should recite "O Araṇyānī..." (araṇyāni...) to destroy fear thereof.

258.s:
brāhmnīmāsādya sūkte dve ṛcaṃ brāhmīṃ śatāvarīṃ /
pṛthagadbhirghṛtair vātha medhāṃ lakṣmīñca vindati //
258.d:
ब्राह्म्नीमासाद्य सूक्ते द्वे ऋचं ब्राह्मीं शतावरीं /
पृथगद्भिर्घृतैर् वाथ मेधां लक्ष्मीञ्च विन्दति //
258.m: Having approached the Brāhmī plant, reciting the two hymns, the Brāhmī verse, and the Śatāvarī plant, / respectively with water or clarified butter, he attains intellect and fortune.

258.s:
māsa ity asapatnaghnaṃ saṃgrāmaṃ vijigīṣataḥ /
brahmaṇo 'gniḥ saṃvidānaṃ garbhamṛtyunivāraṇaṃ //
258.d:
मास इत्य् असपत्नघ्नं संग्रामं विजिगीषतः /
ब्रह्मणो ऽग्निः संविदानं गर्भमृत्युनिवारणं //
258.m: "A month..." (māsaḥ...) destroys enemies for one desiring victory in battle. / "Agni of the Creator in agreement..." (brahmaṇo 'gniḥ saṃvidānaḥ...) averts death in the womb.

258.s:
apahīti japetsūktaṃ śucirdusvapnanāśanaṃ /
yenedamiti vaijaptvā samādhiṃ vindate paraṃ //
258.d:
अपहीति जपेत्सूक्तं शुचिर्दुस्वप्ननाशनं /
येनेदमिति वैजप्त्वा समाधिं विन्दते परं //
258.m: Pure, he should recite the hymn "Drive away..." (apahi...) to destroy bad dreams. / Having recited "By which this..." (yenedam...), he indeed attains supreme absorption.

258.s:
mayo bhūrvāta ity etat gavāṃ svastyayanaṃ paraṃ /
śāmbarīmindrajālaṃ vā māyāmetena vārayet //
258.d:
मयो भूर्वात इत्य् एतत् गवां स्वस्त्ययनं परं /
शाम्बरीमिन्द्रजालं वा मायामेतेन वारयेत् //
258.m: "May the wind be healing..." (mayobhūr vātaḥ...) is the supreme blessing for cattle. / By this one averts sorcery, magic tricks, or illusion.

258.s:
mahītrīṇāmavarostviti pathi svastyayanaṃ japet /
agnaye vidviṣannevaṃ japecca ripunāśanaṃ //
258.d:
महीत्रीणामवरोस्त्विति पथि स्वस्त्ययनं जपेत् /
अग्नये विद्विषन्नेवं जपेच्च रिपुनाशनं //
258.m: One should recite on a journey for safe travel: "May the lowest of the great three..." (mahī trīṇām avaro 'stu...). / Likewise, reciting "Hostile to Agni..." (agnaye vidviṣan...), one destroys enemies.

258.s:
vāstoṣpatena mantreṇa yajeta gṛhadevatāḥ /
japasyaiṣa vidhiḥ prokto hute jñeyo viśeṣataḥ //
258.d:
वास्तोष्पतेन मन्त्रेण यजेत गृहदेवताः /
जपस्यैष विधिः प्रोक्तो हुते ज्ञेयो विशेषतः //
258.m: One should worship the deities of the house with the hymn to Vāstoṣpati. / This rule has been declared for recitation; it should especially be understood for fire oblations.

258.s:
homānte dakṣiṇā deyā pāpaśāntirhutena tu /
hutaṃ śāmyati cānnena annahemapradānataḥ //
258.d:
होमान्ते दक्षिणा देया पापशान्तिर्हुतेन तु /
हुतं शाम्यति चान्नेन अन्नहेमप्रदानतः //
258.m: At the conclusion of a fire oblation, a sacrificial fee should be given; pacification of sin comes through fire oblation. / And the fire oblation is pacified by food, through the gift of food and gold.

258.s:
viprāśiṣastvamoghāḥ syurbahiḥsnānantu sarvataḥ /
:p 446
siddhārthakā yavā dhānyaṃ payo ghṛtaṃ tathā //
258.d:
विप्राशिषस्त्वमोघाः स्युर्बहिःस्नानन्तु सर्वतः /
:प् 446
सिद्धार्थका यवा धान्यं पयो घृतं तथा //
258.m:
The blessings of brāhmaṇas are infallible; and bathing outside everywhere [is effective].
[page 446]
White mustard seeds, barley, grain, milk, and clarified butter,

258.s:
kṣīravṛkṣāstathedhmantu homā vai sarvakāmadāḥ /
samidhaḥ kaṇṭhakinyaś ca rājikā rudhiraṃ viṣaṃ //
258.d:
क्षीरवृक्षास्तथेध्मन्तु होमा वै सर्वकामदाः /
समिधः कण्ठकिन्यश् च राजिका रुधिरं विषं //
258.m: milky trees as firewood—these fire oblations grant all desires. / Thorny fuel-sticks, black mustard, blood, poison,

258.s:
abhicāre tathā śailaṃ aśanaṃ śaktavaḥ payaḥ /
dadhi bhaikṣyaṃ phalaṃ mūlamṛgvidhānamudāhṛtaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe ṛgvidhānaṃ
nāmāṣṭapañcāśadadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athonaṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
yajurvidhānaṃ
258.d:
अभिचारे तथा शैलं अशनं शक्तवः पयः /
दधि भैक्ष्यं फलं मूलमृग्विधानमुदाहृतं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे ऋग्विधानं
नामाष्टपञ्चाशदधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथोनषष्ट्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
यजुर्विधानं
258.m:
and likewise rock [salt] in sorcery. Food, roasted barley flour, milk, / curd, alms-food, fruit, and roots [are the offerings]. Thus the Ṛgvidhāna has been declared.
Thus in the great Agni Purāṇa, the two hundred and fifty-eighth chapter, entitled "The Application of Ṛgveda Mantras" (Ṛgvidhāna).
Now, the two hundred and fifty-ninth chapter:
The Application of Yajurveda Mantras (Yajurvidhāna)

259.s:
puṣkara uvāca
yajurvidhānaṃ vakṣyāmi bhuktimuktipradaṃ śṛṇu /
oṃkārapūrvikā rāma mahāvyāhṛtayo matāḥ //
259.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
यजुर्विधानं वक्ष्यामि भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदं शृणु /
ओंकारपूर्विका राम महाव्याहृतयो मताः //
259.m: Puṣkara said: / I will proclaim the application of the Yajurveda, which bestows worldly enjoyment and liberation; listen, O Rāma. / The great mystical utterances preceded by the syllable Om are considered

259.s:
sarvakalmaṣanāśinyaḥ sarvakāmapradās tathā /
ājyāhutisahasreṇa devānārādhayedbudhaḥ //
259.d:
सर्वकल्मषनाशिन्यः सर्वकामप्रदास् तथा /
आज्याहुतिसहस्रेण देवानाराधयेद्बुधः //
259.m: destroyers of all sins and bestowers of all desires. / A wise man should propitiate the gods with a thousand oblations of clarified butter.

259.s:
manasaḥ kāṅkṣitaṃ rāma manasepsitakāmadaṃ /
śāntikāmo yavaiḥ kuryāttilaiḥ pāpāpanuttaye //
259.d:
मनसः काङ्क्षितं राम मनसेप्सितकामदं /
शान्तिकामो यवैः कुर्यात्तिलैः पापापनुत्तये //
259.m: It grants what is desired in the mind, O Rāma, fulfilling whatever is wished by the mind. / Desiring peace, he should do so with barley; with sesame seeds, for the removal of sin;

259.s:
dhānyaiḥ siddhārthakaiś caiva sarvakāma karais tathā /
audumbarībhiridhmābhiḥ pasukāmasya śasyate //
259.d:
धान्यैः सिद्धार्थकैश् चैव सर्वकाम करैस् तथा /
औदुम्बरीभिरिध्माभिः पसुकामस्य शस्यते //
259.m: and with grains and white mustard seeds, which fulfill all desires. / With firewood from the udumbara tree, it is praised for one desiring cattle;

259.s:
dadhnā caivānnakāmasya payasā śāntimicchataḥ /
apāmārgasamiddhastu kāmayan kanakaṃ bahu //
:p 447
259.d:
दध्ना चैवान्नकामस्य पयसा शान्तिमिच्छतः /
अपामार्गसमिद्धस्तु कामयन् कनकं बहु //
:प् 447
259.m:
with curd for one desiring food; with milk for one desiring peace; / with fuel-sticks of apāmārga for one desiring much gold.
[page 447]

259.s:
kanyākāmo ghṛtāktāni yugmaśo grathitāni tu /
jātīpuṣpāṇi juhuyādgrāmārthī tilataṇḍulān //
259.d:
कन्याकामो घृताक्तानि युग्मशो ग्रथितानि तु /
जातीपुष्पाणि जुहुयाद्ग्रामार्थी तिलतण्डुलान् //
259.m: One desiring a maiden should offer jasmine flowers smeared with clarified butter and tied in pairs; / one desiring a village should offer sesame seeds and husked rice.

259.s:
vaśyakarmaṇi śākhoḍhavāsāpāmārgameva ca /
viṣāsṛṅmiśrasamidho vyādhighātasya bhārgava //
259.d:
वश्यकर्मणि शाखोढवासापामार्गमेव च /
विषासृङ्मिश्रसमिधो व्याधिघातस्य भार्गव //
259.m: In rites of subjugation, [he should use] śākhoṭaka, vāsā, and apāmārga; / for the destruction of disease, O descendant of Bhṛgu, [he should offer] fuel-sticks mixed with poison and blood.

259.s:
kruddhastu juhuyātsamyak śatrūṇāṃ badhakāmyayā /
sarvavrīhimayīṃ kṛtvā rājñaḥ pratikṛtiṃ dvija //
259.d:
क्रुद्धस्तु जुहुयात्सम्यक् शत्रूणां बधकाम्यया /
सर्वव्रीहिमयीं कृत्वा राज्ञः प्रतिकृतिं द्विज //
259.m: Enraged, he should offer oblations duly with the desire to kill enemies. / Having made an effigy of a king entirely of rice grain, O twice-born,

259.s:
sahasraśastu juhuyādrājā vaśagato bhavet /
vastrakāmasya puṣpāṇi darvā vyādhivināśinī //
259.d:
सहस्रशस्तु जुहुयाद्राजा वशगतो भवेत् /
वस्त्रकामस्य पुष्पाणि दर्वा व्याधिविनाशिनी //
259.m: he should make oblations thousands of times; the king will come under his power. / Flowers are for one desiring clothing; dūrvā grass destroys diseases.

259.s:
brahmavarcasakāmasya vāsograñca vidhīyate /
pratyaṅgireṣu juhuyāttuṣakaṇṭakabhasmabhiḥ //
259.d:
ब्रह्मवर्चसकामस्य वासोग्रञ्च विधीयते /
प्रत्यङ्गिरेषु जुहुयात्तुषकण्टकभस्मभिः //
259.m: For one desiring spiritual radiance, the hem of a garment is prescribed. / In counter-spells, one should offer with chaff, thorns, and ashes;

259.s:
vidveṣaṇe ca pakṣmāṇi kākakauśikayos tathā /
kāpilañca ghṛtaṃ hutvā tathā candragrahe dvija //
259.d:
विद्वेषणे च पक्ष्माणि काककौशिकयोस् तथा /
कापिलञ्च घृतं हुत्वा तथा चन्द्रग्रहे द्विज //
259.m: and in rites of creating enmity, the feathers of a crow and an owl. / And having offered tawny cow's clarified butter during a lunar eclipse, O twice-born,

259.s:
vacācūrṇena sampātātsamānīya ca tāṃ vacāṃ /
sahasramantritāṃ bhuktvā medhāvī jāyate naraḥ //
259.d:
वचाचूर्णेन सम्पातात्समानीय च तां वचां /
सहस्रमन्त्रितां भुक्त्वा मेधावी जायते नरः //
259.m: Having collected [residual] drops with calamus powder, a man who consumes that calamus, / consecrated with a thousand [mantras], becomes intelligent.

259.s:
ekādaśāṅgulaṃ śaṅku lauhaṃ khādirameva ca(1) /
dviṣato badhosīti japannikhanedripuveśmani //
259.d:
एकादशाङ्गुलं शङ्कु लौहं खादिरमेव च(1) /
द्विषतो बधोसीति जपन्निखनेद्रिपुवेश्मनि //
259.m: Reciting "You are the slayer of the enemy," one should bury in the enemy's house / an eleven-finger peg of iron or indeed of khadira wood.

259.s:
uccāṭanamidaṃ karma śatrūṇāṃ kathitaṃ tava /
cakṣuṣyā iti japtvā ca vinaṣṭañcakṣurāpnuyāt //
259.d:
उच्चाटनमिदं कर्म शत्रूणां कथितं तव /
चक्षुष्या इति जप्त्वा च विनष्टञ्चक्षुराप्नुयात् //
259.m: This rite of eradication (uccāṭana) of enemies has been explained to you. / And having recited the "Cakṣuṣyā" [hymn], one recovers lost sight.

259.s:
upayuñjata ity edanuvākantathānnadaṃ /
tanūnapāgne saditi dūrvāṃ hutvārtivarjitaḥ //
259.d:
उपयुञ्जत इत्य् एदनुवाकन्तथान्नदं /
तनूनपाग्ने सदिति दूर्वां हुत्वार्तिवर्जितः //
259.m: Likewise, the anuvāka [beginning] "They employ" (upayuñjate) grants food. / Offering dūrvā grass with "O fire, child of strength, seated..." (tanūnapāgne sat), one is freed from distress.

259.s:
bheṣajamasīti dadhyājyair homaḥ paśūpasarganut(2) /
:n
1 khādirameva veti ga.. , gha.. , ña.. ca
2 paśūpasargaheti ka.. , cha.. ca
:p 448
tryamvakaṃ yajāmahe homaḥ saubhāgyavardhanaḥ //
259.d:
भेषजमसीति दध्याज्यैर् होमः पशूपसर्गनुत्(2) /
:न्
1 खादिरमेव वेति ग.. , घ.. , ञ.. च
2 पशूपसर्गहेति क.. , छ.. च
:प् 448
त्र्यम्वकं यजामहे होमः सौभाग्यवर्धनः //
259.m:
A fire oblation with curd and clarified butter using "You are medicine" (bheṣajam asi) removes afflictions of cattle.
[Footnote]
1 "khādiram eva vā" in manuscripts ga, gha, and ña.
2 "paśūpasargahā" in manuscripts ka and cha. / [Page 448]
A fire oblation with "We worship Tryambaka" (tryambakaṃ yajāmahe) increases good fortune.

259.s:
kanyānāma gṛhītvā tu kanyalābhakaraḥ paraḥ /
bhayeṣu tu japannityaṃ bhayebhyo vipramucyate //
259.d:
कन्यानाम गृहीत्वा तु कन्यलाभकरः परः /
भयेषु तु जपन्नित्यं भयेभ्यो विप्रमुच्यते //
259.m: Uttering the maiden's name, it is supreme in securing a maiden. / Reciting it constantly in times of danger, one is freed from dangers.

259.s:
dhustūrapuṣpaṃ saghṛtaṃ hutvā syāt sarvakāmabhāk /
hutvā tu guggulaṃ rāma svapne paśyati śaṅkaraṃ //
259.d:
धुस्तूरपुष्पं सघृतं हुत्वा स्यात् सर्वकामभाक् /
हुत्वा तु गुग्गुलं राम स्वप्ने पश्यति शङ्करं //
259.m: Having offered thorn-apple flowers with clarified butter, one attains all desires. / Having offered bdellium (guggulu), O Rāma, one sees Śiva in a dream.

259.s:
yuñjate mano 'nuvākaṃ japtvā dīrghāyurāpnuyāt /
viṣṇoravāṭamityetat(1) sarvabādhāvināśanaṃ //
259.d:
युञ्जते मनो ऽनुवाकं जप्त्वा दीर्घायुराप्नुयात् /
विष्णोरवाटमित्येतत्(1) सर्वबाधाविनाशनं //
259.m: Having recited the anuvāka [beginning] "They harness the mind" (yuñjate manaḥ), one attains long life. / This [mantra], "Viṣṇu's wicker work" (viṣṇor avāṭam), destroys all obstacles.

259.s:
rakṣoghnañca yaśasyañca tathaiva vijayapradaṃ /
ayatno agnirityetat saṃgrāme vijayapradaṃ //
259.d:
रक्षोघ्नञ्च यशस्यञ्च तथैव विजयप्रदं /
अयत्नो अग्निरित्येतत् संग्रामे विजयप्रदं //
259.m: It slays demons, bestows fame, and likewise grants victory. / This [mantra], "Agni without effort" (ayatno agniḥ), grants victory in battle.

259.s:
idamāpaḥ pravahata snāne pāpāpanodanaṃ /
viśvakarmannu haviṣā sūcīṃ lauhīndaśāṅgulām //
259.d:
इदमापः प्रवहत स्नाने पापापनोदनं /
विश्वकर्मन्नु हविषा सूचीं लौहीन्दशाङ्गुलाम् //
259.m: "May these waters carry away" (idam āpaḥ pravahata) dispels sin during bathing. / With "Viśvakarman with the oblation" (viśvakarmann u haviṣā), an iron needle ten fingers long

259.s:
kanyāyā nikhaneddvāri sānyasmai na pradīyate /
deva savitaretena juhuyādbalakāmo dvijottama //
259.d:
कन्याया निखनेद्द्वारि सान्यस्मै न प्रदीयते /
देव सवितरेतेन जुहुयाद्बलकामो द्विजोत्तम //
259.m: should be buried at the door of the maiden; she will not be given to another. / With "O God Savitṛ" (deva savitar), one desirous of strength should make offerings, O best of the twice-born.

259.s:
agnau svāheti juhuyādbalakāmo dvijottama /
tilair yavaiś ca dharmajña tathāpāmārgataṇḍulaiḥ //
259.d:
अग्नौ स्वाहेति जुहुयाद्बलकामो द्विजोत्तम /
तिलैर् यवैश् च धर्मज्ञ तथापामार्गतण्डुलैः //
259.m: One desirous of strength should offer into the fire with "svāhā", O best of the twice-born, / with sesame seeds, barley grains, O knower of righteousness, and grains of apāmārga.

259.s:
sahasramantritāṃ kṛtvā tathā gorocanāṃ dvija /
tilakañca tathā kṛtvā janasya priyatāmiyāt //
259.d:
सहस्रमन्त्रितां कृत्वा तथा गोरोचनां द्विज /
तिलकञ्च तथा कृत्वा जनस्य प्रियतामियात् //
259.m: Consecrating yellow pigment (gorocanā) a thousand times, O twice-born, / and making a mark on the forehead with it, one becomes beloved to the people.

259.s:
rudrāṇāñca tathā japyaṃ sarvāghavinisūdanaṃ /
sarvakarmakaro homas tathā sarvatra śantidaḥ //
259.d:
रुद्राणाञ्च तथा जप्यं सर्वाघविनिसूदनं /
सर्वकर्मकरो होमस् तथा सर्वत्र शन्तिदः //
259.m: The recitation to the Rudras destroys all sins. / A fire oblation accomplishes all purposes and brings peace everywhere:

259.s:
ajāvikānāmaśvānāṃ kuñjarāṇāṃ tathā gavāṃ /
manuṣyāṇānnarendrāṇāṃ bālānāṃ yoṣitāmapi //
259.d:
अजाविकानामश्वानां कुञ्जराणां तथा गवां /
मनुष्याणान्नरेन्द्राणां बालानां योषितामपि //
259.m: for goats and sheep, horses, elephants, and cattle; / for men, kings, children, and women;

259.s:
grāmāṇāṃ nagarānāñca deśānāmapi bhārgava /
:n
1 viṣṇorvirāṭamityetaditi gha.. , ña.. ca / viṣṭorarāṭamityetaditi ka.. ,
ja.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 449
upadrutānāṃ dharmajña vyādhitānāṃ tathaiva ca //
259.d:
ग्रामाणां नगरानाञ्च देशानामपि भार्गव /
:न्
1 विष्णोर्विराटमित्येतदिति घ.. , ञ.. च / विष्टोरराटमित्येतदिति क.. ,
ज.. , ट.. च
:प् 449
उपद्रुतानां धर्मज्ञ व्याधितानां तथैव च //
259.m:
for villages, cities, and countries as well, O Bhārgava,
[Footnote]
1 "viṣṇor virāṭam ity etat" in gha and ña; "viṣṭor arāṭam ity etat" in ka, ja, and ṭa. / [Page 449]
for those afflicted, O knower of righteousness, and those who are diseased.

259.s:
marake samanuprāpte ripuje ca tathā bhaye /
rudrahomaḥ parā śāntiḥ pāyasena ghṛtena ca //
259.d:
मरके समनुप्राप्ते रिपुजे च तथा भये /
रुद्रहोमः परा शान्तिः पायसेन घृतेन च //
259.m: When pestilence has arrived and danger caused by enemies, / a fire oblation to Rudra with milk-rice and clarified butter is the supreme pacification.

259.s:
kuṣmāṇḍaghṛtahomena sarvān pāpān vyapohati /
śaktuyāvakabhaikṣāśī naktaṃ manujasattama //
259.d:
कुष्माण्डघृतहोमेन सर्वान् पापान् व्यपोहति /
शक्तुयावकभैक्षाशी नक्तं मनुजसत्तम //
259.m: By means of a fire oblation of clarified butter with the Kūṣmāṇḍa [hymns], one removes all sins. / Eating barley-meal, barley gruel, or alms food at night, O best of men,

259.s:
bahiḥsnānarato māsānmucyate brahmahatyayā /
madhuvāteti mantreṇa homādito 'khilaṃ labhet //
259.d:
बहिःस्नानरतो मासान्मुच्यते ब्रह्महत्यया /
मधुवातेति मन्त्रेण होमादितो ऽखिलं लभेत् //
259.m: and devoted to bathing outside for a month, one is freed from the murder of a Brahmin. / From a fire oblation with the mantra "May the winds blow sweet" (madhu vātāḥ), one obtains everything.

259.s:
dadhi krāvneti hutvā tu putrān prāpnotyasaṃśayaṃ /
tathā ghṛtavatītyetadāyuṣyaṃ syāt ghṛtena tu //
259.d:
दधि क्राव्नेति हुत्वा तु पुत्रान् प्राप्नोत्यसंशयं /
तथा घृतवतीत्येतदायुष्यं स्यात् घृतेन तु //
259.m: Having offered with "Dadhikrāvā" (dadhi krāvṇaḥ), one obtains sons without a doubt. / Likewise, this [mantra] "Rich in clarified butter" (ghṛtavatī) with clarified butter promotes long life.

259.s:
svastina indra ity etatsarvabādhāvināśanaṃ /
iha gāvaḥ prajyāyadhvamiti puṣṭivivardhanam //
259.d:
स्वस्तिन इन्द्र इत्य् एतत्सर्वबाधाविनाशनं /
इह गावः प्रज्यायध्वमिति पुष्टिविवर्धनम् //
259.m: "May Indra [grant] us well-being" (svasti na indraḥ)—this destroys all obstacles. / "May cattle breed here" (iha gāvaḥ prajāyadhvam) increases prosperity.

259.s:
ghṛtāhutisahasreṇa tathā lakṣmīvināśanaṃ /
śruveṇa devasya tveti hutvāpāmārgataṇḍulaṃ //
259.d:
घृताहुतिसहस्रेण तथा लक्ष्मीविनाशनं /
श्रुवेण देवस्य त्वेति हुत्वापामार्गतण्डुलं //
259.m: With a thousand offerings of clarified butter, it destroys misfortune (alaksmi). / Having offered grains of apāmārga with the ladle using "At the god's..." (devasya tvā),

259.s:
mucyate vikṛtācchīghramabhicārānna saṃśayaḥ /
rudra pātu palaśasya samidbhiḥ kanakaṃ labhet //
259.d:
मुच्यते विकृताच्छीघ्रमभिचारान्न संशयः /
रुद्र पातु पलशस्य समिद्भिः कनकं लभेत् //
259.m: one is quickly freed from malevolent sorcery (abhicāra) and transformation, no doubt. / With fuel sticks of palāśa using "May Rudra protect" (rudra pātu), one obtains gold.

259.s:
śivo bhavetyagnyutpāte vrīhibhirjuhuyānnaraḥ /
yāḥ senā iti caitacca taskarebhyo bhayāpaham //
259.d:
शिवो भवेत्यग्न्युत्पाते व्रीहिभिर्जुहुयान्नरः /
याः सेना इति चैतच्च तस्करेभ्यो भयापहम् //
259.m: In case of fire portents, a man should offer with rice grains using "Be auspicious" (śivo bhava). / And this [mantra], "Which armies" (yāḥ senāḥ), dispels fear from thieves.

259.s:
yo asmabhyamavātīyāddhutvā kṛṣṇatilānnaraḥ /
sahasraśo 'bhicārācca mucyate vikṛtāddvija //
259.d:
यो अस्मभ्यमवातीयाद्धुत्वा कृष्णतिलान्नरः /
सहस्रशो ऽभिचाराच्च मुच्यते विकृताद्द्विज //
259.m: A man who offers black sesame seeds a thousand times with "Whoever attacks us" (yo asmabhyam avātīyāt), / is freed from sorcery and transformation, O twice-born.

259.s:
annenānnapatetyevaṃ hutvā cānnamavāpnuyāt /
haṃsaḥ śuciḥ sadityetajjaptantoye 'ghanāśanaṃ //
259.d:
अन्नेनान्नपतेत्येवं हुत्वा चान्नमवाप्नुयात् /
हंसः शुचिः सदित्येतज्जप्तन्तोये ऽघनाशनं //
259.m: Having offered with "Lord of food, with food..." (annena annapate), one obtains food. / "The swan seated in purity" (haṃsaḥ śucisat), recited in water, destroys sin.

259.s:
catvāri bhaṅgetyetattu sarvapāpaharaṃ jale /
devā yajñeti japtvā tu brahmaloke mahīyate //
:p 450
259.d:
चत्वारि भङ्गेत्येतत्तु सर्वपापहरं जले /
देवा यज्ञेति जप्त्वा तु ब्रह्मलोके महीयते //
:प् 450
259.m:
"Catvāri bhṛṅgā...", recited in water, removes all sins. / Having recited "The gods [performed] the sacrifice" (devā yajñam), one is exalted in the world of Brahmā.
[Page 450]

259.s:
vasanteti ca hutvājyaṃ ādityādvaramāpnuyāt /
suparṇosīti cetyasya karmavyāhṛtivadbhavet //
259.d:
वसन्तेति च हुत्वाज्यं आदित्याद्वरमाप्नुयात् /
सुपर्णोसीति चेत्यस्य कर्मव्याहृतिवद्भवेत् //
259.m: Having offered clarified butter with "Spring..." (vasanta), one obtains a boon from the sun. / And of "You are the winged one" (suparṇo 'si), the ritual action is like that of the vyāhṛtis.

259.s:
namaḥ svāheti trirjaptvā bandhanānmokṣamāpnuyāt /
antarjale trirāvartya drupadā sarvapāpamuk //
259.d:
नमः स्वाहेति त्रिर्जप्त्वा बन्धनान्मोक्षमाप्नुयात् /
अन्तर्जले त्रिरावर्त्य द्रुपदा सर्वपापमुक् //
259.m: Having recited "Homage! Svāhā!" (namaḥ svāhā) three times, one attains freedom from bondage. / Repeating the Drupadā [verse] three times within water frees one from all sin.

259.s:
iha gāvaḥ prajāyadhvaṃ mantroyaṃ buddhivardhanaḥ /
hutantu sarpiṣā dadhnā payasā pāyasena vā //
259.d:
इह गावः प्रजायध्वं मन्त्रोयं बुद्धिवर्धनः /
हुतन्तु सर्पिषा दध्ना पयसा पायसेन वा //
259.m: The mantra "May cattle breed here" (iha gāvaḥ prajāyadhvam) increases intelligence / when offered with clarified butter, curd, milk, or milk-rice.

259.s:
śatam ya(1) iti caitena hutvā parṇaphalāṇi ca /
ārogyaṃ śriyamāpnoti jīvitañca cirantathā //
259.d:
शतम् य(1) इति चैतेन हुत्वा पर्णफलाणि च /
आरोग्यं श्रियमाप्नोति जीवितञ्च चिरन्तथा //
259.m: And having offered leaves and fruits with "A hundred..." (śatam yaḥ), / one attains health, prosperity, and long life.

259.s:
oṣadhīḥ pratimodagdhvaṃ(2) vapane lavane 'rthakṛt /
aśvāvatī pāyasena homācchāntimavāpnuyāt //
259.d:
ओषधीः प्रतिमोदग्ध्वं(2) वपने लवने ऽर्थकृत् /
अश्वावती पायसेन होमाच्छान्तिमवाप्नुयात् //
259.m: "Rejoice, O plants" (oṣadhīḥ pratimodadhvam) brings wealth during sowing and reaping. / Through a fire oblation of milk-rice with "Rich in horses" (aśvāvatī), one attains peace.

259.s:
tasmā iti ca mantrena bandhanastho vimucyate /
yuvā suvāsā ity eva vāsāṃsyāpnoti cottamam //
259.d:
तस्मा इति च मन्त्रेन बन्धनस्थो विमुच्यते /
युवा सुवासा इत्य् एव वासांस्याप्नोति चोत्तमम् //
259.m: A person in fetters is released with the mantra "To him..." (tasmai). / With "The youth well-dressed" (yuvā suvāsāḥ), one obtains excellent garments.

259.s:
muñcantu mā śapathyāni sarvāntakavināśanam(3) /
mā māhiṃsīstilājyena hutaṃ ripuvināśanaṃ(4) //
259.d:
मुञ्चन्तु मा शपथ्यानि सर्वान्तकविनाशनम्(3) /
मा माहिंसीस्तिलाज्येन हुतं रिपुविनाशनं(4) //
259.m: "May the curses release me" (muñcantu mā śapathyāḥ) destroys all death. / An offering of sesame and clarified butter with "Do not harm me" (mā mā hiṃsīḥ) destroys enemies.

259.s:
namo 'stu sarvasarpebhyo ghṛtena pāyasena tu /
kṛṇudhavaṃ rāja ity etadabhicāravināśanaṃ //
259.d:
नमो ऽस्तु सर्वसर्पेभ्यो घृतेन पायसेन तु /
कृणुधवं राज इत्य् एतदभिचारविनाशनं //
259.m: With "Homage to all serpents" (namo 'stu sarvasarpebhyaḥ) using clarified butter and milk-rice, / and "Make, O king" (kṛṇudhvaṃ rājan), it destroys sorcery.

259.s:
dūrvākāṇḍāyutaṃ hutvā kāṇḍāt kāṇḍeti mānavaḥ /
grāme janapade vāpi marakantu śamannayet //
259.d:
दूर्वाकाण्डायुतं हुत्वा काण्डात् काण्डेति मानवः /
ग्रामे जनपदे वापि मरकन्तु शमन्नयेत् //
259.m: Having offered ten thousand joints of dūrvā grass with "From joint to joint" (kāṇḍāt kāṇḍāt), a man / brings an end to pestilence in a village or a district.

259.s:
rogārto mucyate rogāt tathā duḥkhāttu duḥkhitaḥ /
:n
1 śatañceti ṭa.. / śataṃ veti ka..
2 auṣadhayaḥ pratimodadhyamiti ja..
3 sarvakilviṣanāśanamiti gha.. , ña.. ca
4 vighnavināśanamiti ka.. , cha.. ca
:p 451
auḍumbarīś ca samidho madhumānno vanaspatiḥ //
259.d:
रोगार्तो मुच्यते रोगात् तथा दुःखात्तु दुःखितः /
:न्
1 शतञ्चेति ट.. / शतं वेति क..
2 औषधयः प्रतिमोदध्यमिति ज..
3 सर्वकिल्विषनाशनमिति घ.. , ञ.. च
4 विघ्नविनाशनमिति क.. , छ.. च
:प् 451
औडुम्बरीश् च समिधो मधुमान्नो वनस्पतिः //
259.m:
One afflicted with disease is freed from disease, and one suffering from grief is freed from grief.
[Footnote]
1 "śatañ ca" in ṭa; "śataṃ vā" in ka.
2 "oṣadhayaḥ pratimodadhvam" in ja.
3 "sarvakilviṣanāśanam" in gha and ña.
4 "vighnavināśanam" in ka and cha. / [Page 451]
And having offered firewood sticks of udumbara with "Sweet-bearing is the lord of the forest for us" (madhumān no vanaspatiḥ)

259.s:
hutvā sahasraśo rāma dhanamāpnoti mānavaḥ /
saubhāgyaṃ mahadāpnoti vyavahāre tathā trayam //
259.d:
हुत्वा सहस्रशो राम धनमाप्नोति मानवः /
सौभाग्यं महदाप्नोति व्यवहारे तथा त्रयम् //
259.m: a thousand times, O Rāma, a man obtains wealth; / he obtains great good fortune and threefold success in transactions.

259.s:
apāṃ garbhamiti hutvā devaṃ varṣāpayeddhruvam /
apaḥ piveti ca tathā hutvā dadhi ghṛtaṃ madhu //
259.d:
अपां गर्भमिति हुत्वा देवं वर्षापयेद्ध्रुवम् /
अपः पिवेति च तथा हुत्वा दधि घृतं मधु //
259.m: Having offered with "Child of the waters" (apāṃ garbham), one certainly makes the rain god rain. / And having likewise offered curd, clarified butter, and honey with "Drink the waters" (apaḥ piba),

259.s:
pravartayati dharmajña mahāvṛṣṭimanantaraṃ /
namaste rudra ity etat sarvopadravanāśanaṃ //
259.d:
प्रवर्तयति धर्मज्ञ महावृष्टिमनन्तरं /
नमस्ते रुद्र इत्य् एतत् सर्वोपद्रवनाशनं //
259.m: one immediately brings about heavy rain, O knower of righteousness. / This [hymn], "Homage to you, O Rudra" (namas te rudra), destroys all calamities.

259.s:
sarvaśāntikaraṃ proktaṃ mahāpātakanāśanaṃ /
adhyavocadityanena rakṣaṇaṃ vyādhitasya tu //
259.d:
सर्वशान्तिकरं प्रोक्तं महापातकनाशनं /
अध्यवोचदित्यनेन रक्षणं व्याधितस्य तु //
259.m: It is declared to bring all pacification and destroy major sins (mahāpātaka). / With "He spoke on our behalf" (adhyavocat), there is protection for the diseased,

259.s:
rakṣoghnañca yaśasyañca cirāyuḥpuṣṭivardhanam /
siddhārthakānāṃ kṣepeṇa pathi caitajjapan sukhī //
259.d:
रक्षोघ्नञ्च यशस्यञ्च चिरायुःपुष्टिवर्धनम् /
सिद्धार्थकानां क्षेपेण पथि चैतज्जपन् सुखी //
259.m: destruction of demons, bestowal of fame, and increase of long life and vigor. / Reciting this on a journey while throwing white mustard seeds, one remains safe.

259.s:
asau yastāmra ity etat paṭhannityaṃ divākaraṃ /
upatiṣṭheta dharmajña sāyaṃ prātaratandritaḥ //
259.d:
असौ यस्ताम्र इत्य् एतत् पठन्नित्यं दिवाकरं /
उपतिष्ठेत धर्मज्ञ सायं प्रातरतन्द्रितः //
259.m: Constantly reciting this [verse], "He who is copper-colored" (asau yas tāmraḥ), one should wait upon the sun, / evening and morning without laziness, O knower of righteousness.

259.s:
annamakṣayamāpnoti dīrghamāyuś ca vindati /
pramuñca(1) dhanvannityetat ṣaḍbhirāyudhamantraṇaṃ //
259.d:
अन्नमक्षयमाप्नोति दीर्घमायुश् च विन्दति /
प्रमुञ्च(1) धन्वन्नित्येतत् षड्भिरायुधमन्त्रणं //
259.m: One obtains inexhaustible food and finds long life. / With the six [verses beginning with] "Unstring the bow" (pramuñca dhanvaḥ), consecration of weapons

259.s:
ripūṇāṃ bhayadaṃ yuddhenātrakāryā vicāraṇā /
māno mahānta ity evaṃ bālānāṃ śāntikārakaṃ //
259.d:
रिपूणां भयदं युद्धेनात्रकार्या विचारणा /
मानो महान्त इत्य् एवं बालानां शान्तिकारकं //
259.m: strikes fear into enemies in battle—no doubt should be entertained here. / The [verse beginning with] "Do not [harm] our great ones" (mā no mahāntam) brings pacification for children.

259.s:
namo hiraṇyavāhave ity anuvākasaptakam /
rājikāṃ kaṭutailāktāṃ juhuyācchatrunāśanīṃ //
259.d:
नमो हिरण्यवाहवे इत्य् अनुवाकसप्तकम् /
राजिकां कटुतैलाक्तां जुहुयाच्छत्रुनाशनीं //
259.m: With the seven sections beginning with “namo hiraṇyavāhave” (“Homage to the golden-armed”), / one should offer mustard smeared with pungent oil; it destroys enemies.

259.s:
namo vaḥ kirikebhyaś ca padmalakṣāhutair naraḥ /
rājyalakṣmīmavāpnoti tathā bilvaiḥ suvarṇakam //
259.d:
नमो वः किरिकेभ्यश् च पद्मलक्षाहुतैर् नरः /
राज्यलक्ष्मीमवाप्नोति तथा बिल्वैः सुवर्णकम् //
259.m: Through a hundred thousand oblations with “namo vaḥ kirikebhyaḥ” (“Homage to you, the sparklers”) using lotuses, a man / obtains the royal fortune, and similarly, gold through bilva fruits.

259.s:
imā rudrāyeti tilair homācca dhanamāpyate /
:n
1 prayuñjeti ga.. , gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 452
dūrvāhomena cānyena sarvavyādhivivarjitaḥ //
259.d:
इमा रुद्रायेति तिलैर् होमाच्च धनमाप्यते /
:न्
1 प्रयुञ्जेति ग.. , घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 452
दूर्वाहोमेन चान्येन सर्वव्याधिविवर्जितः //
259.m:
Wealth is obtained through fire oblations with sesame seeds using “imā rudrāya” (“These to Rudra”).
[Footnote]
1. "prayuñje" thus in manuscripts ga, gha, and ña. / [Page 452]
And by another fire oblation with dūrvā grass, one is freed from all diseases.

259.s:
āśuḥ śiśāna ity etadāyudhānāñca rakṣaṇe /
saṃgrāme kathitaṃ rāma sarvaśatrunivarhaṇaṃ //
259.d:
आशुः शिशान इत्य् एतदायुधानाञ्च रक्षणे /
संग्रामे कथितं राम सर्वशत्रुनिवर्हणं //
259.m: The mantra “āśuḥ śiśānaḥ” (“Swiftly sharpening”) is taught for protecting weapons, / and in battle, O Rāma, for destroying all enemies.

259.s:
rājasāmeti juhuyāt sahasraṃ pañcabhirdvija /
ājyāhutīnāṃ dharmajña cakṣūrogādvimucyate //
259.d:
राजसामेति जुहुयात् सहस्रं पञ्चभिर्द्विज /
आज्याहुतीनां धर्मज्ञ चक्षूरोगाद्विमुच्यते //
259.m: O twice-born knower of righteousness, one should offer a thousand oblations of clarified butter / with five verses of “rājasāma”; one is freed from eye disease.

259.s:
śanno vanaspate gehe homaḥ syādvāstudoṣanut /
agna āyūṃsi hutvājyaṃ dveṣaṃ nāpnoti kenacit //
259.d:
शन्नो वनस्पते गेहे होमः स्याद्वास्तुदोषनुत् /
अग्न आयूंसि हुत्वाज्यं द्वेषं नाप्नोति केनचित् //
259.m: A fire oblation in the house with “śaṃ no vanaspate” (“May the lord of the forest bring us peace”) removes defects of site architecture. / Having offered clarified butter with “agna āyūṃṣi” (“O Agni, life-spans”), one suffers no hatred from anyone.

259.s:
apāṃ pheneti lājābhirhutvā jayamavāpnuyāt /
bhadrā itīndriyair hīno japan syāt sakalendriyaḥ //
259.d:
अपां फेनेति लाजाभिर्हुत्वा जयमवाप्नुयात् /
भद्रा इतीन्द्रियैर् हीनो जपन् स्यात् सकलेन्द्रियः //
259.m: Having offered roasted grains with “apāṃ phena” (“With foam of the waters”), one obtains victory. / One who is deprived of sense organs, reciting “bhadrāḥ” (“Auspicious”), becomes endowed with all sense organs.

259.s:
agniś ca pṛthivī ceti vaśīkaraṇamuttamam /
adhvaneti japan mantraṃ vyavahāre jayī bhavet //
259.d:
अग्निश् च पृथिवी चेति वशीकरणमुत्तमम् /
अध्वनेति जपन् मन्त्रं व्यवहारे जयी भवेत् //
259.m: “Agniś ca pṛthivī ca” (“Both Agni and the earth”) is supreme for subjugation. / Reciting the mantra “adhvanaḥ” (“From the paths”), one becomes victorious in legal affairs.

259.s:
brahma rājanyamiti ca karmārambhe tu siddhikṛt /
saṃvatsarosīti dhṛtair lakṣahomādarogavān //
259.d:
ब्रह्म राजन्यमिति च कर्मारम्भे तु सिद्धिकृत् /
संवत्सरोसीति धृतैर् लक्षहोमादरोगवान् //
259.m: And “brahma rājanyam” (“The priest and the warrior”) brings success at the beginning of actions. / By a hundred thousand fire oblations of clarified butter with “saṃvatsaro 'si” (“You are the year”), one becomes free from disease.

259.s:
ketuṃ kṛṇvannitītyetat saṃgrāme jayavardhanam /
indrognirdharma ity etadraṇe dharmanibandhanam(1) //
259.d:
केतुं कृण्वन्नितीत्येतत् संग्रामे जयवर्धनम् /
इन्द्रोग्निर्धर्म इत्य् एतद्रणे धर्मनिबन्धनम्(1) //
259.m: The mantra “ketuṃ kṛṇvan” (“Making a banner”) increases victory in battle. / “Indro 'gnir dharmaḥ” (“Indra, Agni, Dharma”) binds righteousness in war.

259.s:
dhanvā nāgeti mantraś ca dhanurgrāhanikaḥ paraḥ /
yajīteti tathā mantro vijñeyo hy abhimantraṇe //
259.d:
धन्वा नागेति मन्त्रश् च धनुर्ग्राहनिकः परः /
यजीतेति तथा मन्त्रो विज्ञेयो ह्य् अभिमन्त्रणे //
259.m: The mantra “dhanvā nāgā” is supreme for taking up the bow. / Likewise, the mantra “yajīta” should be known for consecration [of weapons].

259.s:
mantraścāhirathetyetaccharāṇāṃ(2) mantraṇe bhavet /
vahnīnāṃ pitarityetattūrṇamantraḥ prakīrtitaḥ //
259.d:
मन्त्रश्चाहिरथेत्येतच्छराणां(2) मन्त्रणे भवेत् /
वह्नीनां पितरित्येतत्तूर्णमन्त्रः प्रकीर्तितः //
259.m: The mantra “ahiratha” is used for consecrating arrows. / “Vahnīnāṃ pitaḥ” is proclaimed as the mantra for the trumpet.

259.s:
yuñjantīti tathāśvānāṃ yojane mantra ucyate /
āśuḥ śiśāna ity etadyatrārambhaṇamucyate //
:n
1 dharmavivardhanamiti ja..
2 mantraś ca hi ratha hy etaccharāṇāmiti ka.. , cha.. ,ca
:p 453
259.d:
युञ्जन्तीति तथाश्वानां योजने मन्त्र उच्यते /
आशुः शिशान इत्य् एतद्यत्रारम्भणमुच्यते //
:न्
1 धर्मविवर्धनमिति ज..
2 मन्त्रश् च हि रथ ह्य् एतच्छराणामिति क.. , छ.. ,च
:प् 453
259.m:
Likewise, “yuñjanti” (“They yoke”) is spoken of as the mantra for yoking horses. / “Āśuḥ śiśānaḥ” is spoken of for commencing the expedition.
[Footnote]
1. "dharmavivardhanam" thus in manuscript ja.
2. "mantraś ca hi ratha hy etaccharāṇām" thus in manuscripts ka and cha. / [Page 453]

259.s:
viṣṇoḥ krameti mantraś ca rathārohaṇikaḥ paraḥ /
ājaṅghetīti cāśvānāṃ tāḍanīyamudāhṛtaṃ //
259.d:
विष्णोः क्रमेति मन्त्रश् च रथारोहणिकः परः /
आजङ्घेतीति चाश्वानां ताडनीयमुदाहृतं //
259.m: The mantra “viṣṇoḥ kramaḥ” (“The stride of Viṣṇu”) is supreme for mounting the chariot. / And “ājaṅghā” is taught for whipping the horses.

259.s:
yāḥ senā abhitvarīti parasainyamukhe japet /
dundubhya iti cāpyetaddundubhītāḍnaṃ bhavet //
259.d:
याः सेना अभित्वरीति परसैन्यमुखे जपेत् /
दुन्दुभ्य इति चाप्येतद्दुन्दुभीताड्नं भवेत् //
259.m: One should recite “yāḥ senā abhitvarīḥ” (“Those armies that hasten forward”) facing the enemy's army. / And “dundubhyaḥ” (“To the war-drums”) is for beating the war-drum.

259.s:
etaiḥ pūrvahutair mantraiḥ kṛtvaivaṃ vijayī bhavet /
yamena dattamityasya koṭihomādvicakṣaṇaḥ //
259.d:
एतैः पूर्वहुतैर् मन्त्रैः कृत्वैवं विजयी भवेत् /
यमेन दत्तमित्यस्य कोटिहोमाद्विचक्षणः //
259.m: Having acted with these mantras previously offered into the fire, one becomes victorious. / From ten million fire oblations of “yamena dattam” (“Given by Yama”), a wise man

259.s:
rathamutpādayecchīghraṃ saṃgrāme vijayapradam /
ā kṛṣṇeti tathaitasya karmavyāhṛtivadbhavet //
259.d:
रथमुत्पादयेच्छीघ्रं संग्रामे विजयप्रदम् /
आ कृष्णेति तथैतस्य कर्मव्याहृतिवद्भवेत् //
259.m: can swiftly produce a chariot that grants victory in battle. / And the use of “ā kṛṣṇena” (“With the dark [realm]”) is like that of the sacred utterances.

259.s:
śivasaṃkalpajāpena(1) samādhiṃ manaso labhet /
pañcanadyaḥ pañcalakṣaṃ hutvā lakṣmīmavāpnuyāt //
259.d:
शिवसंकल्पजापेन(1) समाधिं मनसो लभेत् /
पञ्चनद्यः पञ्चलक्षं हुत्वा लक्ष्मीमवाप्नुयात् //
259.m: By the recitation of the Śivasaṅkalpa hymn, one obtains absorption of the mind. / Having offered five hundred thousand oblations with “pañca nadyaḥ” (“Five rivers”), one obtains Lakṣmī.

259.s:
yadā badhūndakṣāyaṇāṃ mantreṇānena mantritam /
sahasrakṛtvaḥ kanakaṃ dhārayedripuvāraṇaṃ //
259.d:
यदा बधून्दक्षायणां मन्त्रेणानेन मन्त्रितम् /
सहस्रकृत्वः कनकं धारयेद्रिपुवारणं //
259.m: Gold consecrated a thousand times with this mantra, “yad ābadhnan dākṣāyaṇāḥ” (“What the descendants of Dakṣa bound”), / should be worn; it wards off enemies.

259.s:
imaṃ jīvebhya drati ca śilāṃ loṣṭrañcaturdiśaṃ /
kṣipedgṛhe tadā tasya na syāccaurabhayaṃ niśi //
259.d:
इमं जीवेभ्य द्रति च शिलां लोष्ट्रञ्चतुर्दिशं /
क्षिपेद्गृहे तदा तस्य न स्याच्चौरभयं निशि //
259.m: Throwing a stone or a clod of earth in the four directions in the house with “imaṃ jīvebhyaḥ” (“This for the living”), / one then has no fear of thieves at night.

259.s:
parimegāmaneneti(2) vaśīkaraṇamuttamaṃ /
hantumabhyāgatastatra vaśībhavati mānavaḥ //
259.d:
परिमेगामनेनेति(2) वशीकरणमुत्तमं /
हन्तुमभ्यागतस्तत्र वशीभवति मानवः //
259.m: “Pari me gām anena” is an excellent means of subjugation; / a man who arrives there to kill becomes subjugated.

259.s:
bhakṣyatāmvūlapuṣpādyaṃ mantritantu prayacchati /
yasya dharmajña vaśagaḥ somya śīghraṃ bhaviṣyati //
259.d:
भक्ष्यताम्वूलपुष्पाद्यं मन्त्रितन्तु प्रयच्छति /
यस्य धर्मज्ञ वशगः सोम्य शीघ्रं भविष्यति //
259.m: O knower of righteousness, gentle one, when one gives consecrated food, betel, flowers, and the like, / that person will swiftly become subordinate to him.

259.s:
śanno mitra itītyetat sadā sarvatra śāntidaṃ /
gaṇānāṃ tvā gaṇapatiṃ kṛtvā homañcatuṣpathe //
259.d:
शन्नो मित्र इतीत्येतत् सदा सर्वत्र शान्तिदं /
गणानां त्वा गणपतिं कृत्वा होमञ्चतुष्पथे //
259.m: “Śaṃ no mitraḥ” (“May Mitra be auspicious to us”) always and everywhere grants peace. / Having performed a fire oblation at a crossroad with “gaṇānāṃ tvā gaṇapatim” (“Thee, the lord of the hosts”),

259.s:
vaśīkuryājjagatsarvam sarvadhānyair asaṃśayam /
:n
1 śivasaṃkalpa ity etaditi gha.. , ja.. ca
2 parāṅne gāyanenetīti ka..
:p 454
hiraṇyavarṇāḥ śucayo mantroyamabhiṣecane //
259.d:
वशीकुर्याज्जगत्सर्वम् सर्वधान्यैर् असंशयम् /
:न्
1 शिवसंकल्प इत्य् एतदिति घ.. , ज.. च
2 पराङ्ने गायनेनेतीति क..
:प् 454
हिरण्यवर्णाः शुचयो मन्त्रोयमभिषेचने //
259.m:
using all types of grain, one undoubtedly subjugates the entire world.
[Footnote]
1. "śivasaṃkalpa ity etat" thus in manuscripts gha and ja.
2. "parāṅne gāyaneneti" thus in manuscript ka. / [Page 454]
“Hiraṇyavarṇāḥ śucayaḥ” (“Golden-hued, pure”) is this mantra for consecration by aspersion.

259.s:
śanno devīrabhiṣṭaye tathā śāntikaraḥ paraḥ /
ekacakreti mantreṇa hutenājyena bhāgaśaḥ(1) //
259.d:
शन्नो देवीरभिष्टये तथा शान्तिकरः परः /
एकचक्रेति मन्त्रेण हुतेनाज्येन भागशः(1) //
259.m: “Śaṃ no devīr abhiṣṭaye” (“May the divine waters be for our aid”) is likewise supreme for pacification. / With clarified butter offered in portions with the mantra “ekacakra” (“Single-wheeled”),

259.s:
grahebhyaḥ śāntimāpnoti prasādaṃ na ca saṃśayaḥ /
gāvo bhaga iti dvābhyāṃ hutvājyaṅgā avāpnuyāt //
259.d:
ग्रहेभ्यः शान्तिमाप्नोति प्रसादं न च संशयः /
गावो भग इति द्वाभ्यां हुत्वाज्यङ्गा अवाप्नुयात् //
259.m: one undoubtedly attains peace and grace from the planets. / Having offered clarified butter with the two verses beginning “gāvo bhagaḥ” (“Cows are fortune”), one obtains cattle.

259.s:
pravādāṃśaḥ sopaditi(2) gṛhayajñe vidhīyate /
devebhyo vanaspata iti drumayajñe vidhīyate //
259.d:
प्रवादांशः सोपदिति(2) गृहयज्ञे विधीयते /
देवेभ्यो वनस्पत इति द्रुमयज्ञे विधीयते //
259.m: “Pravādāṃśaḥ sopat” is prescribed in the domestic sacrifice. / “Devebhyo vanaspate” is prescribed in the tree sacrifice.

259.s:
gāyatrī vaiṣṇavī jñeyā tadviṣṇoḥ paramampadaṃ /
sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ sarvakāmakarantathā(3) //
:e ity āgeneye mahāpurāṇe yajurvidhānaṃ
nāmonaṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha ṣaṣṭhyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
sāmavidhānaṃ
259.d:
गायत्री वैष्णवी ज्ञेया तद्विष्णोः परमम्पदं /
सर्वपापप्रशमनं सर्वकामकरन्तथा(3) //
:ए इत्य् आगेनेये महापुराणे यजुर्विधानं
नामोनषष्ट्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ षष्ठ्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
सामविधानं
259.m:
The Gāyatrī addressed to Viṣṇu is to be known as “tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam” (“That highest step of Viṣṇu”); / it pacifies all sins and fulfills all desires.
Thus in the great Āgneya Purāṇa, the two hundred and fifty-ninth chapter, entitled “The Application of Yajur-mantras.”
Now the two hundred and sixtieth chapter:
The Application of Sāma-chants

260.s:
puṣkara uvāca
yujurvidhānaṅkathitaṃ vakṣye sāmnāṃ vidhānakaṃ /
saṃhitāṃ vaiṣṇavīñjaptvā hutvā syāt sarvakāmabhāk //
260.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
युजुर्विधानङ्कथितं वक्ष्ये साम्नां विधानकं /
संहितां वैष्णवीञ्जप्त्वा हुत्वा स्यात् सर्वकामभाक् //
260.m: Puṣkara said: / The application of the Yajur-mantras has been declared; I shall explain the application of the Sāma-chants. / Reciting and offering fire oblations with the Vaiṣṇava collection, one attains all desires.

260.s:
saṃhitāñchāndasīṃ sādhu japtvā prīṇāti śaṅkaraṃ /
skandīṃ paitryāṃ saṃhitāñca japtvā syāttu prasādavān //
:n
1 bhāgata iti ka.. , ga.. , cha.. , ña.. ca
2 pravādīśaṃ sopaditīti kha.. , cha.. ca
3 sarvaśāntikarantatheti gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 455
260.d:
संहिताञ्छान्दसीं साधु जप्त्वा प्रीणाति शङ्करं /
स्कन्दीं पैत्र्यां संहिताञ्च जप्त्वा स्यात्तु प्रसादवान् //
:न्
1 भागत इति क.. , ग.. , छ.. , ञ.. च
2 प्रवादीशं सोपदितीति ख.. , छ.. च
3 सर्वशान्तिकरन्तथेति घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 455
260.m:
Reciting well the metrical collection, one pleases Śaṅkara. / Reciting the Skānda collection and the Pitṛ collection, one attains favor.
[Footnote]
1. "bhāgataḥ" thus in manuscripts ka, ga, cha, and ña.
2. "pravādīśaṃ sopadi" thus in manuscripts kha and cha.
3. "sarvaśāntikaraṃ tathā" thus in manuscripts gha and ña. / [Page 455]

260.s:
yata indra bhajāmahe hiṃsādoṣavināśanaṃ /
avakīrṇī mucyate ca agnistigmeti vai japan //
260.d:
यत इन्द्र भजामहे हिंसादोषविनाशनं /
अवकीर्णी मुच्यते च अग्निस्तिग्मेति वै जपन् //
260.m: “Yata indra bhajāmahe” destroys the sin of violence. / Reciting “agnis tigmā” (“Agni is sharp”), a fallen celibate is freed [from his sin].

260.s:
sarvapāpaharaṃ jñeyaṃ paritoyañca tāsu ca(1) /
avikreyañca vikrīya japedghṛtavatīti ca //
260.d:
सर्वपापहरं ज्ञेयं परितोयञ्च तासु च(1) /
अविक्रेयञ्च विक्रीय जपेद्घृतवतीति च //
260.m: “Pari toyañ ca tāsu ca” is known to remove all sins. / Having sold what is unsellable, one should recite “ghṛtavatī”.

260.s:
ayāno deva saviturjñeyanduḥsvapnanāśanaṃ /
abodhyagniritimantreṇa ghṛtaṃ rāma yathāvidhi //
260.d:
अयानो देव सवितुर्ज्ञेयन्दुःस्वप्ननाशनं /
अबोध्यग्निरितिमन्त्रेण घृतं राम यथाविधि //
260.m: “Ayā no deva savitaḥ” should be known to destroy nightmares. / With the mantra “abodhhy agniḥ” (“Agni has been awakened”), O Rāma, clarified butter is consecrated according to rule;

260.s:
abhyukṣya ghṛtaśeṣeṇa mekhalābandha iṣyate /
strīṇāṃ yāsāntu garbhāṇi patanti bhṛgusattama //
260.d:
अभ्युक्ष्य घृतशेषेण मेखलाबन्ध इष्यते /
स्त्रीणां यासान्तु गर्भाणि पतन्ति भृगुसत्तम //
260.m: having sprinkled [the woman] with the remainder of the clarified butter, the binding of the girdle is prescribed / for women whose embryos miscarry, O best of the Bhṛgus.

260.s:
maṇiṃ jātasya bālasya vadhnīyāttadanantaraṃ /
somaṃ rājānametena vyādhibhirvipramucyate //
260.d:
मणिं जातस्य बालस्य वध्नीयात्तदनन्तरं /
सोमं राजानमेतेन व्याधिभिर्विप्रमुच्यते //
260.m: Immediately afterward, one should tie an amulet on the newborn child. / With this “somaṃ rājānam” (“Soma, the king”), one is fully freed from diseases.

260.s:
sarpasāma prayuñjīno nāpnuyāt sarpajambhayaṃ /
mādya tvā vādyatetyetaddhutvā vipraḥ sahasraśaḥ //
260.d:
सर्पसाम प्रयुञ्जीनो नाप्नुयात् सर्पजम्भयं /
माद्य त्वा वाद्यतेत्येतद्धुत्वा विप्रः सहस्रशः //
260.m: Employing the Sarpasāma, one incurs no danger from snakes. / A Brahmin, offering a thousand oblations with “mādya tvā vādyatā”,

260.s:
śatāvarimaṇibaddhvā nāpnuyācchastrato bhayaṃ /
dīrghatamasorka iti huttvānnaṃ prāpnuyādbahu //
260.d:
शतावरिमणिबद्ध्वा नाप्नुयाच्छस्त्रतो भयं /
दीर्घतमसोर्क इति हुत्त्वान्नं प्राप्नुयाद्बहु //
260.m: and having bound a śatāvarī amulet, incurs no fear from weapons. / Offering with “dīrghatamasorkaḥ”, one obtains abundant food.

260.s:
svamadhyāyantīti japanna mriyeta pipāsayā(2) /
tvamimā oṣadhī hy etajjaptvā vyādhiṃ na vāpnuyāt //
260.d:
स्वमध्यायन्तीति जपन्न म्रियेत पिपासया(2) /
त्वमिमा ओषधी ह्य् एतज्जप्त्वा व्याधिं न वाप्नुयात् //
260.m: Reciting “svam adhyāyanti”, one does not die of thirst. / Reciting “tvam imā oṣadhīḥ” (“Thou these herbs”), one suffers no illness.

260.s:
pathi devavratañjaptvā bhayebhyo vipramucyate /
yadindro munaye tveti hutaṃ saubhāgyavardhanaṃ //
260.d:
पथि देवव्रतञ्जप्त्वा भयेभ्यो विप्रमुच्यते /
यदिन्द्रो मुनये त्वेति हुतं सौभाग्यवर्धनं //
260.m: Reciting the Devavrata on a journey, one is freed from dangers. / “Yad indro munaye tvā”, offered in the fire, increases good fortune.

260.s:
bhago na citra ity evaṃ netrayo rañjanaṃ hitaṃ /
saubhāgyavardhanaṃ rāma nātra kārya vicāraṇā //
260.d:
भगो न चित्र इत्य् एवं नेत्रयो रञ्जनं हितं /
सौभाग्यवर्धनं राम नात्र कार्य विचारणा //
260.m: Applying collyrium to the eyes with “bhago na citraḥ” is beneficial; / it increases good fortune, O Rāma, there is no doubt about this.

260.s:
japendreti vargañca tathā saunbhāgyavardhanaṃ /
:n
1 paritoyaṃ yutāyutamiti ja.. , ṭa.. ca
2 pipāsita iti gha.. , ña.. ca
:p 456
pari priyā hi vaḥ kāriḥ(1) kāmyāṃ saṃśrāvayet striyaṃ //
260.d:
जपेन्द्रेति वर्गञ्च तथा सौन्भाग्यवर्धनं /
:न्
1 परितोयं युतायुतमिति ज.. , ट.. च
2 पिपासित इति घ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 456
परि प्रिया हि वः कारिः(1) काम्यां संश्रावयेत् स्त्रियं //
260.m:
Reciting the section “japendra” likewise increases good fortune.
[Footnote]
[Variant readings:] 1. 'paritoyaṃ yutāyutam' in manuscripts ja and ṭa.
2. 'pipāsitaḥ' in manuscripts gha and ña.
One should cause the woman whom one desires to hear [the chant beginning with] 'pari priyā hi vaḥ kāriḥ'.

260.s:
sā taṅkāmayate rāma nātra kāryā vicāraṇā /
rathantaraṃ vāmadevyaṃ brahmavarcasavardhanaṃ //
260.d:
सा तङ्कामयते राम नात्र कार्या विचारणा /
रथन्तरं वामदेव्यं ब्रह्मवर्चसवर्धनं //
260.m: She will desire him, O Rāma; no doubt should be entertained here. / The Rathantara and Vāmadevya [sāmans] increase spiritual splendor.

260.s:
prāśayedbālakaṃ nityaṃ vacācūrṇaṃ ghṛtaplutaṃ /
indramidgāthinaṃ japtvā bhavecchrutidharastvasau //
260.d:
प्राशयेद्बालकं नित्यं वचाचूर्णं घृतप्लुतं /
इन्द्रमिद्गाथिनं जप्त्वा भवेच्छ्रुतिधरस्त्वसौ //
260.m: One should daily feed a child calamus powder drenched in clarified butter, / having recited [the mantra beginning with] 'indramidgāthinaḥ'; he will then retain whatever he hears.

260.s:
hutvā rathantarañjaptvā putramāpnotyasaṃśayaṃ /
mayi śrīriti mantroyaṃ japtavyaḥ śrīvivardhanaḥ //
260.d:
हुत्वा रथन्तरञ्जप्त्वा पुत्रमाप्नोत्यसंशयं /
मयि श्रीरिति मन्त्रोयं जप्तव्यः श्रीविवर्धनः //
260.m: Having offered oblations and recited the Rathantara, one obtains a son without doubt. / The mantra 'mayi śrīḥ' should be recited to increase fortune.

260.s:
vairūpyasyāṣṭakaṃ nityaṃ prayuñjānaḥ śriyaṃ labhet /
saptāṣṭakaṃ prayuñjānaḥ sarvān kāmānavāpnuyāt //
260.d:
वैरूप्यस्याष्टकं नित्यं प्रयुञ्जानः श्रियं लभेत् /
सप्ताष्टकं प्रयुञ्जानः सर्वान् कामानवाप्नुयात् //
260.m: Practicing the octad of Vairūpya daily, one attains fortune. / Practicing the seven octads, one attains all desired objects.

260.s:
gavyeṣuṇeti yo nityaṃ sāyaṃ prātaratantritaḥ /
upasthānaṃ gavāṃ kuryāttasya syustāḥ sadā gṛhe //
260.d:
गव्येषुणेति यो नित्यं सायं प्रातरतन्त्रितः /
उपस्थानं गवां कुर्यात्तस्य स्युस्ताः सदा गृहे //
260.m: He who, untiring, attends upon cows morning and evening with [the chant beginning with] 'gavyeṣuṇā', / they will always remain in his house.

260.s:
ghṛtāktantu yavadroṇaṃ vāta āvātu bheṣajaṃ /
anena vidhivat sarvāṃ māyāṃ vyapohati //
260.d:
घृताक्तन्तु यवद्रोणं वात आवातु भेषजं /
अनेन विधिवत् सर्वां मायां व्यपोहति //
260.m: [Offering] a droṇa of barley smeared with clarified butter with [the hymn] 'vāta ā vātu bheṣajam', / one duly dispels every sorcerous illusion.

260.s:
pradevo dāsena tilān hutvā kārmaṇakṛntanaṃ /
abhi tvā pūrvapītaye vaṣaṭkārasamanvitaṃ //
260.d:
प्रदेवो दासेन तिलान् हुत्वा कार्मणकृन्तनं /
अभि त्वा पूर्वपीतये वषट्कारसमन्वितं //
260.m: Offering sesame seeds with [the hymn] 'pra devo dāsena' cuts through malevolent magic. / [With the chant] 'abhi tvā pūrvapītaye' accompanied by the vaṣaṭ-call,

260.s:
vāsakedhmasahasrantu hutaṃ yuddhe jayapradaṃ /
hastyaśvapuruṣān kuryādbudhaḥ piṣṭamayān śubhān //
260.d:
वासकेध्मसहस्रन्तु हुतं युद्धे जयप्रदं /
हस्त्यश्वपुरुषान् कुर्याद्बुधः पिष्टमयान् शुभान् //
260.m: a thousand sticks of vāsaka firewood offered [into the fire] grants victory in battle. / A wise person should make auspicious effigies of elephants, horses, and men out of flour.

260.s:
parakīyānathoddeśya pradhānapuruṣāṃs tathā /
susvinnān piṣṭakavarān kṣureṇot kṛtya bhāgaśaḥ //
260.d:
परकीयानथोद्देश्य प्रधानपुरुषांस् तथा /
सुस्विन्नान् पिष्टकवरान् क्षुरेणोत् कृत्य भागशः //
260.m: Specifying those belonging to the enemy as well as their foremost chiefs, / and cutting the well-steamed flour cakes into pieces with a razor,

260.s:
abhi tvā śūra ṇonumo mantreṇānena mantravit /
kṛtvā sarṣapatailāktān krodhena(2) juhuyāttataḥ //
:n
1 paripriyādeva kāririti kha.. , cha.. ca / paripriyādeva kaviriti gha.. , ña.. ca
2 mantreṇeti kha.. , cha.. , ja.. ca
:p 457
260.d:
अभि त्वा शूर णोनुमो मन्त्रेणानेन मन्त्रवित् /
कृत्वा सर्षपतैलाक्तान् क्रोधेन(2) जुहुयात्ततः //
:न्
1 परिप्रियादेव कारिरिति ख.. , छ.. च / परिप्रियादेव कविरिति घ.. , ञ.. च
2 मन्त्रेणेति ख.. , छ.. , ज.. च
:प् 457
260.m:
the knower of mantras, reciting the mantra 'abhi tvā śūra nonumaḥ', / should smear them with mustard oil and then offer them in the fire with wrath.
[Footnote]
[Variant readings:] 1. 'paripriyādeva kāriḥ' in manuscripts kha and cha; 'paripriyādeva kaviḥ' in manuscripts gha and ña.
2. 'mantreṇa' in manuscripts kha, cha, and ja.

260.s:
etat kṛtvā budhaḥ karma saṃgrāme jayamāpnuyāt /
gāruḍaṃ vāmadevyañca rathantaravṛhadrathau //
260.d:
एतत् कृत्वा बुधः कर्म संग्रामे जयमाप्नुयात् /
गारुडं वामदेव्यञ्च रथन्तरवृहद्रथौ //
260.m: Having performed this rite, the wise person attains victory in battle. / The Gāruḍa, Vāmadevya, Rathantara, and Bṛhadratha sāmans

260.s:
sarvapāpapraśamanāḥ kathitāḥ saṃśayaṃ vinā
//25//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe sāmavidhānaṃ nāma
ṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athaikaṣaṣṭhyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
atharvavidhānaṃ
260.d:
सर्वपापप्रशमनाः कथिताः संशयं विना
//25//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे सामविधानं नाम
षष्ट्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथैकषष्ठ्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
अथर्वविधानं
260.m:
are declared to pacify all sins without doubt. //25
Thus ends the two hundred and sixtieth chapter, entitled 'The Rules for Sāmans', in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the two hundred and sixty-first chapter.
Rules for the Atharva[veda]

261.s:
puṣkara uvāca
sāmnāṃ vidhānaṃ kathitaṃ vakṣye cātharvaṇāmatha /
śāntātīyaṃ gaṇaṃ hutvā śāntimāpnoti mānavaḥ //
261.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
साम्नां विधानं कथितं वक्ष्ये चाथर्वणामथ /
शान्तातीयं गणं हुत्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति मानवः //
261.m: Puṣkara said: / The ritual procedure for the Sāmans has been declared, and now I shall speak of the Atharvan hymns. / Having offered the Śāntātīya group into the fire, a man attains peace.

261.s:
bhaiṣajyañca gaṇaṃ hutvā sarvānrogān vyāpohati /
trisaptīyaṃ gaṇaṃ hutvā sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate //
261.d:
भैषज्यञ्च गणं हुत्वा सर्वान्रोगान् व्यापोहति /
त्रिसप्तीयं गणं हुत्वा सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते //
261.m: And having offered the Bhaiṣajya group into the fire, he dispels all diseases. / Having offered the Trisaptīya group into the fire, he is freed from all sins.

261.s:
kvacinnāpnoti ca bhayaṃ hutvā caivābhayaṅgaṇaṃ /
na kvacijjāyate rāma gaṇaṃ hutvā parājitaṃ //
261.d:
क्वचिन्नाप्नोति च भयं हुत्वा चैवाभयङ्गणं /
न क्वचिज्जायते राम गणं हुत्वा पराजितं //
261.m: And having offered the Abhaya group into the fire, he attains fear nowhere. / Having offered the Aparājita group into the fire, O Rāma, he is never defeated anywhere.

261.s:
āyuṣyañca gaṇaṃ hutvā apamṛtyuṃ vyapohati /
svastimāpnoti sarvatra hutvā svastyayanaṅgaṇaṃ //
261.d:
आयुष्यञ्च गणं हुत्वा अपमृत्युं व्यपोहति /
स्वस्तिमाप्नोति सर्वत्र हुत्वा स्वस्त्ययनङ्गणं //
261.m: And having offered the Āyuṣya group into the fire, he averts premature death. / Having offered the Svastyayana group into the fire, he attains well-being everywhere.

261.s:
śreyasā yogamāpnoti śarmavarmagaṇantathā /
vāstoṣpatyagaṇaṃ hutvā vāstudoṣān vyapohati //
261.d:
श्रेयसा योगमाप्नोति शर्मवर्मगणन्तथा /
वास्तोष्पत्यगणं हुत्वा वास्तुदोषान् व्यपोहति //
261.m: Likewise [offering] the Śarmavarman group, he attains union with the highest good. / Having offered the Vāstoṣpatya group into the fire, he dispels architectural defects of the site.

261.s:
tathā raudragaṇaṃ hutvā sarvān doṣān vyapohati /
etair daśaguṇair homī hy aṣṭādaśasu śāntiṣu //
261.d:
तथा रौद्रगणं हुत्वा सर्वान् दोषान् व्यपोहति /
एतैर् दशगुणैर् होमी ह्य् अष्टादशसु शान्तिषु //
261.m: Likewise, having offered the Raudra group into the fire, he dispels all afflictions. / One who performs fire oblations tenfold with these [hymns] indeed [succeeds] in the eighteen pacifying rites.

260-r2.m: [Page 458]

260-r2.s:
vaiṣṇavī śāntiraindrī ca brāhmī raudrī tathaiva ca /
vāyavyā vāruṇī caiva kauverī bhārgavī tathā //
260-r2.d:
वैष्णवी शान्तिरैन्द्री च ब्राह्मी रौद्री तथैव च /
वायव्या वारुणी चैव कौवेरी भार्गवी तथा //
260-r2.m:
the Vaiṣṇavī pacification, the Aindrī, the Brāhmī, and likewise the Raudrī,
the Vāyavyā, the Vāruṇī, the Kauverī, and the Bhārgavī,

260-r2.s:
prājāpatyā tathā tvāṣṭrī kaumārī vahnidevatā /
mārudgaṇā ca gāndhārī śāntair nairṛtakī tathā //
260-r2.d:
प्राजापत्या तथा त्वाष्ट्री कौमारी वह्निदेवता /
मारुद्गणा च गान्धारी शान्तैर् नैरृतकी तथा //
260-r2.m:
the Prājāpatyā, the Tvāṣṭrī, the Kaumārī, that of the god of fire,
that belonging to the troop of Maruts, the Gāndhārī, the Nairṛtī among pacifications,

260-r2.s:
śāntirāṅgirasī yāmyā pārthivī sarvakāmadā /
yastvāṃ mṛtyuriti hy etajjaptaṃ mṛtyuvināśanaṃ //
260-r2.d:
शान्तिराङ्गिरसी याम्या पार्थिवी सर्वकामदा /
यस्त्वां मृत्युरिति ह्य् एतज्जप्तं मृत्युविनाशनं //
260-r2.m:
the Āṅgirasī, the Yāmyā, and the Pārthivī, which grants all desires.
When recited, [the mantra] 'yastvāṃ mṛtyuḥ' destroys death.

260-r2.s:
suparṇastveti hutvā ca bhujagair naiva bādhyate /
indreṇa dattamityetat sarvakāmakarambhavet //
260-r2.d:
सुपर्णस्त्वेति हुत्वा च भुजगैर् नैव बाध्यते /
इन्द्रेण दत्तमित्येतत् सर्वकामकरम्भवेत् //
260-r2.m:
Having offered oblations with [the mantra beginning with] 'suparṇastvā', one is not afflicted by serpents.
The [mantra] 'indreṇa dattam' fulfills all desires.

260-r2.s:
indreṇa dattamityetat sarvabādhāvināśanaṃ /
imā devīti mantraś ca sarvaśāntikaraḥ paraḥ //
260-r2.d:
इन्द्रेण दत्तमित्येतत् सर्वबाधाविनाशनं /
इमा देवीति मन्त्रश् च सर्वशान्तिकरः परः //
260-r2.m:
The [mantra] 'indreṇa dattam' destroys all afflictions.
And the mantra 'imā devīḥ' is supreme for effecting all peace.

260-r2.s:
devā maruta ity etat sarvakāmakarambhavet /
yamasya lokādityetat duḥsvapnaśamanamparaṃ //
260-r2.d:
देवा मरुत इत्य् एतत् सर्वकामकरम्भवेत् /
यमस्य लोकादित्येतत् दुःस्वप्नशमनम्परं //
260-r2.m:
The [mantra] 'devā marutaḥ' fulfills all desires.
The [mantra] 'yamasya lokāt' is the supreme pacifier of bad dreams.

260-r2.s:
indraś ca pañcabaṇijeti(1) hutaṃ strīṇāṃ saubhāgyavardhanaṃ /
kāmo me vājīti hutaṃ strīṇāṃ saubhāgyavardhanaṃ //
260-r2.d:
इन्द्रश् च पञ्चबणिजेति(1) हुतं स्त्रीणां सौभाग्यवर्धनं /
कामो मे वाजीति हुतं स्त्रीणां सौभाग्यवर्धनं //
260-r2.m:
[The mantra beginning with] 'indraś ca pañcabaṇijā' offered into fire increases women's good fortune.
[The mantra beginning with] 'kāmo me vājī' offered into fire increases women's good fortune.

260-r2.s:
tubhyameva javīmannityayutantu hutambhavet /
agne gobhinna ity etat(2) medhāvṛddhikaramparaṃ //
260-r2.d:
तुभ्यमेव जवीमन्नित्ययुतन्तु हुतम्भवेत् /
अग्ने गोभिन्न इत्य् एतत्(2) मेधावृद्धिकरम्परं //
260-r2.m:
Ten thousand oblations should be offered with [the mantra beginning with] 'tubhyameva javīman'.
The [mantra] 'agne gobhinnaḥ' is supreme for increasing intelligence.

260-r2.s:
dhruvaṃ dhruveṇeti hutaṃ sthānalābhakaraṃ bhavet /
alaktajīveti śunā kṛṣilābhakaraṃ bhavet //
260-r2.d:
ध्रुवं ध्रुवेणेति हुतं स्थानलाभकरं भवेत् /
अलक्तजीवेति शुना कृषिलाभकरं भवेत् //
260-r2.m:
[The mantra] 'dhruvaṃ dhruveṇa' offered into fire grants the attainment of status.
The [mantra beginning with] 'alaktajīvā' [recited over] a dog brings profit from agriculture.

260-r2.s:
ahante bhagna ity etat bhavetsaubhāgyavardhanaṃ /
ye me pāśas tathāpyetat bandhanāmnokṣakāraṇaṃ //
260-r2.d:
अहन्ते भग्न इत्य् एतत् भवेत्सौभाग्यवर्धनं /
ये मे पाशस् तथाप्येतत् बन्धनाम्नोक्षकारणं //
260-r2.m:
The [mantra] 'ahante bhagnaḥ' increases good fortune.
Likewise, the [mantra] 'ye me pāśāḥ' brings liberation from fetters.

260-r2.s:
śapantvahanniti ripūn nāśayeddhomajāpyataḥ /
:n
1 indra vanaṃ vanik cetīti gha.. , ja.. ca
2 agne saubhāgya ity etaditi ja..
:p 459
tvamuttamamitītyetadyaśobuddhivivardhanaṃ //
260-r2.d:
शपन्त्वहन्निति रिपून् नाशयेद्धोमजाप्यतः /
:न्
1 इन्द्र वनं वनिक् चेतीति घ.. , ज.. च
2 अग्ने सौभाग्य इत्य् एतदिति ज..
:प् 459
त्वमुत्तममितीत्येतद्यशोबुद्धिविवर्धनं //
260-r2.m:
With [the mantra beginning with] 'śapantvahan', one destroys enemies through fire oblation and recitation.
[Footnote]
[Variant readings:] 1. 'indra vanaṃ vaṇik ca' in manuscripts gha and ja.
2. 'agne saubhāgya ity etat' in manuscript ja.
The [mantra beginning with] 'tvamuttamam' increases renown and intellect.

260-r2.s:
yathā mṛgamatītyetat strīṇāṃ saubhāgyavardhanaṃ /
yena cehadidañcaiva garbhalābhakaraṃ bhavet //
260-r2.d:
यथा मृगमतीत्येतत् स्त्रीणां सौभाग्यवर्धनं /
येन चेहदिदञ्चैव गर्भलाभकरं भवेत् //
260-r2.m:
The [hymn beginning with] "yathā mṛgam" increases the good fortune of women;
and that [beginning with] "yena ceha" brings about conception.

260-r2.s:
ayante yonirityetat putralābhakaraṃ bhavet /
śivaḥ śivābhirityetat bhavetsaubhāgyavardhanaṃ(1) //
260-r2.d:
अयन्ते योनिरित्येतत् पुत्रलाभकरं भवेत् /
शिवः शिवाभिरित्येतत् भवेत्सौभाग्यवर्धनं(1) //
260-r2.m:
"ayaṃ te yoniḥ" brings about the birth of a son;
"śivaḥ śivābhiḥ" increases good fortune.

260-r2.s:
vṛhaspatir naḥ paripātu pathi svastyayanaṃ bhavet /
muñcāmi tveti kathitamapamṛtyunivāraṇaṃ //
260-r2.d:
वृहस्पतिर् नः परिपातु पथि स्वस्त्ययनं भवेत् /
मुञ्चामि त्वेति कथितमपमृत्युनिवारणं //
260-r2.m:
"bṛhaspatir naḥ paripātu pathi" produces safe travel.
"muñcāmi tvā" is declared to ward off untimely death.

260-r2.s:
atharvaśiraso 'dhyetā sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate /
prādhānyena tu mantrāṇāṃ kiñcit karma taveritaṃ //
260-r2.d:
अथर्वशिरसो ऽध्येता सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते /
प्राधान्येन तु मन्त्राणां किञ्चित् कर्म तवेरितं //
260-r2.m:
He who recites the Atharvaśiras is freed from all sins.
Thus, primarily according to the mantras, a portion of ritual action has been declared to you.

260-r2.s:
vṛkṣāṇāṃ yajñiyānāntu samidhaḥ prathamaṃ haviḥ /
ājyañca vrīhayaś caiva tathā vai gaurasarṣapāḥ //
260-r2.d:
वृक्षाणां यज्ञियानान्तु समिधः प्रथमं हविः /
आज्यञ्च व्रीहयश् चैव तथा वै गौरसर्षपाः //
260-r2.m:
The prime offering is firewood of sacrificial trees;
clarified butter, paddy grains, and indeed white mustard seeds,

260-r2.s:
akṣatāni tilāś caiva dadhikṣīre ca bhārgava /
darbhāstathaiva dūrvāś ca vilvāni kamalāni ca //
260-r2.d:
अक्षतानि तिलाश् चैव दधिक्षीरे च भार्गव /
दर्भास्तथैव दूर्वाश् च विल्वानि कमलानि च //
260-r2.m:
unbroken barley grains, sesame seeds, curds, and milk, O descendant of Bhṛgu,
likewise darbha grass, dūrvā grass, vilva fruits, and lotuses:

260-r2.s:
śāntipuṣṭikarāṇyāhurdravyāṇyetāni sarvaśaḥ /
tailaṅkaṇāni dharmajña rājikā rudhiraṃ viṣaṃ //
260-r2.d:
शान्तिपुष्टिकराण्याहुर्द्रव्याण्येतानि सर्वशः /
तैलङ्कणानि धर्मज्ञ राजिका रुधिरं विषं //
260-r2.m:
they say that all these substances produce pacification and nourishment.
O knower of dharma, oil, broken grains, black mustard, blood, poison,

260-r2.s:
samidhaḥ kaṇṭakopetā abhicāreṣu yojayet /
ārṣaṃ vai daivataṃ chando viniyogajña ācaret //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe atharvavidhānaṃ
nāmaikaṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:n
1 kruddhaṃ bhūpaṃ prasādayediti gha.. , ja.. , jha.. ca
:p 460
:ś atha dviṣaṣṭhyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
utpātaśāntiḥ
260-r2.d:
समिधः कण्टकोपेता अभिचारेषु योजयेत् /
आर्षं वै दैवतं छन्दो विनियोगज्ञ आचरेत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे अथर्वविधानं
नामैकषष्ट्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:न्
1 क्रुद्धं भूपं प्रसादयेदिति घ.. , ज.. , झ.. च
:प् 460
:श् अथ द्विषष्ठ्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
उत्पातशान्तिः
260-r2.m:
[and] thorny firewood one should employ in hostile sorcery rites.
One who knows their ritual application should perform [them with knowledge of] the seer, the deity, and the metre.
Thus ends the two hundred and sixty-first chapter, entitled "The Atharva Regulations", in the great Agni Purāṇa.
[Footnote]
1. "kruddhaṃ bhūpaṃ prasādayet" thus in manuscripts gha, ja, and jha. / [Page 460]
Now begins the two hundred and sixty-second chapter:
Pacification of Portents.

262.s:
puṣkara uvāca
śrīsūktaṃ prativedañca jñeyaṃ lakṣmīvivardhanaṃ /
hiraṇyavarṇā hariṇīmṛcaḥ pañcadaśa śriyaḥ //
262.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
श्रीसूक्तं प्रतिवेदञ्च ज्ञेयं लक्ष्मीविवर्धनं /
हिरण्यवर्णा हरिणीमृचः पञ्चदश श्रियः //

262.s:
ratheṣvakṣeṣu vājeti catasro yajuṣi śriyaḥ /
srāvantīyaṃ tathā sāma śrīsūktaṃ sāmavedake //
262.d:
रथेष्वक्षेषु वाजेति चतस्रो यजुषि श्रियः /
स्रावन्तीयं तथा साम श्रीसूक्तं सामवेदके //
262.m:
"ratheṣv akṣeṣu vājeṣu" comprises four verses to Śrī in the Yajurveda;
likewise the Srāvantīya chant is the Śrīsūkta in the Sāmaveda.

262.s:
śriyaṃ dhātarmayi dhehi prāktamātharvaṇe tathā /
śrīsūktaṃ yo japedbhaktyā hutvā śrīstasya vai bhavet //
262.d:
श्रियं धातर्मयि धेहि प्राक्तमाथर्वणे तथा /
श्रीसूक्तं यो जपेद्भक्त्या हुत्वा श्रीस्तस्य वै भवेत् //
262.m:
In the Atharvaveda, it is recited as "śriyaṃ dhātar mayi dhehi".
He who, with devotion, offers fire oblations and recites the Śrīsūkta, prosperity shall be his.

262.s:
padmāni cātha vilvāni hutvājyaṃ vā tilān śriyaḥ /
ekantu pauruṣaṃ sūktaṃ prativedantu sarvadaṃ //
262.d:
पद्मानि चाथ विल्वानि हुत्वाज्यं वा तिलान् श्रियः /
एकन्तु पौरुषं सूक्तं प्रतिवेदन्तु सर्वदं //
262.m:
Having offered lotuses, vilva fruits, clarified butter, or sesame seeds of Śrī—
and the single Puruṣasūkta in each Veda bestows all things.

262.s:
sūktena ddadyānniṣpāpo hy ekaikayā(1) jalāñjaliṃ /
snāta ekaikayā puṣpaṃ viṣṇordatvāghahā bhavet //
262.d:
सूक्तेन द्दद्यान्निष्पापो ह्य् एकैकया(1) जलाञ्जलिं /
स्नात एकैकया पुष्पं विष्णोर्दत्वाघहा भवेत् //
262.m:
Freed from sin, one should offer a handful of water with each [verse of the] sūkta;
having bathed, giving a flower to Viṣṇu with each one, he becomes a destroyer of sins.

262.s:
snāta ekaikayā datvā phalaṃ syāt sarvakāmabhāk /
mahāpāpopapānto bhavejjaptvā tu pauruṣaṃ //
262.d:
स्नात एकैकया दत्वा फलं स्यात् सर्वकामभाक् /
महापापोपपान्तो भवेज्जप्त्वा तु पौरुषं //
262.m:
Having bathed, by offering a fruit with each one, he enjoys all desires.
Having recited the Puruṣasūkta, he is freed from mortal sins and minor sins.

262.s:
kṛcchrair viśuddho japtvā ca hutvā snātvātha sarvabhāk /
aṣṭādaśabhyaḥ śāntibhyastisro 'nyāḥ śāntayo varāḥ //
262.d:
कृच्छ्रैर् विशुद्धो जप्त्वा च हुत्वा स्नात्वाथ सर्वभाक् /
अष्टादशभ्यः शान्तिभ्यस्तिस्रो ऽन्याः शान्तयो वराः //
262.m:
Purified by kṛcchra penances, reciting [it], offering fire oblations, and having bathed, he enjoys all.
Out of eighteen pacifications, three other pacifications are the best:

262.s:
amṛtā cābhayavā saumyā sarvotpātavimardanāḥ /
amṛtā sarvadavatyā abhayā brahmadaivatā //
262.d:
अमृता चाभयवा सौम्या सर्वोत्पातविमर्दनाः /
अमृता सर्वदवत्या अभया ब्रह्मदैवता //
262.m:
the Amṛtā, the Abhayā, and the Saumyā, which crush all portents.
The Amṛtā has all deities as its divinity; the Abhayā has Brahmā as its deity;

262.s:
saumyā ca sarvadaivatyā ekā syātsarvakāmadā /
:n
1 hy ekaikaśa iti ka.. , gha.. , cha.. , ña.. ca
:p 461
abhayāyā maṇiḥ kāryo varuṇasya bhṛgūttama //
262.d:
सौम्या च सर्वदैवत्या एका स्यात्सर्वकामदा /
:न्
1 ह्य् एकैकश इति क.. , घ.. , छ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 461
अभयाया मणिः कार्यो वरुणस्य भृगूत्तम //
262.m:
and the Saumyā has all deities as its divinity; each single one grants all desires.
[Footnote]
1. "hy ekaikaśaḥ" thus in manuscripts ka, gha, cha, and ña. / [Page 461]
For the Abhayā, an amulet of Varuṇa should be made, O best of the Bhṛgus;

262.s:
śatakāṇḍo 'mṛtāyāś ca saumyāyāḥ śaṅkajo maṇiḥ /
taddaivatyās tathā mantrāḥ siddhau(1) syānmaṇibandhanaṃ //
262.d:
शतकाण्डो ऽमृतायाश् च सौम्यायाः शङ्कजो मणिः /
तद्दैवत्यास् तथा मन्त्राः सिद्धौ(1) स्यान्मणिबन्धनं //
262.m:
the hundred-knotted [dūrvā] for the Amṛtā, and an amulet made of conch for the Saumyā.
Likewise the mantras belong to those deities; upon accomplishment, tying the amulet should take place.

262.s:
divyāntarīkṣabhaumādisamutpātārdanā imāḥ /
divyāntarīkṣabhaumantu adbhutaṃ trividhaṃ śṛṇu //
262.d:
दिव्यान्तरीक्षभौमादिसमुत्पातार्दना इमाः /
दिव्यान्तरीक्षभौमन्तु अद्भुतं त्रिविधं शृणु //
262.m:
These destroy celestial, atmospheric, and terrestrial portents.
Hear from me about the three kinds of portents—celestial, atmospheric, and terrestrial:

262.s:
graharkṣavaikṛtaṃ divyamāntarīkṣannibodha me /
ulkāpātaś ca digdāhaḥ pariveśastathaiva ca //
262.d:
ग्रहर्क्षवैकृतं दिव्यमान्तरीक्षन्निबोध मे /
उल्कापातश् च दिग्दाहः परिवेशस्तथैव च //
262.m:
aberrations of planets and lunar mansions are celestial; know from me the atmospheric:
the fall of meteors, the red glow of the horizon, and likewise halos [around the sun or moon],

262.s:
gandharvanagarañcaiva vṛṣṭiś ca vikṛtā ca yā /
carasthirabhavaṃ bhūmau bhūkampamapi bhūmijaṃ //
262.d:
गन्धर्वनगरञ्चैव वृष्टिश् च विकृता च या /
चरस्थिरभवं भूमौ भूकम्पमपि भूमिजं //
262.m:
and the city of the Gandharvas, and unnatural rainfall.
Whatever occurs among mobile or immobile things on earth, and an earthquake, is born of the earth.

262.s:
saptāhābhyanatare vṛṣṭāvadbhutaṃ bhayakṛdbhavet /
śāntiṃ vinā tribhirvaṣair adbhutaṃ bhayakṛdbhavet //
262.d:
सप्ताहाभ्यनतरे वृष्टावद्भुतं भयकृद्भवेत् /
शान्तिं विना त्रिभिर्वषैर् अद्भुतं भयकृद्भवेत् //
262.m:
If rain falls within a week [of it], the portent causes fear;
without pacification, the portent causes fear for three years.

262.s:
devatārcāḥ(2) pranṛtyanti vepante prajvalanti ca /
āraṭhanti(3) ca rodanti prasvidyante hasanti ca //
262.d:
देवतार्चाः(2) प्रनृत्यन्ति वेपन्ते प्रज्वलन्ति च /
आरठन्ति(3) च रोदन्ति प्रस्विद्यन्ते हसन्ति च //
262.m:
If divine images dance, tremble, and blaze,
or wail, weep, perspire, and laugh,

262.s:
arcāvikāropaśamo 'bhyarcya hutvā prajāpateḥ /
anagnirdīpyate yatra rāṣṭre ca bhṛśanisvanaṃ //
262.d:
अर्चाविकारोपशमो ऽभ्यर्च्य हुत्वा प्रजापतेः /
अनग्निर्दीप्यते यत्र राष्ट्रे च भृशनिस्वनं //
262.m:
the pacification of a change in an image is performed after worship and fire oblations to Prajāpati.
Where fire blazes without fuel in a kingdom and makes a loud sound,

262.s:
na dīpyate cendhanavāṃstadrāṣṭraṃ pāḍyate nṛpaiḥ /
agnivaikṛtyaśamanamagnimantraiś ca bhārgava //
262.d:
न दीप्यते चेन्धनवांस्तद्राष्ट्रं पाड्यते नृपैः /
अग्निवैकृत्यशमनमग्निमन्त्रैश् च भार्गव //
262.m:
or does not blaze even when supplied with fuel, that kingdom is oppressed by kings.
The pacification of fire's unnatural state is by means of Agni's mantras, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

262.s:
akāle phalitā vṛkṣāḥ kṣīraṃ raktaṃ sravanti ca /
vṛkṣotpātapraśamanaṃ śivaṃ pūjya ca kārayet //
262.d:
अकाले फलिता वृक्षाः क्षीरं रक्तं स्रवन्ति च /
वृक्षोत्पातप्रशमनं शिवं पूज्य च कारयेत् //
262.m:
When trees bear fruit out of season, and ooze milk or blood,
one should bring about the pacification of tree portents by worshipping Śiva.

262.s:
ativṛṣṭiranāvṛṣṭirdurbhikṣāyobhayaṃ mataṃ /
:n
1 siddhyā iti gha.. , ña.. ca
2 devatāśceti kha.. , cha.. ca
3 āvaṭantīti kha.. , gha.. , cha.. , ña.. ca
:p 462
anṛtau tridinārabdhavṛṣṭirjñeyā bhayāya hi //
262.d:
अतिवृष्टिरनावृष्टिर्दुर्भिक्षायोभयं मतं /
:न्
1 सिद्ध्या इति घ.. , ञ.. च
2 देवताश्चेति ख.. , छ.. च
3 आवटन्तीति ख.. , घ.. , छ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 462
अनृतौ त्रिदिनारब्धवृष्टिर्ज्ञेया भयाय हि //
262.m:
Excessive rain and drought are both considered to lead to famine.
[Footnote] / 1. "siddhyā" thus in manuscripts gha and ña.
2. "devatāś ca" thus in manuscripts kha and cha.
3. "āvaṭan" thus in manuscripts kha, gha, cha, and ña. / [Page 462]
Rain beginning out of season and lasting three days should be known to cause fear.

262.s:
vṛṣṭivaikṛtyanāśaḥ syātparjaṇyendvarkapūjanāt /
nagarādapasarpante samīpamupayānti ca //
262.d:
वृष्टिवैकृत्यनाशः स्यात्पर्जण्येन्द्वर्कपूजनात् /
नगरादपसर्पन्ते समीपमुपयान्ति च //
262.m:
The destruction of unnatural rainfall comes from worshipping Parjanya, the Moon, and the Sun.
If rivers, lakes, and springs withdraw from a city,

262.s:
nadyo hradapraśravaṇā virasāś ca bhavanti ca /
śalilāśayavaikṛtye japtavyo vāruṇo manuḥ //
262.d:
नद्यो ह्रदप्रश्रवणा विरसाश् च भवन्ति च /
शलिलाशयवैकृत्ये जप्तव्यो वारुणो मनुः //
262.m:
or draw near it, or become tasteless—
in the case of an unnatural state of bodies of water, the mantra of Varuṇa is to be recited.

262.s:
akālaprasavā nāryaḥ kālato vāprajās tathā /
vikṛtaprasavāś caiva yugmaprasavanādikaṃ //
262.d:
अकालप्रसवा नार्यः कालतो वाप्रजास् तथा /
विकृतप्रसवाश् चैव युग्मप्रसवनादिकं //
262.m:
When women give birth out of season, or produce no offspring in season,
or have unnatural births, twins, and the like,

262.s:
strīṇāṃ prasavavaikṛtye strīviprādiṃ prapūjayet /
vaḍavā hastinī gaurvā yadi yugmaṃ prasūyate //
262.d:
स्त्रीणां प्रसववैकृत्ये स्त्रीविप्रादिं प्रपूजयेत् /
वडवा हस्तिनी गौर्वा यदि युग्मं प्रसूयते //
262.m:
in an unnatural state of women's childbirth, one should worship women, brāhmaṇas, and others.
If a mare, female elephant, or cow gives birth to twins,

262.s:
vijātyaṃ vikṛtaṃ vāpi ṣaḍbhirmāsair mriyeta vai /
vikṛtaṃ vā prasūyante paracakrabhayaṃ bhavet //
262.d:
विजात्यं विकृतं वापि षड्भिर्मासैर् म्रियेत वै /
विकृतं वा प्रसूयन्ते परचक्रभयं भवेत् //
262.m:
or to a different species or a deformed creature, it surely dies in six months;
or if they give birth to monstrosities, there will be danger from an enemy army.

262.s:
homaḥ prasūtivaikṛtye japo viprādipūjanaṃ /
yāni yānānyayuktāni yuktāni na vahanti ca //
262.d:
होमः प्रसूतिवैकृत्ये जपो विप्रादिपूजनं /
यानि यानान्ययुक्तानि युक्तानि न वहन्ति च //
262.m:
In the case of an unnatural birth, a fire oblation, recitation, and the worship of brāhmaṇas and others [should be performed].
When unhitched conveyances move, and hitched ones do not carry [their loads],

262.s:
ākāśe tūryanādāś ca mahadbhayamupasthitaṃ /
praviśanti yadā grāmamāraṇyā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ //
262.d:
आकाशे तूर्यनादाश् च महद्भयमुपस्थितं /
प्रविशन्ति यदा ग्राममारण्या मृगपक्षिणः //
262.m:
and the sounds of musical instruments [are heard] in the sky, great danger is imminent.
When wild beasts and birds enter a village,

262.s:
araṇyaṃ yānti vā grāmyāḥ jalaṃ yānti sthalodbhavāḥ /
sthalaṃ vā jalajā yānti rājadvārādike śivāḥ //
262.d:
अरण्यं यान्ति वा ग्राम्याः जलं यान्ति स्थलोद्भवाः /
स्थलं वा जलजा यान्ति राजद्वारादिके शिवाः //
262.m: or domestic animals go into the forest; when land animals enter water, / or aquatic creatures go onto land; or when jackals [cry] at the king's gate and the like;

262.s:
pradoṣe kukkuṭo vāse śivā cārkodaye bhavet /
gṛhaṅkapotaḥ praviśet kravyāhā mūrdhni līyate //
262.d:
प्रदोषे कुक्कुटो वासे शिवा चार्कोदये भवेत् /
गृहङ्कपोतः प्रविशेत् क्रव्याहा मूर्ध्नि लीयते //
262.m:
or a rooster cries at dusk, or a jackal [howls] at sunrise;
or a pigeon enters a house, or a flesh-eating bird perches on a person's head;

262.s:
madhurāṃ makṣikāṃ kuryāt kāko maithunago dṛśi /
prāsādatoraṇodyānadvāraprākāraveśmanāṃ //
262.d:
मधुरां मक्षिकां कुर्यात् काको मैथुनगो दृशि /
प्रासादतोरणोद्यानद्वारप्राकारवेश्मनां //
262.m:
or a fly produces honey, or a crow is seen mating;
or the motiveless collapse of temples, archways, gardens,

262.s:
animittantu patanaṃ dṛḍhānāṃ rājamṛtyave /
rajasā vātha dhūmena diśo yatra samākulāḥ //
:p 463
262.d:
अनिमित्तन्तु पतनं दृढानां राजमृत्यवे /
रजसा वाथ धूमेन दिशो यत्र समाकुलाः //
:प् 463

262.s:
ketūdayoparāgau ca chidratā śaśisūryayoḥ /
graharkṣavikṛtiryatra tatrāpi bhayamādiśet //
262.d:
केतूदयोपरागौ च छिद्रता शशिसूर्ययोः /
ग्रहर्क्षविकृतिर्यत्र तत्रापि भयमादिशेत् //
262.m: The appearance of comets, eclipses, and blemishes on the moon and sun, / and where there is abnormality among the planets and asterisms: there too one should predict danger.

262.s:
agniryatra ma dīpyeta sravante codakambhakāḥ /
mṛtirbhayaṃ śūnyatādirutpātānāṃ phalambhavet //
262.d:
अग्निर्यत्र म दीप्येत स्रवन्ते चोदकम्भकाः /
मृतिर्भयं शून्यतादिरुत्पातानां फलम्भवेत् //
262.m: Where fire does not burn, and water-jars leak, / death, danger, desolation, and the like will be the fruit of portents.

262.s:
dvijadevādipūjābhyaḥ śāntirjapyaistu homataḥ //33//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe utpātaśāntirnāma
dviṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha triṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
devapūjāvaiśvadevabaliḥ
262.d:
द्विजदेवादिपूजाभ्यः शान्तिर्जप्यैस्तु होमतः //33//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे उत्पातशान्तिर्नाम
द्विषष्ट्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ त्रिषष्ट्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
देवपूजावैश्वदेवबलिः
262.m:
Pacification comes from worship of twice-born and deities, and through recitation [of mantras] and fire oblation. // 33
Thus ends the two hundred and sixty-second chapter in the great Purāṇa of Agni, entitled 'Pacification of Portents.'
Now begins the two hundred and sixty-third chapter:
Worship of the deities and the Vaiśvadeva offering.

263.s:
puṣkara uvāca
devapūjādikaṃ karma vakṣye cotpātamardanam /
āpohiṣṭeti tisṛbhiḥ snāto 'rghyaṃ vioṣṇaverpayet //
263.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
देवपूजादिकं कर्म वक्ष्ये चोत्पातमर्दनम् /
आपोहिष्टेति तिसृभिः स्नातो ऽर्घ्यं विओष्णवेर्पयेत् //
263.m: Puṣkara said: / I will speak of the rite consisting of worship of the gods and the like, which crushes portents. / Having bathed, one should offer water offering to Viṣṇu with the three verses beginning with 'āpo hi ṣṭhā'.

263.s:
hiraṇyavarṇā iti ca pādyañca tisṛbhirdvija /
śanna āpo hy ācamanamidamāpo 'bhiṣecanaṃ //
263.d:
हिरण्यवर्णा इति च पाद्यञ्च तिसृभिर्द्विज /
शन्न आपो ह्य् आचमनमिदमापो ऽभिषेचनं //
263.m: And foot-water with the three verses beginning with 'hiraṇyavarṇāḥ', O twice-born, / sipping water with 'śaṃ na āpaḥ', and aspersion with 'idam āpaḥ'.

263.s:
rathe akṣe ca tisṛbhirgandhaṃ yuveti(1) vastrakaṃ /
puṣpaṃ puṣpavatītyevaṃ dhūpandhūposi cāpyatha //
263.d:
रथे अक्षे च तिसृभिर्गन्धं युवेति(1) वस्त्रकं /
पुष्पं पुष्पवतीत्येवं धूपन्धूपोसि चाप्यथ //
263.m: Perfume with the three verses 'rathe akṣe', garment with 'yuvā', / flower with 'puṣpavatī', and incense with 'dhūpo 'si'.

263.s:
tejosi śukraṃ dīpaṃ syānmadhuparkaṃ dadhīti ca /
hiraṇyagarbha ity aṣṭāvṛcaḥ proktā nivedane //
263.d:
तेजोसि शुक्रं दीपं स्यान्मधुपर्कं दधीति च /
हिरण्यगर्भ इत्य् अष्टावृचः प्रोक्ता निवेदने //
263.m: Lamp should be offered with 'tejo 'si śukram', and madhuparka with 'dadhikrāvṇaḥ'. / Eight verses beginning with 'hiraṇyagarbhaḥ' are prescribed for offering

263.s:
annasya manujaśreṣṭha pānasya ca sugandhinaḥ /
cāmaravyajanopānacchatraṃ yānāsane tathā //
:n
1 gandhaṃ svadheti ka.. , ga.. ,gha.. , ja.. ca
:p 464
263.d:
अन्नस्य मनुजश्रेष्ठ पानस्य च सुगन्धिनः /
चामरव्यजनोपानच्छत्रं यानासने तथा //
:न्
1 गन्धं स्वधेति क.. , ग.. ,घ.. , ज.. च
:प् 464
263.m:
food, O best of men, and fragrant drink; / likewise a flywhisk, fan, shoes, parasol, vehicle, and seat.
[Footnote]
1. "gandhaṃ svadhā" thus in manuscripts ka, ga, gha, and ja. / [Page 464]

263.s:
yat kiñcidevamādi syātsāvitreṇa nivedayet /
pauruṣantu japet sūktaṃ tadeva juhuyāttathā //
263.d:
यत् किञ्चिदेवमादि स्यात्सावित्रेण निवेदयेत् /
पौरुषन्तु जपेत् सूक्तं तदेव जुहुयात्तथा //
