263.m: Whatever else there may be of this sort, one should offer with the Sāvitrī verse. / One should recite the Puruṣasūkta and also offer fire oblations with it.

263.s:
arcābhave tathā vedyāñjale pūrṇaghate tathā /
nadītīre 'tha kamale śāntiḥ syādviṣṇupūjanāt //
263.d:
अर्चाभवे तथा वेद्याञ्जले पूर्णघते तथा /
नदीतीरे ऽथ कमले शान्तिः स्याद्विष्णुपूजनात् //
263.m: In an image, or on an altar, in water, in a full water-jar, / on a riverbank, or upon a lotus, pacification arises from the worship of Viṣṇu.

263.s:
tato homaḥ prakartavyo dīpyamāne vibhāvasau /
parisammṛjya paryukṣya paristīrya paristaraiḥ //
263.d:
ततो होमः प्रकर्तव्यो दीप्यमाने विभावसौ /
परिसम्मृज्य पर्युक्ष्य परिस्तीर्य परिस्तरैः //
263.m: Then fire oblation is to be performed when the fire is blazing, / having swept round, sprinkled round, and strewed [the altar] with strew-grasses.

263.s:
sarvānnāgraṃ samuddhṛtya juhuyāt prayatastataḥ /
vāsudevāya devāya prabhave cāvyayāya ca //
263.d:
सर्वान्नाग्रं समुद्धृत्य जुहुयात् प्रयतस्ततः /
वासुदेवाय देवाय प्रभवे चाव्ययाय च //
263.m: Taking a portion of the foremost of all the food, one should then attentively offer fire oblations / to Lord Vāsudeva, the sovereign and imperishable;

263.s:
agnaye caiva somāya mitrāya varuṇāya ca /
indrāya ca mahābhāga indrāgnibhyāṃ tathaiva ca //
263.d:
अग्नये चैव सोमाय मित्राय वरुणाय च /
इन्द्राय च महाभाग इन्द्राग्निभ्यां तथैव च //
263.m: to Agni, to Soma, to Mitra, and to Varuṇa; / to Indra, O noble one, and likewise to Indrāgni;

263.s:
viśvebhyaś caiva devebhyaḥ prajānāṃ pataye namaḥ /
anumatyai tathā rāma dhanvantaraya eva ca //
263.d:
विश्वेभ्यश् चैव देवेभ्यः प्रजानां पतये नमः /
अनुमत्यै तथा राम धन्वन्तरय एव च //
263.m: to the All-Gods, 'Homage to the Lord of Creatures'; / to Anumati, O Rāma, and likewise to Dhanvantari;

263.s:
vāstoṣpatyai tato devyai tataḥ sviṣṭikṛte 'gnaye /
sacaturthyantanāmnā(1) tu hutvaitebhyo baliṃ haret //
263.d:
वास्तोष्पत्यै ततो देव्यै ततः स्विष्टिकृते ऽग्नये /
सचतुर्थ्यन्तनाम्ना(1) तु हुत्वैतेभ्यो बलिं हरेत् //
263.m: then to the goddess presiding over the home, and then to Agni Sviṣṭakṛt. / Having offered fire oblations to these with their names ending in the dative case, one should present the food offering.

263.s:
takṣopatakṣamabhitaḥ pūrveṇāgnimataḥ param /
aśvānāmapi dharmajña ūrṇānāmāni cāpyatha //
263.d:
तक्षोपतक्षमभितः पूर्वेणाग्निमतः परम् /
अश्वानामपि धर्मज्ञ ऊर्णानामानि चाप्यथ //
263.m: On either side of Takṣa and Upatakṣa, and beyond that to the east of the fire, / O knower of righteousness, and then the names of the horses and the woolen-clad deities:

263.s:
nirundhī dhūmriṇīkā ca asvapantī(2) tathaiva ca /
meghapatnī(3) ca nāmāni sarveṣāmeva bhārgava //
263.d:
निरुन्धी धूम्रिणीका च अस्वपन्ती(2) तथैव च /
मेघपत्नी(3) च नामानि सर्वेषामेव भार्गव //
263.m: Nirundhī, Dhūmriṇīkā, Asvapantī, / and Meghapatnī—all these names indeed, O Bhārgava,

263.s:
āgneyādyāḥ krameṇātha tataḥ śaktiṣu nikṣipet /
nandinyai ca subhāgyai ca sumaṅgalyai ca bhārgava //
:n
1 sa caturthīkanāmneti pāṭhaḥ sādhuḥ
2 aśvaparṇīti ja..
3 meghaparṇīti ja..
:p 465
263.d:
आग्नेयाद्याः क्रमेणाथ ततः शक्तिषु निक्षिपेत् /
नन्दिन्यै च सुभाग्यै च सुमङ्गल्यै च भार्गव //
:न्
1 स चतुर्थीकनाम्नेति पाठः साधुः
2 अश्वपर्णीति ज..
3 मेघपर्णीति ज..
:प् 465
263.m:
beginning with Agni in order. Then one should cast offerings to the powers: / to Nandinī, to Subhāgyā, and to Sumaṅgalā, O Bhārgava;
[Footnote]
1. The reading "sa caturthīkanāmnā" is correct.
2. "aśvaparṇī" thus in manuscript ja.
3. "meghaparṇī" thus in manuscript ja. / [Page 465]

263.s:
bhadrakālyai tato datvā sthūṇāyāñca tathā śriye /
hiraṇyakeśyai ca tathā vanaspataya eva ca //
263.d:
भद्रकाल्यै ततो दत्वा स्थूणायाञ्च तथा श्रिये /
हिरण्यकेश्यै च तथा वनस्पतय एव च //
263.m: then having given to Bhadrakālī, and likewise at the post to Śrī, / and to Hiraṇyakeśī, and also to Vanaspati;

263.s:
dharmādharmamayau dvāre gṛhamadhye dhruvāya ca /
mṛtyave ca vahirdadyādvaruṇāyodakāśaye //
263.d:
धर्माधर्ममयौ द्वारे गृहमध्ये ध्रुवाय च /
मृत्यवे च वहिर्दद्याद्वरुणायोदकाशये //
263.m: to the two consisting of righteousness and unrighteousness at the door, and in the middle of the house to Dhruva; / one should give outside to Death, and to Varuṇa at a reservoir of water;

263.s:
bhūtebhyaś ca bahirdadyāccharaṇe dhanadāya ca /
indrāyendrapuruṣebhyo dadyāt pūrveṇa mānavaḥ //
263.d:
भूतेभ्यश् च बहिर्दद्याच्छरणे धनदाय च /
इन्द्रायेन्द्रपुरुषेभ्यो दद्यात् पूर्वेण मानवः //
263.m: and outside to the spirits, and in the shelter to the Bestower of Wealth; / a man should give to the east to Indra and Indra's attendants;

263.s:
yamāya tatpuruṣebhyo dadyāddakṣiṇatas tathā /
varuṇāya tatpuruṣebhyo dadyātpaścimatas tathā //
263.d:
यमाय तत्पुरुषेभ्यो दद्याद्दक्षिणतस् तथा /
वरुणाय तत्पुरुषेभ्यो दद्यात्पश्चिमतस् तथा //
263.m: he should give to the south to Yama and his attendants; / he should give to the west to Varuṇa and his attendants;

263.s:
somāya somapuruṣebhya udagdadyādanantaraṃ /
brahmaṇe brahmapuruṣebhyo madhye dadyāttathaiva ca //
263.d:
सोमाय सोमपुरुषेभ्य उदग्दद्यादनन्तरं /
ब्रह्मणे ब्रह्मपुरुषेभ्यो मध्ये दद्यात्तथैव च //
263.m: thereafter he should give to the north to Soma and Soma's attendants; / and likewise in the center he should give to Brahmā and Brahmā's attendants;

263.s:
ākāśe ca tathā cordhve sthaṇḍilāya kṣitau tathā /
divā divācarebhyaś ca rātrau rātricareṣu ca //
263.d:
आकाशे च तथा चोर्ध्वे स्थण्डिलाय क्षितौ तथा /
दिवा दिवाचरेभ्यश् च रात्रौ रात्रिचरेषु च //
263.m: and likewise above in the sky, and on the ground to the sacrificial ground; / by day to those who roam by day, and at night to those who roam at night.

263.s:
baliṃ vahis tathā dadyātsāyaṃ prātastu pratyahaṃ /
piṇḍanirvapaṇaṃ kuryāt prātaḥ sāyanna kārayet //
263.d:
बलिं वहिस् तथा दद्यात्सायं प्रातस्तु प्रत्यहं /
पिण्डनिर्वपणं कुर्यात् प्रातः सायन्न कारयेत् //
263.m: He should thus give the food offering outside every day, morning and evening. / He should make the offering of rice-balls in the morning; he should not do it in the evening.

263.s:
pitre tu prathamaṃ dadyāttatpitre tadanantaram /
prapitāmahāya tanmātre pitṛmātre tato 'rpayet //
263.d:
पित्रे तु प्रथमं दद्यात्तत्पित्रे तदनन्तरम् /
प्रपितामहाय तन्मात्रे पितृमात्रे ततो ऽर्पयेत् //
263.m: He should give first to the father, immediately after to his father, / [then] to the paternal great-grandfather, then offer to his mother, [and] to the father's mother;

263.s:
tanmātre dakṣiṇāgreṣu kuśeṣvevaṃ yajet pitṝn /
indravāruṇavāyavyā yāmyā vā nairṛtāya ye //
263.d:
तन्मात्रे दक्षिणाग्रेषु कुशेष्वेवं यजेत् पितॄन् /
इन्द्रवारुणवायव्या याम्या वा नैरृताय ये //
263.m: [and] to her mother; thus he should worship the ancestors on kuśa grass pointing south. / 'Those crows belonging to Indra, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Yama, or Nirṛti—

263.s:
te kākāḥ pitṛgṛhantu imaṃ piṇḍaṃ mayodvṛtam /
kākapiṇḍantu mantreṇa śunaḥ piṇḍaṃ pradāpayet //
263.d:
ते काकाः पितृगृहन्तु इमं पिण्डं मयोद्वृतम् /
काकपिण्डन्तु मन्त्रेण शुनः पिण्डं प्रदापयेत् //
263.m: let them take this ball of food raised by me for the ancestors.' / With this mantra for the crow's ball of food, he should also cause a ball of food to be given to the dog:

263.s:
vivasvataḥ kule jātau dvau śyāvaśabalau(1) śunau /
teṣāṃ piṇḍaṃ pradāsyāmi pathi rakṣantu me sadā //
:n
1 śyāmaśabalāviti ja.. , ña.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 466
263.d:
विवस्वतः कुले जातौ द्वौ श्यावशबलौ(1) शुनौ /
तेषां पिण्डं प्रदास्यामि पथि रक्षन्तु मे सदा //
:न्
1 श्यामशबलाविति ज.. , ञ.. , ट.. च
:प् 466
263.m:
'The two dark and brindled dogs born in the lineage of Vivasvat: / to them I shall give a ball of food; let them protect me always on the road.'
[Footnote]
1. "śyāmaśabalau" thus in manuscripts ja, ña, and ṭa. / [Page 466]

263.s:
saurabheyyaḥ(1) sarvahitāḥ pavitrāḥ pāpanāśanāḥ(2) /
pratigṛhṇantu me grāsaṃ gāvastrailokyamātaraḥ //
263.d:
सौरभेय्यः(1) सर्वहिताः पवित्राः पापनाशनाः(2) /
प्रतिगृह्णन्तु मे ग्रासं गावस्त्रैलोक्यमातरः //
263.m: 'May the daughters of Surabhi, beneficent to all, pure, destroyers of sin, / mothers of the three worlds, the cows, receive my morsel.'

263.s:
grogrāsañca svastyayanaṃ kṛtvā bhikṣāṃ pradāpayet /
atithīndīnān pūjayitvā gṛhī bhuñjīta ca svayaṃ //
oṃ bhūḥ svāhā oṃ bhūvaḥ svāhā oṃ svaḥ svāhā oṃ
bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā
oṃ devakṛtasyainaso 'vayajanamasi svāhā oṃ pitṛkṛtasyainaso
'vayajanamasi svāhā oṃ ātmakṛtasyainaso 'vayajanamasi svāhā oṃ
manuṣyakṛtasyainaso 'vayajanamasi svāhā oṃ enasa enaso 'vayajanamasi
svāhā / yaccāhameno vidvāṃś cakāra yaccavidvāṃstasya sarvasyainaso
'vayajanamasi svāhā agnaye sviṣṭikṛte svāhā oṃ prajāpataye svāhā
||
263.d:
ग्रोग्रासञ्च स्वस्त्ययनं कृत्वा भिक्षां प्रदापयेत् /
अतिथीन्दीनान् पूजयित्वा गृही भुञ्जीत च स्वयं //
ओं भूः स्वाहा ओं भूवः स्वाहा ओं स्वः स्वाहा ओं
भूर्भुवः स्वः स्वाहा
ओं देवकृतस्यैनसो ऽवयजनमसि स्वाहा ओं पितृकृतस्यैनसो
ऽवयजनमसि स्वाहा ओं आत्मकृतस्यैनसो ऽवयजनमसि स्वाहा ओं
मनुष्यकृतस्यैनसो ऽवयजनमसि स्वाहा ओं एनस एनसो ऽवयजनमसि
स्वाहा / यच्चाहमेनो विद्वांश् चकार यच्चविद्वांस्तस्य सर्वस्यैनसो
ऽवयजनमसि स्वाहा अग्नये स्विष्टिकृते स्वाहा ओं प्रजापतये स्वाहा
||
263.m:
Having offered the cow's morsel and recited an auspicious blessing, he should bestow alms. / Having honored guests and the afflicted, the householder may eat himself:
'Oṃ bhūḥ svāhā! Oṃ bhuvaḥ svāhā! Oṃ svaḥ svāhā! Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā! / Oṃ, you are the expiation of sin committed against the gods, svāhā! Oṃ, you are the expiation of sin committed against the ancestors, svāhā! Oṃ, you are the expiation of sin committed against oneself, svāhā! Oṃ, you are the expiation of sin committed against humans, svāhā! Oṃ, you are the expiation of sin upon sin, svāhā! And whatever sin I have committed knowingly, and whatever unknowingly, of all that sin you are the expiation, svāhā! To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, svāhā! Oṃ, to Prajāpati, svāhā!'

263.s:
viṣṇupūjāvaiśvadevabaliste kīrtito mayā //29//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe devapūjāvaiśvadevabalirnāma
triṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha catuḥṣaṣṭhyadhiakadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
dikpālādisnānaṃ
263.d:
विष्णुपूजावैश्वदेवबलिस्ते कीर्तितो मया //29//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे देवपूजावैश्वदेवबलिर्नाम
त्रिषष्ट्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ चतुःषष्ठ्यधिअकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
दिक्पालादिस्नानं
263.m:
The worship of Viṣṇu and the Vaiśvadeva food offering have thus been declared to you by me. // 29
Thus ends the two hundred and sixty-third chapter in the great Purāṇa of Agni, entitled 'Worship of Deities and the Vaiśvadeva Offering.'
Now begins the two hundred and sixty-fourth chapter:
Bathing [with mantras] of the guardians of the directions and others.

264.s:
agnir uvāca
sarvārthasādhanaṃ snānaṃ vakṣye śāntikaraṃ śṛṇu /
snāpayecca sarittīre grahān viṣṇuṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ //
:n
1 saurabheyā iti ka.. , gha.. , cha.. , ña.. ca
2 puṣparāśaya iti ja.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 467
264.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
सर्वार्थसाधनं स्नानं वक्ष्ये शान्तिकरं शृणु /
स्नापयेच्च सरित्तीरे ग्रहान् विष्णुं विचक्षणः //
:न्
1 सौरभेया इति क.. , घ.. , छ.. , ञ.. च
2 पुष्पराशय इति ज.. , ट.. च
:प् 467
264.m:
Agni said: / Listen to the pacifying bath that accomplishes all aims, which I shall explain. / A wise person should bathe Viṣṇu and the planets on a riverbank;
[Footnote]
1. "saurabheyāḥ" thus in manuscripts ka, gha, cha, and ña.
2. "puṣparāśayaḥ" thus in manuscripts ja and ṭa. / [Page 467]

264.s:
devālaye jvarārtyādau vināyakagrahārdite /
vidyārthino hrade gehe jayakāmasya tīrthake //
264.d:
देवालये ज्वरार्त्यादौ विनायकग्रहार्दिते /
विद्यार्थिनो ह्रदे गेहे जयकामस्य तीर्थके //
264.m: in a temple when suffering from fever and the like, or afflicted by Vināyaka and seizing spirits; / in a pool for one desiring knowledge; in the home or at a sacred ford for one desiring victory.

264.s:
padminyāṃ snāpayennārīṃ garbho yasyāḥ sravettathā /
aśokasannidhau snāyājjāto yasyā vinaśyati //
264.d:
पद्मिन्यां स्नापयेन्नारीं गर्भो यस्याः स्रवेत्तथा /
अशोकसन्निधौ स्नायाज्जातो यस्या विनश्यति //
264.m: One should bathe a woman whose fetus miscarries in a lotus pond; / she whose child perishes upon birth should bathe in the vicinity of an aśoka tree.

264.s:
puṣpārthināñca puṣpāḍhye putrārthināñca sāgare /
gṛhasaubhāgyakāmānāṃ sarveṣāṃ viṣṇusannidhau //
264.d:
पुष्पार्थिनाञ्च पुष्पाढ्ये पुत्रार्थिनाञ्च सागरे /
गृहसौभाग्यकामानां सर्वेषां विष्णुसन्निधौ //
264.m: For those desiring flowers, [the bath should be] in a place rich in flowers, and in the ocean for those desiring a son; / for all who desire household good fortune, it should be in the presence of Viṣṇu.

264.s:
vaiṣṇave revatīpuṣye sarveṣāṃ snānamuttamaṃ /
snānakāmasya saptāhampūrvamutsādanaṃ smṛtaṃ //
264.d:
वैष्णवे रेवतीपुष्ये सर्वेषां स्नानमुत्तमं /
स्नानकामस्य सप्ताहम्पूर्वमुत्सादनं स्मृतं //
264.m: Under the asterism of Viṣṇu [Śravaṇā], or Revatī and Puṣya, a bath is supreme for all. / For one desiring a bath, anointing [the body] seven days prior is prescribed.

264.s:
punar navāṃ rocanāñca śatāṅgaṃ guruṇī tvacaṃ /
madhūkaṃ rajanī dve ca tagarannāgakeśaram //
264.d:
पुनर् नवां रोचनाञ्च शताङ्गं गुरुणी त्वचं /
मधूकं रजनी द्वे च तगरन्नागकेशरम् //
264.m: Punar-navā, rocanā, śatāṅga, heavy bark, / madhūka, the two kinds of turmeric, tagara, nāgakeśara,

264.s:
ambarīñcaiva mañjiṣṭhāṃ māṃsīyāsakamardanaiḥ /
priyaṅgusarṣapaṃ kuṣṭhambalāmbrāhmīñca kuṅkumaṃ //
264.d:
अम्बरीञ्चैव मञ्जिष्ठां मांसीयासकमर्दनैः /
प्रियङ्गुसर्षपं कुष्ठम्बलाम्ब्राह्मीञ्च कुङ्कुमं //
264.m: ambarī, mañjiṣṭhā, māṃsī, and rubs of yāsaka, / priyaṅgu, mustard, kuṣṭha, balā, brāhmī, saffron,

264.s:
pañcagavyaṃ śaktumiśraṃ udvartya snānamācaret /
maṇḍale karṇikāyāñca viṣṇuṃ brāhmaṇamarcayet //
264.d:
पञ्चगव्यं शक्तुमिश्रं उद्वर्त्य स्नानमाचरेत् /
मण्डले कर्णिकायाञ्च विष्णुं ब्राह्मणमर्चयेत् //
264.m: and the five products of the cow mixed with barley meal: rubbing [with these], one should perform the bath. / In a maṇḍala, in its pericarp, one should worship Viṣṇu and a Brahmin.

264.s:
dakṣe vāme haraṃ pūrvaṃ patre pūrvādike kramāt /
likhedindrādikāndevān sāyudhān sahabāndhavān(1) //
264.d:
दक्षे वामे हरं पूर्वं पत्रे पूर्वादिके क्रमात् /
लिखेदिन्द्रादिकान्देवान् सायुधान् सहबान्धवान्(1) //
264.m: On the right [and] on the left, first Hara, and on the petal, beginning with the east in succession, / one should draw Indra and the other gods, with their weapons and their retinues.

264.s:
snānamaṇḍalakān dikṣu kuryāccaiva vidikṣu ca /
viṣṇubrahmeśaśakrādīṃstadastrāṇyarcya homayet //
264.d:
स्नानमण्डलकान् दिक्षु कुर्याच्चैव विदिक्षु च /
विष्णुब्रह्मेशशक्रादींस्तदस्त्राण्यर्च्य होमयेत् //
264.m: One should make bath-maṇḍalas in the directions and in the intermediate directions. / Having worshipped Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Īśa, Śakra, and the others, and their weapons, one should offer fire oblations.

264.s:
ekaikasya tvaṣṭaśataṃ samidhastu tilān dhṛtaṃ /
bhadraḥ subhadraḥ siddhārthaḥ kalasāḥ puṣṭivardhanāḥ //
264.d:
एकैकस्य त्वष्टशतं समिधस्तु तिलान् धृतं /
भद्रः सुभद्रः सिद्धार्थः कलसाः पुष्टिवर्धनाः //
264.m: One hundred and eight firewood sticks, sesamum, and ghee for each one. / The jars that increase prosperity are Bhadra, Subhadra, Siddhārtha,

264.s:
amoghaścitrabhānuś ca parjanyo 'tha sudarśanaḥ /
sthāpayettu vaṭānenān sāśvirudramarudgaṇān //
:n
1 sahavāhanāniti gha.. , ja.. ca
:p 468
264.d:
अमोघश्चित्रभानुश् च पर्जन्यो ऽथ सुदर्शनः /
स्थापयेत्तु वटानेनान् साश्विरुद्रमरुद्गणान् //
:न्
1 सहवाहनानिति घ.. , ज.. च
:प् 468
264.m:
Amogha, Citrabhānu, Parjanya, and Sudarśana. / One should set up these under a banyan tree, along with the two Aśvins, the Rudras, and the host of the Maruts:
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: "with their vehicles" in manuscripts gha and ja. Page 468]

264.s:
viśve devas tathā daityā vasavo munayas tathā /
āveśayantu suprītās tathānyā api devatāḥ //
264.d:
विश्वे देवस् तथा दैत्या वसवो मुनयस् तथा /
आवेशयन्तु सुप्रीतास् तथान्या अपि देवताः //
264.m: "May the Viśvedevas, likewise the Daityas, the Vasus, and the sages, / and likewise the other deities, enter [here] well pleased."

264.s:
oṣadhīr nikṣipet kumbhe jayantīṃ vijayāṃ jayāṃ /
śatāvarīṃ śatapuṣpāṃ viṣṇukrāntāparājitām //
264.d:
ओषधीर् निक्षिपेत् कुम्भे जयन्तीं विजयां जयां /
शतावरीं शतपुष्पां विष्णुक्रान्तापराजिताम् //
264.m: One should place medicinal herbs into the jar: jayantī, vijayā, jayā, / śatāvarī, śatapuṣpā, viṣṇukrāntā, aparājitā,

264.s:
jyotiṣmatīmatibalāñcandanośīrakeśaraṃ /
kastūrikāñca karpūraṃ bālakaṃ patrakaṃ tvacaṃ //
264.d:
ज्योतिष्मतीमतिबलाञ्चन्दनोशीरकेशरं /
कस्तूरिकाञ्च कर्पूरं बालकं पत्रकं त्वचं //
264.m: jyotiṣmatī, atibalā, sandalwood, uśīra, kesara, / musk, camphor, bālaka, leaf, bark,

264.s:
jātīphalaṃ lavaṅgañca mṛttikāṃ pañcagavyakaṃ /
bhadrapīṭhe sthitaṃ sādhyaṃ snāpayeyurdvijā balāt //
264.d:
जातीफलं लवङ्गञ्च मृत्तिकां पञ्चगव्यकं /
भद्रपीठे स्थितं साध्यं स्नापयेयुर्द्विजा बलात् //
264.m: nutmeg, clove, earth, and the five products of the cow. / Stationed on an auspicious seat, the subject should be forcibly bathed by the twice-born.

264.s:
rājābhiṣekamantroktadevānāṃ homakāḥ pṛthak /
pūrṇāhutintato datvā gurave dakṣiṇāṃ dadet //
264.d:
राजाभिषेकमन्त्रोक्तदेवानां होमकाः पृथक् /
पूर्णाहुतिन्ततो दत्वा गुरवे दक्षिणां ददेत् //
264.m: There are separate homa-offerers for the gods stated in the royal consecration mantra. / Then, having offered the full oblation, he should give a sacrificial fee to the guru.

264.s:
indro 'bhiṣikto guruṇā purā daityān jaghāna ha /
dikpālasnānaṅkathitaṃ saṃgrāmādau jayādikaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe dikpālādisnānaṃ nāma
catuḥṣaṣṭhyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha pañcaṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
vināyakasnānaṃ
264.d:
इन्द्रो ऽभिषिक्तो गुरुणा पुरा दैत्यान् जघान ह /
दिक्पालस्नानङ्कथितं संग्रामादौ जयादिकं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे दिक्पालादिस्नानं नाम
चतुःषष्ठ्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ पञ्चषष्ट्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
विनायकस्नानं
264.m:
Indra, consecrated by his guru in ancient times, indeed slew the Daityas. / The bath of the guardians of the directions has been declared, bringing victory and the like in battle and other [ventures].
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and sixty-fourth chapter, entitled "The Bath of the Guardians of the Directions and Others."
Now, the two hundred and sixty-fifth chapter:
The bath for Vināyaka.
